grammar: Poner uses the irregular future stem pondr- plus -é. Here poner el arroz means contributing the rice to a shared meal, with no physical placement destination.
register: Familiar Mexican coordination for a shared meal.
note: Ofrecer = offer; verduras = vegetables; comida del sábado = Saturday's main meal; pondré el arroz = I will contribute the rice.

sentence: Ana, ahora tú y yo queremos pasear; mañana, después de caminar seis horas, seguramente querremos descansar en casa y no salir otra vez.
part_of_speech: first-person plural irregular simple future indicative verb
grammar: Querer uses the future stem querr-. The anticipated tiredness explains a change from the pair's present preference.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Pasear = go for a stroll; seguramente = probably; después de caminar seis horas = after walking for six hours.

sentence: Luis, mañana tienes una consulta con la médica para hablar del tratamiento; después sabrás la fecha de tu siguiente revisión, que ahora no tienes.
part_of_speech: second-person singular irregular simple future indicative verb
grammar: Sabrás uses the irregular future stem sabr- and addresses Luis as tú. The consultation supplies information currently missing.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Tratamiento = treatment; siguiente revisión = next checkup; después = afterward.

sentence: Mañana vamos a mover el sillón al otro cuarto; con ese espacio libre, este librero cabrá junto a la ventana.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular simple future indicative verb
grammar: Caber uses the irregular future stem cabr-. The planned move creates the space needed for the bookcase.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Sillón = armchair; librero = bookcase; espacio libre = free space; mover = move.

sentence: El lunes abre la nueva biblioteca y habrá tres salas de estudio; hoy solo tenemos una mesa para todos.
part_of_speech: impersonal singular simple future indicative verb
grammar: Existential habrá remains singular before plural tres salas. It introduces future facilities rather than forming a compound tense.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Biblioteca = library; salas de estudio = study rooms; para todos = for everyone.

sentence: Hoy la pintura de la puerta está húmeda; mañana a las ocho estará seca y vamos a colocar el letrero a esa hora.
part_of_speech: feminine singular adjective
grammar: Seca agrees with pintura and describes its expected condition after drying. Tomorrow at eight is the reference time for attaching the sign.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Húmeda = wet; seca = dry; colocar el letrero = put up the sign; a esa hora = at that time.

sentence: Todavía tengo dudas sobre la mudanza, pero creo que será una buena decisión: la nueva casa queda junto a la escuela de mis hijos.
part_of_speech: feminine plural noun
grammar: Tener dudas sobre introduces reservations about a choice. Those reservations coexist with the favorable prediction introduced by creo que.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Tener dudas sobre = have doubts about; mudanza = move; una buena decisión = a good decision.

sentence: Pagué quinientos pesos por esta bicicleta; mañana voy a reparar los frenos y creo que después valdrá mil.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular simple future indicative verb
grammar: Valer uses the future stem valdr-. Valdrá estimates the bicycle's value after repair; pagué states the different amount already paid.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Bicicleta = bicycle; frenos = brakes; quinientos = five hundred; valer = be worth.

sentence: Luis, te debo doscientos pesos del boleto; tienes razón. Mañana te pagaré la deuda en efectivo, te lo prometo.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative verb
grammar: Deber followed by a money amount expresses a financial debt. Te identifies Luis as the person owed money; pagaré states the repayment commitment.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Te debo doscientos pesos = I owe you two hundred pesos; del boleto = for the ticket here; deuda = debt; en efectivo = in cash.

sentence: Mamá, Ana y yo nos vamos ahora a comprar el pan; volveremos a casa antes de las dos para comer contigo. Te damos nuestra palabra.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun in a fixed commitment expression
grammar: Dar su palabra means to pledge or promise. Nuestra identifies the pledge as shared by Ana and the speaker; te identifies the mother receiving it.
register: Familiar Mexican family conversation; emphatic reassurance.
note: Te damos nuestra palabra = we give you our word; contigo = with you; volveremos = we will return.

sentence: Mi hermana necesita su uniforme para trabajar el lunes; la tienda ya confirmó la entrega del uniforme para el sábado y ella recibirá el paquete en casa ese día.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Entrega names the delivery event confirmed by the store. Ese día refers to Saturday, when the sister is expected to receive the uniform.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Uniforme = uniform; entrega = delivery; confirmó = confirmed; ese día = that day.

sentence: Ahora no encuentro a Luis; su bicicleta está en la entrada de la biblioteca y supongo que estará adentro, pero no tengo confirmación.
part_of_speech: third-person singular simple future indicative verb expressing present conjecture
grammar: Estará conjectures about Luis's location now. The bicycle is indirect evidence; supongo and the lack of confirmation preserve uncertainty.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Supongo que = I suppose that; adentro = inside; confirmación = confirmation.

sentence: No tengo reloj ni teléfono; por la luz de la tarde, serán como las seis ahora, pero solo es un cálculo.
part_of_speech: third-person plural simple future indicative clock-time verb expressing present conjecture
grammar: Serán estimates the current time without a clock. Its plural form follows the plural hour expression las seis.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Reloj = clock or watch; como las seis = around six; un cálculo = an estimate.

sentence: Mi nueva vecina parece de mi edad; tendrá unos treinta años ahora, como yo, pero no conozco su fecha de nacimiento.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular simple future indicative age verb expressing present conjecture
grammar: Tendrá with años conjectures about the neighbor's present age. Appearance supplies uncertain evidence; the speaker does not know her birth date.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Vecina = female neighbor; de mi edad = my age; unos treinta = about thirty; fecha de nacimiento = birth date.

sentence: Ahora salen clientes de la panadería con bolsas de pan; todavía habrá bolillos, supongo, pero no he entrado a preguntar.
part_of_speech: impersonal singular simple future indicative verb expressing present conjecture
grammar: Habrá conjectures about bread available now and remains singular before plural bolillos. Customers carrying bread provide indirect evidence.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Panadería = bakery; bolillos = crusty bread rolls; supongo = I suppose; no he entrado = I have not gone in.

sentence: Esta mochila no tiene etiqueta de precio; costará unos cuatrocientos pesos, por el material y el tamaño, pero voy a preguntar antes de comprar.
part_of_speech: third-person singular simple future indicative verb expressing present conjecture
grammar: Costará estimates the backpack's current price. The missing price tag and planned inquiry distinguish this estimate from an agreed payment.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Mochila = backpack; etiqueta de precio = price tag; cuatrocientos = four hundred; tamaño = size.

sentence: La reunión de esta tarde durará unas dos horas, calculo; por eso prefiero comer antes de entrar, porque todavía no sé la hora de salida.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative verb
grammar: Calculo qualifies the predicted duration as the speaker's estimate. Unas dos horas is approximate, and the ending time remains unknown.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Calculo = I estimate; durará = will last; unas dos horas = about two hours; hora de salida = finishing time here.

sentence: Veo nubes oscuras que vienen hacia nuestra casa; creo que lloverá pronto y voy a meter las sillas del patio a la casa.
part_of_speech: feminine plural noun
grammar: Oscuras agrees with feminine plural nubes. The approaching clouds are the visible basis for the speaker's rain prediction.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Nube = cloud; oscuras = dark; hacia = toward; pronto = soon; meter = bring inside here.

sentence: El ruido de la calle no me deja estudiar; quizá cerrar la ventana funcionará, por eso prefiero probar esa solución antes de cambiar de cuarto.
part_of_speech: third-person singular simple future indicative verb
grammar: Funcionar applies to a solution's effectiveness here. Quizá leaves its future success uncertain, so the speaker chooses a test before moving rooms.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Quizá = perhaps; solución = solution; cambiar de cuarto = move to a different room.

sentence: Mañana vamos a plantar flores en el patio; esta cubeta servirá para llevar el agua desde la llave, por eso la voy a guardar.
part_of_speech: third-person singular simple future indicative verb
grammar: Servir means to be useful for a purpose here. Para llevar specifies the bucket's anticipated use; no food is being served.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Plantar flores = plant flowers; cubeta = bucket; llave = water tap here; guardar = keep.

sentence: Luis, la reparación cuesta mil pesos y tú y yo tenemos seiscientos; Ana va a aportar trescientos mañana y todavía nos faltará dinero: cien pesos.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb
grammar: Aportar introduces Ana's contribution toward the shared expense. After that contribution, Luis and the speaker will still be one hundred pesos short.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish with familiar singular address.
note: Reparación = repair; seiscientos = six hundred; aportar = contribute; trescientos = three hundred; cien = one hundred.

sentence: Mañana vamos a subir la mesa al segundo piso; hará falta otra persona para cargarla, porque Ana y yo no podemos con todo el peso.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached feminine singular direct-object clitic
grammar: Cargarla combines cargar with attached direct-object la, referring to la mesa. The weight explains why Ana and the speaker will need another helper.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Cargar = carry a load; segundo piso = second floor; hará falta otra persona = another person will be needed; peso = weight.

sentence: Esta falda llega hasta el piso; después de cortar cinco centímetros de tela quedará más corta y ya no voy a pisarla al caminar.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached feminine singular direct-object clitic
grammar: Pisar takes the thing stepped on as its direct object. In pisarla, attached la refers to the skirt whose length will be reduced.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Pisar = step on; tela = fabric; centímetros = centimeters; quedará más corta = will end up shorter; al caminar = while walking.

sentence: Luis, te parecerá raro, pero prefiero caminar una hora hasta casa: necesito ahorrar el dinero del camión para la comida.
part_of_speech: third-person singular simple future indicative verb anticipating an addressee's reaction
grammar: Te parecerá raro anticipates Luis's possible judgment before explaining the choice. Te identifies Luis as the evaluator.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Raro = odd; ahorrar = save money; dinero del camión = money for the bus fare.

sentence: —Ana, ¿compramos los boletos hoy? —Ya veremos; todavía no tengo el horario de mi trabajo y no quiero decidir ahora.
part_of_speech: first-person plural simple future indicative verb in a deferred-decision expression
grammar: In ya veremos, ver postpones a decision. Ana explicitly declines to decide before receiving her work schedule.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Ya veremos = we'll see; horario de mi trabajo = my work schedule; decidir = decide.

sentence: Luis, dirás que el taxi es muy caro, pero hoy mi mamá no puede caminar hasta la parada y tengo que llevarla a la clínica.
part_of_speech: second-person singular irregular simple future indicative verb anticipating an objection
grammar: Dirás que anticipates an objection attributed to Luis. The speaker answers it with the mother's present transport need.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Parada = bus stop here; llevarla = take her, referring to the speaker's mother; clínica = clinic.

sentence: Luis, este sillón será muy bonito, como dices, pero ocupa toda la sala y no deja espacio para caminar.
part_of_speech: third-person singular simple future indicative copular verb expressing concession
grammar: Será provisionally concedes Luis's praise while pero introduces the speaker's practical objection. The chair and space problem are current.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Como dices = as you say; ocupa toda la sala = takes up the whole living room.

sentence: El sábado vamos a poner música durante la tarde; a Luis le importará el ruido, porque trabaja de noche y necesita dormir antes de su turno.
part_of_speech: masculine singular mass noun
grammar: El ruido names the anticipated sound disturbance. A Luis and le identify the person to whom it will matter because he needs to sleep.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Poner música = play music; ruido = noise; turno = work shift here; antes de su turno = before his shift.

sentence: Hoy tapamos la gotera con plástico, pero el techo sigue dañado; el problema volverá con la próxima lluvia y necesitamos una reparación completa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular simple future indicative verb
grammar: Volverá has el problema as its subject and predicts recurrence. It does not describe a person's return to a place or govern another infinitive.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Tapamos = we covered or blocked; plástico = plastic; techo = roof here; dañado = damaged; lluvia = rain.

sentence: El pasillo está oscuro porque el mueble tapa la lámpara; mañana vamos a cambiar el foco, pero seguirá oscuro sin mover ese mueble.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb
grammar: Tapa describes the furniture obstructing the lamp. El mueble is the subject and la lámpara the direct object; that obstruction explains the predicted continuing darkness.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Mueble = piece of furniture; tapar = block or obstruct here; lámpara = lamp; sin mover = without moving.

sentence: Ana, todavía no tenemos una solución para el cobro doble; tú y yo resolveremos ese problema mañana con la encargada, te lo prometo.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun phrase
grammar: Cobro names a charge, and doble identifies the duplication being disputed. Tú y yo identifies the speaker and Ana as the people committed to resolving it.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Cobro doble = duplicate charge; encargada = woman in charge; solución = solution; te lo prometo = I promise you that.

sentence: Con mi presupuesto de doscientos pesos, podría comprar una mesa de segunda mano; es una opción y todavía no decido.
part_of_speech: first-person singular irregular conditional indicative modal verb
grammar: Podría introduces a tentative option under the stated budget. It uses podr- plus conditional -ía and does not assert a completed purchase or present ability.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Presupuesto = budget; de segunda mano = secondhand; una opción = an option; todavía no decido = I have not decided yet here.

sentence: Comprar un carro solo para ir a esa tienda sería un gasto innecesario: está a diez minutos a pie y prefiero caminar.
part_of_speech: third-person singular conditional indicative copular verb
grammar: Sería evaluates the hypothetical purchase named by comprar un carro. The infinitive supplies the contemplated choice without a past-subjunctive condition.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Gasto innecesario = unnecessary expense; a diez minutos a pie = a ten-minute walk away.

sentence: Con un cambio al turno de la mañana, tendría las tardes libres para estudiar; todavía no he aceptado ese horario.
part_of_speech: first-person singular irregular conditional indicative verb
grammar: Tendría presents a consequence of the contemplated shift change. The speaker has not accepted the schedule, so the free afternoons are hypothetical.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Turno de la mañana = morning shift; tardes libres = free afternoons; no he aceptado = I have not accepted.

sentence: Luis, me pides consejo para reparar tu computadora; yo haría primero una copia de los archivos, antes de probar otro arreglo.
part_of_speech: first-person singular irregular conditional indicative verb expressing advice
grammar: Yo haría presents the speaker's recommended action for Luis's situation. It offers advice rather than promising that the speaker will perform the repair.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Consejo = advice; computadora = computer; copia de los archivos = copy of the files; arreglo = repair here.

sentence: Por las huellas junto a la ventana, yo diría que alguien entró por ahí, pero no vi a la persona.
part_of_speech: first-person singular irregular conditional indicative verb qualifying an opinion
grammar: Diría qualifies an inference rather than claiming direct knowledge. The footprints are evidence, and no vi states the speaker's limitation.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Huellas = footprints here; alguien = someone; entró por ahí = came in through there.

sentence: Ana y yo estamos eligiendo un destino para las vacaciones; yo querría ir a un pueblo tranquilo, pero primero quiero escuchar las ideas de Ana.
part_of_speech: first-person singular irregular conditional indicative verb expressing a tentative wish
grammar: Querría presents a tentative preference in an ongoing shared choice. The speaker leaves room for Ana's ideas rather than making an immediate demand.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Eligiendo = choosing; destino = destination; pueblo tranquilo = quiet small town.

sentence: Ayer mi hermana anunció que vendría hoy a mi casa a las seis; ahora son las cinco y todavía no tengo confirmación de su salida.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular conditional indicative verb expressing future relative to a past report
grammar: Vendría locates the expected visit after yesterday's announcement. It reports the sister's earlier announcement without guaranteeing her actual arrival.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Anunció = announced; confirmación de su salida = confirmation of her departure.

sentence: Ayer el chofer calculó que el camión saldría hoy a las ocho; ahora son las siete y la hora todavía no está confirmada.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular conditional indicative verb expressing future relative to a past estimate
grammar: Saldría reports a departure later than the driver's estimate yesterday. Calculó and the continuing lack of confirmation preserve the estimate's uncertainty.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Chofer = driver; calculó = estimated; todavía no está confirmada = is still unconfirmed.

sentence: Ana propone una cena en mi casa y ofrece traer las verduras; con ese reparto, yo pondría el arroz, pero todavía no acordamos nada.
part_of_speech: first-person singular irregular conditional indicative verb
grammar: Pondría proposes a contribution under the division introduced by con ese reparto. The absence of agreement distinguishes it from a firm pledge.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Propone = proposes; ofrece = offers; reparto = division of contributions here; todavía no acordamos nada = we have not agreed on anything yet here.

sentence: Con una llamada a la clínica, yo sabría la fecha de mi cita; ahora no la sé y todavía no he llamado.
part_of_speech: first-person singular irregular conditional indicative verb
grammar: Sabría presents knowledge expected under a hypothetical action. The speaker explicitly lacks the date now and has not made the call.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Con una llamada = with one phone call; no la sé = I do not know it, referring to the date; no he llamado = I have not called.

sentence: Con una reparación de los frenos, esta bicicleta valdría mil pesos en la reventa; todavía no decido gastar en el arreglo.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Reventa names selling an item again after its acquisition. Visible valdría estimates its value under a repair still being considered.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: En la reventa = on resale; reparación de los frenos = brake repair; gastar en el arreglo = spend money on the repair.

sentence: Mover el sillón es solo una propuesta; con ese espacio libre, el librero cabría junto a la ventana con dos centímetros de margen, según mis medidas.
part_of_speech: singular noun in a spatial measurement expression
grammar: Margen names the extra space remaining beyond the bookcase's required dimensions. Visible cabría assesses fit under a proposed rearrangement.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Dos centímetros de margen = two centimeters of clearance; propuesta = proposal; según mis medidas = according to my measurements.

sentence: Con dos mesas más en el patio, habría asientos para todos los invitados; todavía estamos comparando esa opción con comer adentro.
part_of_speech: masculine plural noun
grammar: Asientos names places intended for sitting. Visible existential habría remains singular before this plural noun and describes an arrangement still being considered.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Asientos = seats; invitados = guests; estamos comparando = we are comparing; adentro = inside.

sentence: Ahora estoy cansado y me cuesta pensar con claridad; con un descanso antes de la cena, estaría más despejado para conversar, pero todavía tengo trabajo pendiente.
part_of_speech: masculine singular predicative adjective
grammar: Despejado describes mental clarity here. The current difficulty thinking clearly establishes the contrast with the state projected by visible estaría.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Pensar con claridad = think clearly; despejado = clearheaded here; conversar = chat; trabajo pendiente = unfinished work.

sentence: A mi hermana y a mí nos gustaría vivir cerca de nuestros padres, pero las rentas de ese barrio superan nuestro presupuesto.
part_of_speech: third-person singular conditional indicative experiencer verb
grammar: Gustaría agrees with the infinitive activity vivir. Nos identifies the two named experiencers, the speaker and the speaker's sister.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Nos gustaría vivir = we would like to live; rentas = rental costs; superan nuestro presupuesto = exceed our budget.

sentence: Podemos ir al concierto o cenar juntos; yo preferiría la cena para conversar contigo durante la sobremesa, después de comer, porque en el concierto hay mucho ruido.
meaning: time spent at the table after a meal
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Sobremesa names the period of remaining at the table after eating. Visible preferiría presents dinner as a tentative choice between two outings.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Sobremesa = time spent at the table after a meal, often talking; concierto = concert; conversar contigo = talk with you.

sentence: Solo tenemos media hora para cocinar y la sopa tarda más; convendría preparar algo frío antes de salir.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular conditional indicative verb with an infinitival subject
grammar: Preparar algo frío is the infinitival subject evaluated as advisable by convendría. The action takes singular agreement; this is not a grammatically subjectless construction.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Convendría preparar algo frío = preparing something cold would be advisable; antes de salir = before leaving.

sentence: Como tu compañero de clase, creo que deberías revisar la dirección antes de enviar la invitación; hay una errata en el número, pero tú decides.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Errata identifies an error in written text. Visible deberías frames the suggested check as peer advice, with tú decides leaving the decision to the addressee.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Errata = typographical error; revisar la dirección = check the address; como tu compañero de clase = as your male classmate.

sentence: Ana, puedes estudiar en casa o en la biblioteca; podrías probar la biblioteca para concentrarte mejor y evitar el ruido de tu edificio, pero tú eliges.
part_of_speech: pronominal infinitive verb with attached second-person singular familiar te
grammar: Concentrarte expresses focusing your attention, with attached te referring to Ana. The purpose infinitive retains its clitic; visible podrías offers an optional suggestion.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Concentrarte mejor = concentrate better; probar la biblioteca = try studying at the library; evitar = avoid; edificio = building; tú eliges = you choose.

sentence: A Luis le importaría el cambio de horario: con la salida a las seis, tendría problemas para conciliar el trabajo con el cuidado de su hija; todavía estamos negociando.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with a direct object and a con complement
grammar: Conciliar el trabajo con el cuidado de su hija means making those responsibilities compatible. Luis is the understood actor of conciliar and the experiencer identified by a Luis le importaría.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Conciliar el trabajo con el cuidado de su hija = reconcile work with caring for his daughter; salida a las seis = leaving work at six here; negociando = negotiating.

sentence: Podemos reunirnos en mi casa o en el patio común; hablar ahí de noche le molestaría a mi vecina porque ella duerme temprano.
part_of_speech: third-person singular conditional indicative psychological verb with an indirect-object experiencer
grammar: Hablar ahí de noche is the infinitival stimulus subject. Le and a mi vecina identify the neighbor as an indirect-object experiencer in the selected construction.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Le molestaría a mi vecina = it would bother my neighbor; reunirnos = meet together; patio común = shared patio; ahí refers to that patio; duerme temprano = sleeps early.

sentence: Estamos considerando pedir prestada una mesa plegable; nos serviría para improvisar un comedor en el patio, pero todavía no tenemos ninguna.
part_of_speech: transitive infinitive verb
grammar: Improvisar un comedor describes putting together a dining area using the contemplated borrowed table. Visible nos serviría para evaluates the table's usefulness for that purpose.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Improvisar un comedor = put together a dining area using available resources; pedir prestada una mesa = ask to borrow a table; ninguna refers to a table.

sentence: Ya es de noche; viajar en taxi costaría unos trescientos pesos con la tarifa nocturna; solo tengo doscientos y todavía no elijo entre el taxi y el camión.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun phrase
grammar: Tarifa nocturna names the fare applicable at night. Visible costaría estimates an unchosen trip's expense, while tengo states the actual available budget.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Tarifa nocturna = nighttime fare; unos trescientos = about three hundred; elijo entre = I choose between.

sentence: La pintura del cuarto tiene pequeñas fallas; Ana y yo proponemos hacer unos retoques y tardaríamos unas dos horas en terminar, pero aún no fijamos el día.
part_of_speech: masculine plural noun
grammar: Retoques names small corrective finishing changes rather than painting the entire room again. Visible tardaríamos estimates completion time for Ana and the speaker's proposed work.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Hacer unos retoques = do some touch-ups; pequeñas fallas = small imperfections here; aún no fijamos el día = we have not set the day yet.

sentence: Con la ruta directa, ahorraría veinte minutos al día, pero caminaría más hasta la parada; todavía comparo las dos opciones.
part_of_speech: first-person singular conditional indicative transitive verb
grammar: Ahorrar takes a time quantity here and means reducing the time required. The visible longer walk is the tradeoff in this contemplated route choice.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Ahorrar tiempo = save time; ruta directa = direct route; al día = per day; caminaría más = I would walk farther here; comparo = I am comparing.

sentence: Con el turno del sábado, perdería la oportunidad de participar en el taller de teatro de mi barrio; todavía no acepto ese horario porque no quiero renunciar a esa actividad.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb taking an a complement
grammar: Renunciar a una actividad expresses giving up participation in it. The speaker has not accepted the shift and does not want that sacrifice.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Renunciar a esa actividad = give up that activity; participar en = participate in; taller de teatro = theater workshop; barrio = neighborhood.

sentence: Trabajar cerca de casa cuesta menos en transporte; con ese empleo, ganaría tiempo para estar con mi hijo, pero el sueldo sería menor.
part_of_speech: first-person singular conditional indicative verb
grammar: Ganaría with tiempo expresses a prospective practical advantage. It does not mean winning a competition or earning the salary mentioned separately.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Empleo = job; transporte = transportation; sueldo = salary; menor = lower here.

sentence: Con un horario de salida a las cuatro, aceptaría el empleo; ahora la oferta indica las seis y a las cinco recojo a mi hija.
part_of_speech: first-person singular conditional indicative transitive verb
grammar: Aceptar el empleo means agreeing to take the offered job. The conditional makes that acceptance dependent on the proposed departure time rather than reporting an agreement already made.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Aceptar el empleo = accept the job; oferta = offer; indica = specifies; recojo a mi hija = I pick up my daughter.

sentence: Me ofrecen dinero por contar un secreto de mi amiga; rechazaría ese trato por respeto a ella, pero aún no he respondido.
part_of_speech: first-person singular conditional indicative verb
grammar: Rechazaría states a hypothetical principled refusal. Aún no he respondido separates that stance from a completed rejection.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Secreto = secret; trato = deal; por respeto a ella = out of respect for her; respondido = replied.

sentence: El cartel del taller tiene una dirección incorrecta; yo cambiaría ese dato antes de imprimir más copias, pero todavía estamos revisando el texto.
part_of_speech: first-person singular conditional indicative transitive verb
grammar: Cambiar ese dato means altering an item of information in the existing text. This transitive use differs from a neighborhood changing over time and from exchanging a purchased item.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Cambiar ese dato = alter that item of information; cartel = poster; taller = workshop; imprimir = print; revisando = reviewing.

sentence: Era de noche cuando llegamos al pueblo; sería la una, pero no recuerdo la hora exacta.
part_of_speech: third-person singular conditional indicative clock-time verb expressing past conjecture
grammar: Sería estimates a past clock time. Era and llegamos anchor the estimate in a past arrival; singular la una takes singular sería.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Era de noche = it was nighttime; llegamos al pueblo = we arrived in the town; hora exacta = exact time.

sentence: Ayer a las cuatro busqué a Luis; su bicicleta estaba frente a la biblioteca y supongo que estaría adentro, pero no lo vi.
part_of_speech: third-person singular conditional indicative locative verb expressing past conjecture
grammar: Estaría conjectures about Luis's location at yesterday's search. His bicycle supplies indirect evidence, while no lo vi leaves the location unconfirmed.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Frente a = in front of; supongo que = I suppose that; adentro = inside; lo refers to Luis.

sentence: En ese recuerdo yo iba a la primaria; tendría unos ocho años, pero no sé mi edad exacta durante aquella visita a mi abuela.
part_of_speech: first-person singular irregular conditional indicative age verb expressing past conjecture
grammar: Tendría estimates the speaker's age in a childhood memory. It does not predict future possession or state an exact age.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Primaria = elementary school; edad exacta = exact age; tendría unos ocho años = I was probably about eight.

sentence: El lunes mi hermano prometió que volvería a casa el martes; hoy es miércoles y todavía sigue fuera por un retraso del viaje.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative reporting verb
grammar: Prometió reports a commitment rather than merely an announcement or estimate. Visible volvería places the promised return after Monday; the Wednesday update shows that its promised timing was not fulfilled.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Prometer que = promise that; prometió = promised; sigue fuera = is still away; retraso del viaje = travel delay.

sentence: Ayer por la mañana Ana dijo que llamaría a su mamá al anochecer; yo no estaba con Ana y no sé si hizo la llamada.
part_of_speech: temporal prepositional phrase
grammar: Al anochecer identifies nightfall as the time of the intended call. Yesterday morning anchors the report, and visible llamaría places the call later that day without asserting that it occurred.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Al anochecer = at nightfall, when daylight ends; no sé si hizo la llamada = I do not know whether she made the call.

sentence: Mi hermana vive cerca; quiero que venga a cenar conmigo esta noche, pero todavía no la he invitado.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular present subjunctive verb in a wish clause
grammar: Quiero que introduces the speaker's current wish about another person's action. Venga has mi hermana as its understood subject; vive separately asserts where she lives.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Conmigo = with me; no la he invitado = I have not invited her; venga a cenar = she come for dinner in the wish.

sentence: Son las siete y media y sigo en la parada; espero que el camión llegue antes de las ocho para entrar al trabajo a tiempo.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present subjunctive verb in a hope clause
grammar: Espero que presents the bus's arrival as hoped for and still pending. Llegar uses gu before subjunctive -e to preserve its consonant.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Sigo en la parada = I am still at the bus stop; espero que llegue = I hope it arrives.

sentence: Ahora le pido a mi hermano que me ayude a mover la mesa; yo no puedo cargarla solo y él está libre.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present subjunctive verb in a request clause
grammar: The current pido que selects ayude for the requested action. Mi hermano is its subject; me is the speaker as direct object of ayudar.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Mover la mesa = move the table; solo = alone, describing the male speaker; está libre = he is available.

sentence: Señora López, usted está cansada después del viaje; le recomiendo que descanse un rato antes de preparar la cena.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present subjunctive verb referring to usted in a recommendation clause
grammar: Descanse belongs to the subordinate recommendation after le recomiendo que. Usted identifies the respectfully addressed woman as its subject; this is not a direct command.
register: Respectful Mexican Spanish.
note: Le recomiendo que = I recommend that you; cansada = tired, feminine; un rato = a while.

sentence: Luis, tú y yo podemos salir a las seis o a las siete; prefiero que salgamos a las seis para caminar con luz.
part_of_speech: first-person plural irregular present subjunctive verb in a preference clause
grammar: Prefiero que selects salgamos for the desired shared departure. Tú y yo makes the first-person plural subject explicit.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Caminar con luz = walk while there is daylight; salgamos = we leave in the desired choice.

sentence: Ana, mañana vamos a dibujar en mi casa; necesito que traigas tus lápices porque yo solo tengo uno.
part_of_speech: second-person singular irregular present subjunctive verb in a need clause
grammar: Necesito que introduces the speaker's current need for Ana's future action. Traigas refers to familiar tú and uses traig-.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Dibujar = draw; necesito que traigas = I need you to bring; uno refers to one pencil.

sentence: Mis hijos creen que solo importan las calificaciones; quiero que sepan que también valoro su esfuerzo, y todavía no he hablado con ellos.
part_of_speech: third-person plural irregular present subjunctive verb in a wish clause
grammar: Sepan has the speaker's children as its subject and follows quiero que. The following que clause states the fact the speaker wants them to know.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Calificaciones = grades; valoro su esfuerzo = I value their effort; todavía no he hablado con ellos = I have not spoken with them yet.

sentence: Ana y yo todavía no acordamos el reparto de gastos del viaje; es necesario que hagamos una lista antes de comprar los boletos.
part_of_speech: first-person plural irregular present subjunctive verb in a necessity clause
grammar: Es necesario que evaluates the joint action as necessary. Hagamos uses hag- and refers to Ana and the speaker; it does not assert that the list exists.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Reparto de gastos = division of expenses; hagamos una lista = we make a list in the proposed necessary action.

sentence: Todavía no elegimos el salón para la comida; es importante que tenga una entrada sin escalones porque mi abuela usa silla de ruedas.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular present subjunctive verb in an evaluation clause
grammar: Es importante que selects tenga for the required feature of the room still to be chosen. The understood singular subject is el salón.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Salón = event room here; escalones = steps; silla de ruedas = wheelchair.

sentence: Ana, todavía no salimos a comprar; es mejor que vayamos al mercado y no a la tienda porque allá hay más fruta.
part_of_speech: first-person plural irregular present subjunctive verb in an evaluation clause
grammar: Es mejor que evaluates a pending joint destination choice. Vayamos refers to Ana and the speaker and uses the irregular subjunctive stem vay-.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Mercado = market; allá refers to the market; todavía no salimos = we have not left yet here.

sentence: Hay nubes sobre el patio y todavía no cae agua; es posible que llueva esta tarde, pero no tengo un pronóstico.
part_of_speech: impersonal third-person singular stem-changing present subjunctive verb
grammar: Es posible que presents a pending weather event as possible. Llover has the subjunctive form llueva, with o changing to ue.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Sobre el patio = above the patio; todavía no cae agua = no rain is falling yet; pronóstico = forecast.

sentence: Ana propone compartir una sola computadora entre diez alumnos; dudo que ese plan funcione, pero todavía no lo probamos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present subjunctive verb in a doubt clause
grammar: Dudo que withholds endorsement of the plan's effectiveness and selects funcione. The plan has not been tested, so the sentence does not report failure.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Una sola computadora = just one computer; alumnos = students; dudo que = I doubt that; lo refers to the plan.

sentence: No creo que ese cobro sea justo; falta revisar cuánto usa cada grupo la sala y todavía no doy una opinión definitiva.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular present subjunctive copular verb under negated belief
grammar: No creo que presents fairness as an evaluation the speaker does not endorse. The pending review and lack of a final opinion avoid asserting that the charge is unfair.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Cobro = charge; justo = fair; falta revisar = reviewing remains necessary; opinión definitiva = final opinion.

sentence: Ana propone que el pago sea igual; yo creo que cobrar lo mismo a cada alumno es justo: todos usan igual la sala.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative copular verb in an affirmative belief clause
grammar: Creo que presents es justo as the speaker's endorsed evaluation. Ana's visible propone que introduces a proposed arrangement with sea; indicative does not guarantee that the speaker's judgment is objectively correct.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Pago = payment; cobrar lo mismo a cada alumno = charge every student the same amount; justo = fair; usan igual la sala = use the room equally.

sentence: Sé que Ana viene mañana a mi casa: ella confirmó la visita por teléfono; yo quiero que llegue temprano, pero eso todavía no está acordado.
part_of_speech: third-person singular stem-changing present indicative verb with future reference in a knowledge clause
grammar: Sé que presents the visit as a known arrangement supported by Ana's confirmation. Viene has future reference from mañana; quiero que llegue separately expresses the speaker's wish about arrival time.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Confirmó = confirmed; temprano = early; eso refers to arriving early; no está acordado = is not agreed.

sentence: Ana no ha confirmado la cena de hoy; no sé si viene a mi casa o si prefiere comer con su hermana.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb in an indirect yes/no question
grammar: No sé si introduces an unresolved yes/no question with indicative viene. Lack of knowledge alone does not require subjunctive.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: No ha confirmado = has not confirmed; no sé si = I do not know whether; prefiere = prefers.

sentence: Ana, ya te veo aquí en casa; me alegro de que estés con nosotros otra vez porque te extrañamos.
part_of_speech: second-person singular present subjunctive copular verb in an emotional reaction clause
grammar: Me alegro de que selects subjunctive estés for an emotional reaction. Ana's presence is explicitly accepted through ya te veo aquí.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Me alegro de que = I am glad that; te extrañamos = we miss you; nosotros includes the speaker.

sentence: La escuela cierra en diez minutos y mi hijo todavía está en el camión; me preocupa que llegue tarde.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present subjunctive verb in a concern clause
grammar: Me preocupa que introduces the parent's concern about a pending arrival. Me identifies the concerned experiencer; mi hijo is the understood subject of llegue.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Me preocupa que = I am worried that; llegue tarde = he arrives late in this concern.

sentence: Ana, me dijiste que hoy tienes turno de noche; lamento que tengas que trabajar durante la fiesta de tu hija.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative verb expressing regret
grammar: Lamento que expresses regret about Ana's accepted work obligation. The following tengas is present subjunctive; its second que belongs to tener que trabajar.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Lamento que = I am sorry that; turno de noche = night shift; tengas que trabajar = you have to work within the regret clause.

sentence: Mi vecino Diego reparó mi radio sin ayuda; me sorprende que sepa arreglar aparatos con solo quince años.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular present subjunctive verb governing an infinitive
grammar: Me sorprende que selects sepa for surprise about an accepted skill. Diego's successful repair supplies visible evidence; saber plus infinitive expresses learned ability.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Vecino = neighbor; me sorprende que = it surprises me that; aparatos = devices; con solo quince años = at only fifteen.

sentence: Ana, ya comprobamos que puedes caminar sin dolor; es bueno que puedas hacerlo otra vez después del accidente.
part_of_speech: second-person singular stem-changing present subjunctive modal verb in an evaluation clause
grammar: Es bueno que evaluates Ana's established ability positively and selects puedas. The preceding comprobamos que puedes explicitly accepts the ability as real.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Comprobamos = we checked and established here; sin dolor = without pain; hacerlo refers to walking without pain.

sentence: Mi hermano acaba de cargar todas las cajas de la mudanza; es normal que esté cansado después de tanto esfuerzo.
part_of_speech: singular evaluative adjective
grammar: Normal evaluates the brother's tiredness as an expected response to the stated effort. Es normal que takes present subjunctive esté in this evaluation.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Es normal que = it is to be expected that; cajas = boxes; tanto esfuerzo = so much effort.

sentence: Mis hermanas querían venir a cenar con Ana y conmigo, pero hoy trabajan hasta medianoche; es una lástima que no puedan acompañarnos.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun in an expression of regret
grammar: Lástima in es una lástima que presents the situation as regrettable. No puedan describes the sisters' inability to join Ana and the speaker; puedan is plural present subjunctive.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Es una lástima que = it is a pity that; no puedan acompañarnos = they cannot join us within this regret; nos refers to Ana and the speaker.

sentence: El anuncio dice que todo el curso es gratis, pero cada clase cuesta cien pesos; no es verdad que sea gratis.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular present subjunctive copular verb in a rejected claim
grammar: No es verdad que rejects the advertisement's claim and selects sea. The speaker does not assert that the course is free; the stated class price contradicts that claim.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Anuncio = advertisement; gratis = free of charge; no es verdad que = it is not true that.

sentence: Es cierto que los boletos son para mañana; ya comprobé la fecha impresa en ambos.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective expressing factual truth
grammar: Cierto in es cierto que explicitly confirms the truth of the following information. Indicative son presents the ticket date as factual and agrees with los boletos.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Es cierto que = it is true that; fecha impresa = printed date; ambos refers to the two tickets.

sentence: Ana, te mando la dirección y un mapa para que llegues a mi casa; mi calle no tiene letrero.
part_of_speech: second-person singular present subjunctive verb in a purpose clause
grammar: Para que introduces the intended result of sending the address and map and selects llegues. The speaker sends the information; Ana is the intended arriving person.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Te mando = I am sending you; para que llegues = so that you can arrive; letrero = sign.

sentence: Ana y yo tenemos una mesa muy pequeña; nuestra vecina nos presta la suya para que podamos cenar juntos con mis padres.
part_of_speech: purpose subordinating conjunctive locution
grammar: Para que introduces a finite purpose clause with present subjunctive podamos. The neighbor lends the table; Ana and the speaker are the group intended to gain the opportunity to dine with the speaker's parents.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Para que podamos = so that we can; la suya = hers, referring to the neighbor's table; nos presta = lends us.

sentence: Mi hermana Ana sale de viaje en una hora; necesito darle su paquete antes de que salga de casa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular present subjunctive verb in a temporal clause
grammar: Antes de que selects subjunctive salga. The departure is still pending and supplies the deadline for the speaker's intended handover.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Sale de viaje = is leaving on a trip; darle = give her; antes de que salga = before she leaves.

sentence: Ana y yo vamos a preparar la fiesta de cumpleaños de mi hermano Luis sin que se entere de nuestros planes; queremos darle una sorpresa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular pronominal present subjunctive verb phrase
grammar: Sin que selects subjunctive se entere for awareness the planners intend to prevent. Enterarse de means finding out about something; se belongs to the pronominal verb.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Sin que se entere de nuestros planes = without his finding out about our plans; darle refers to Luis.

sentence: Todavía estoy lavando los platos; cuando termine, voy a sentarme contigo a platicar, Ana.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present subjunctive verb in a future temporal clause
grammar: Cuando termine refers to completion still ahead of the current washing and selects present subjunctive. The speaker is the subject of both termine and voy a sentarme.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Sentarme contigo = sit down with you; platicar = chat; termine refers to finishing the dishes.

sentence: Mi papá cocina todos los domingos; cuando termina, todos comemos juntos en su casa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb in a habitual temporal clause
grammar: Cuando termina describes the recurring factual relationship between the father's cooking and the family's meal. Present indicative contrasts with subjunctive for a pending future completion.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Todos los domingos = every Sunday; termina refers to finishing the cooking; su casa is the father's home.

sentence: Todavía estoy atendiendo a un cliente; en cuanto pueda, voy a llamarte para hablar de nuestra salida, Ana.
part_of_speech: first-person singular stem-changing present subjunctive modal verb in a temporal clause
grammar: En cuanto pueda makes a pending opportunity the trigger for the promised call. Pueda refers to the speaker and uses present subjunctive for that future opportunity.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Atendiendo a un cliente = serving a customer; en cuanto pueda = as soon as I can; salida = outing here.

sentence: Mi hermana todavía está en el camión; la estoy esperando aquí en la terminal y voy a quedarme hasta que llegue.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present subjunctive verb in a pending endpoint clause
grammar: Hasta que llegue sets the still-unrealized endpoint of the speaker's wait and selects subjunctive. The sister remains on the bus.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: La refers to the speaker's sister; voy a quedarme = I am going to stay; hasta que llegue = until she arrives.

sentence: La clase de música todavía no empieza; Ana y yo vamos a cenar después de que acabe.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present subjunctive verb in a future temporal clause
grammar: Después de que acabe places dinner after the future end of the class. Present subjunctive marks that pending endpoint, not a completed past event.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Acabar here means end; acabe refers to la clase de música; vamos a cenar = we are going to have dinner.

sentence: Ana, mañana vas a pasar el día aquí conmigo; puedes usar mi computadora mientras estés en casa, porque yo no la necesito.
part_of_speech: second-person singular present subjunctive copular verb in a temporal condition clause
grammar: Mientras estés delimits the offer by Ana's forthcoming presence at the speaker's home. Subjunctive frames that future period as the condition for using the computer.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Pasar el día = spend the day; aquí conmigo = here with me; la refers to the computer.

sentence: Aunque llueva mañana, Ana y yo vamos a comer con mi abuela; todavía no cae agua, pero ya tenemos paraguas para el camino.
part_of_speech: impersonal third-person singular present subjunctive verb in a prospective concessive clause
grammar: Aunque llueva treats tomorrow's rain as a possibility that will not block the meal plan. Aunque does not always require subjunctive.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Aunque llueva = even if it rains here; paraguas = umbrellas; para el camino = for the journey.

sentence: Está cayendo agua sobre el patio; aunque llueve, vamos a comer afuera porque la mesa está bajo techo.
part_of_speech: impersonal third-person singular present indicative verb in a factual concessive clause
grammar: Llueve directly asserts the current rain within the concession. Subjunctive llueva is also possible to background that known rain rather than directly assert it.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Afuera = outside; bajo techo = under cover; the table is protected from the actual rain.

sentence: Busco una mochila que tenga una bolsa interior para las llaves; todavía no he visto ninguna.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular present subjunctive verb in a desired-property relative clause
grammar: Que tenga specifies a required feature of an unidentified backpack being sought. The speaker has not found an actual backpack meeting that description.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Mochila = backpack; bolsa interior = inside pocket; ninguna refers to a backpack.

sentence: Conozco una tienda que tiene mochilas con bolsa interior; ayer vi varias ahí y puedo darte la dirección.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb in an asserted-property relative clause
grammar: Tiene asserts an actual property of a shop the speaker knows. The speaker's visit and observation identify an existing referent rather than a shop only being sought.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Varias = several, referring to backpacks; darte la dirección = give you the address.

sentence: Necesitamos mover esta mesa entre cuatro personas; aquí solo estamos Ana y yo y no hay nadie más que pueda ayudarnos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present subjunctive modal verb in a negated-existence relative clause
grammar: No hay nadie más denies the presence of another available helper; pueda describes the unmet property. Impersonal hay remains singular, and nadie más is the subject represented inside the relative clause.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Mover = move; entre cuatro personas = with four people doing it together; ayudarnos = help us.

sentence: Necesito a alguien que sepa coser; mi falda tiene la costura abierta y todavía no encuentro ayuda.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb expressing a learned skill after saber
grammar: Coser names the skill needed to repair the open seam. Sepa coser describes a required skill in an unidentified helper and uses present subjunctive sepa.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Saber coser = know how to sew; la costura abierta = the open seam; the speaker has not yet found a helper.

sentence: Mi prima todavía no confirma su plan del domingo; quizá venga a comer a mi casa, pero también piensa visitar a una amiga.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular present subjunctive verb after a conjectural adverb
grammar: Quizá venga cautiously entertains an unconfirmed future visit. Quizá can also occur with indicative viene here; the adverb does not mechanically require subjunctive.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Prima = female cousin; quizá = perhaps; piensa visitar = intends to visit.

sentence: El radio no prende; tal vez sea un problema de la pila, pero todavía no he probado una nueva.
part_of_speech: third-person singular irregular present subjunctive copular verb in a tentative explanation
grammar: Tal vez sea offers an unverified present explanation. Tal vez also permits indicative es here; the selected subjunctive does not follow from a universal uncertainty rule.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: No prende = will not turn on; tal vez = maybe; una nueva refers to a new battery.

sentence: No veo a mi hermano en el patio; puede que esté en la cocina, pero todavía no lo he buscado ahí.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present subjunctive locative verb in a possibility construction
grammar: Impersonal puede que introduces a possibility and selects subjunctive esté. Puede does not describe the brother's personal ability; esté locates him tentatively.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Puede que = it may be that; lo refers to the brother; ahí refers to the kitchen.

sentence: Ana no contesta el teléfono; a lo mejor está en el camión, pero solo es una idea mía.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative locative verb after a conjectural locution
grammar: A lo mejor está is an ordinary indicative conjecture about Ana's current location. The speaker explicitly calls it an idea rather than confirmed information.
register: Conversational Mexican Spanish.
note: A lo mejor = maybe; una idea mía = an idea of mine; no contesta = is not answering.

sentence: Ana dice que Luis tiene la culpa del retraso; yo no pienso que tenga toda la responsabilidad, porque el camión también salió tarde.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun in the collocation tener la culpa de
grammar: Culpa supplies the fault or blame component in tener la culpa de. Ana assigns blame to Luis; the speaker's no pienso que tenga withholds endorsement of assigning him all the responsibility.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Tener la culpa del retraso = be at fault for the delay; toda la responsabilidad = all the responsibility; tenga refers to Luis.

sentence: Ana presenta su plan como la única solución; a mí no me parece que sea tan útil, porque no resuelve la falta de sillas.
part_of_speech: singular adjective describing practical usefulness
grammar: Útil evaluates a plan's practical usefulness. A mí no me parece que identifies the speaker as evaluator and introduces an assessment whose positive content the speaker does not endorse; sea is present subjunctive.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Tan útil = so useful; única solución = only solution; no resuelve la falta de sillas = does not solve the chair shortage.

sentence: Ana, te digo que hagas una copia para mi mamá ahora mismo; ella necesita ese documento hoy y yo no puedo salir.
part_of_speech: second-person singular irregular present subjunctive verb in a directive clause
grammar: Te digo que is directive here: the speaker tells Ana to make a copy now. Hagas selects the intended action rather than reporting something Ana habitually does.
register: Familiar, firm Mexican Spanish.
note: Ahora mismo = right now; te digo que hagas = I am telling you to make; ella refers to the speaker's mother.

sentence: Mi hermana Ana dice que mi papá hace el desayuno todos los domingos; ella vive con él y conoce bien su rutina.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb in an attributed factual report
grammar: Dice que reports Ana's assertion of her father's routine, so hace is indicative. Ana is the source; the father performs the repeated action.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Hace el desayuno = makes breakfast; ella refers to Ana; él and su refer to the father.

sentence: Ana, insisto en que vengas a cenar mañana; quiero celebrar tu cumpleaños contigo y ya compré los ingredientes.
part_of_speech: second-person singular irregular present subjunctive verb in an influence clause
grammar: Insisto en que expresses an attempt to influence Ana's future action and selects vengas. It does not report that her visit is already an established fact.
register: Familiar, warmly insistent Mexican Spanish.
note: Insisto en que = I insist that; celebrar = celebrate; ingredientes = ingredients; contigo refers to Ana.

sentence: Mi hermana insiste en que Luis viene mañana; según ella, él ya compró su boleto, pero yo todavía no lo he confirmado.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb in an insistent factual report
grammar: Insiste en que reports the sister's insistence that an arrangement is true. Indicative viene presents her factual claim; the speaker separately withholds personal confirmation.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Según ella = according to her; él and su refer to Luis; lo refers to the claim about his visit.

sentence: Mi hermana nos presta su casa mañana y permite que usemos la cocina; mi amiga Ana y yo vamos a preparar ahí la comida para mis padres.
part_of_speech: first-person plural present subjunctive verb in a permission clause
grammar: Permite que selects present subjunctive usemos for the authorized future action. The speaker's sister grants permission; friend Ana and the speaker are allowed to use the kitchen to prepare a meal for the speaker's parents.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Permite que = allows; usemos = we use within the permission; ahí refers to the sister's house; mis padres are the speaker's parents.

sentence: Mis primos Luis y Diego vienen hoy al taller; la encargada prohíbe que entren al cuarto de pintura porque el piso todavía está mojado.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present subjunctive verb in a prohibition clause
grammar: Prohíbe que selects subjunctive entren for the entry the supervisor forbids. Entren refers to both Luis and Diego, not to the singular supervisor.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Primos = male cousins; taller = workshop; encargada = woman in charge; cuarto de pintura = painting room; mojado = wet.

sentence: Pongo la llave del cuarto en una bolsa cerrada; así evito que se pierda entre las cajas durante la mudanza.
part_of_speech: third-person singular pronominal present subjunctive verb phrase
grammar: Evito que selects subjunctive se pierda for the unwanted event the speaker intends to prevent. La llave is the changing entity; se belongs to perderse and is not a reflexive person object.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Así evito que = this way I prevent; se pierda refers to the key getting lost; cajas = boxes.

sentence: El radio todavía no prende; estoy probando una pila nueva para conseguir que funcione, pero aún no sé si eso basta.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present subjunctive verb in an intended-result clause
grammar: Conseguir que funcione names the result the speaker is currently trying to achieve. Because conseguir is inside the purpose of an ongoing test, the sentence does not guarantee success.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Conseguir que funcione = get it to work; aún no sé si eso basta = I still do not know whether that is enough.

sentence: Mi hermano y yo no podemos cargar la mesa solos; hace falta que venga Luis, el vecino que nos va a ayudar, antes de las seis.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verbal locution with a finite clause as subject
grammar: Hacer falta can express a needed action through que followed by a finite clause. Here the needed action is Luis's pending arrival; venga is present subjunctive.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Hace falta que venga Luis = Luis needs to come; solos = without another helper.

sentence: Ana, para la comida de mañana ya tengo arroz y frijoles; es suficiente que traigas las tortillas, no necesitas comprar nada más.
part_of_speech: singular predicate adjective expressing sufficiency
grammar: Suficiente evaluates the proposed contribution as enough. Es suficiente que takes traigas in present subjunctive here; the sentence does not assert that Ana has already brought the tortillas.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Es suficiente que = it is enough that; no necesitas comprar nada más = you do not need to buy anything else.

sentence: La primera reparación no funcionó, pero todavía tenemos otra pila; vale la pena que intentemos encender el radio de nuevo, aunque no hay garantía de éxito.
part_of_speech: first-person plural present subjunctive verb governing an infinitive
grammar: Intentar followed directly by an infinitive means attempting to perform that action. Intentemos encender names the joint attempt; vale la pena que supplies the present-subjunctive environment.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Intentar encender = try to turn on; vale la pena = it is worthwhile. An attempt does not guarantee success.

sentence: Tengo miedo de que falle el refrigerador durante mi viaje, porque últimamente no enfría bien; por eso mi hermana va a pasar a revisar la comida.
part_of_speech: governed preposition followed by a finite-clause conjunction
grammar: In tener miedo de que, de remains before the conjunction que when the feared event is expressed as a finite clause. Falle is present subjunctive within that feared possibility.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Tengo miedo de que falle = I am afraid that it will fail; refrigerador = refrigerator; pasar a revisar = stop by to check.

sentence: Ana y yo ya ensayamos nuestra presentación; confío en que salga bien mañana y estoy contento con la preparación, aunque todavía falta presentarla.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative verb with an en que complement
grammar: Confiar en que expresses confidence or firm hope concerning an outcome. Here salga is subjunctive within that confident hope; it does not negate the speaker's confidence.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Confío en que salga bien = I am confident it will turn out well; presentarla = deliver the presentation.

sentence: Cierro con llave el cuarto de pintura para impedir que entre mi hijo Luis esta tarde; el piso todavía está mojado.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb governing a finite que-clause
grammar: Impedir que names an action being prevented. The locking is intended to prevent Luis's entry, and entre is present subjunctive within that preventive purpose.
register: Neutral Mexican Spanish.
note: Impedir que alguien entre = prevent someone from entering; cerrar con llave = lock; mojado = wet.

sentence: Ana, voy a hablar con tu hermano Luis para hacer que cambie su horario de ensayo; toca de noche y yo no puedo dormir.
part_of_speech: causative infinitive verb governing a finite que-clause
grammar: Hacer que introduces causing or bringing about another person's action. Here it occurs within the speaker's purpose: Luis is intended to change his schedule, and success is not guaranteed.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Hacer que alguien cambie algo = get someone to change something; ensayo = rehearsal; toca = plays music here.

sentence: Ana, antes de enviar tu invitación, te sugiero que revises la dirección; yo veo dos números distintos y no sé cuál es el correcto.
part_of_speech: first-person singular stem-changing present indicative verb
grammar: Sugerir que introduces a proposed action for another person. Sugiero has the e-to-ie present stem change; revises is present subjunctive within the suggestion.
register: Familiar, tentative Mexican Spanish.
note: Te sugiero que revises = I suggest that you check; distintos = different. The speaker offers advice rather than reporting Ana's review.

sentence: Luis, todavía no acordamos dónde hablar del viaje; propongo que nos reunamos mañana en mi casa, porque ahí podemos conversar sin ruido.
part_of_speech: first-person plural present subjunctive verb with visible pronominal nos
grammar: Propongo que introduces a joint meeting as a proposal. Visible nos belongs to reunirse and includes Luis and the speaker; reunamos supplies the proposed action.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Propongo = I propose; reunirnos = meet or get together; conversar = talk together.

sentence: Ana, mañana tú vas a entregar mi solicitud en la escuela; necesito que recuerdes llevar también mi identificación, porque van a pedir los dos documentos.
part_of_speech: second-person singular present subjunctive verb governing an infinitive
grammar: Necesito que selects recuerdes. Recordar followed directly by llevar means remembering to perform one's own pending action: Ana must both remember and take the identification.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: Solicitud = application; identificación = identification document; recordar llevar = remember to take.

sentence: Hermano, ¿a qué hora empieza tu ceremonia mañana? Tú ya sabes cuándo empieza; dímelo ahora para organizar mi salida.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached first-person singular indirect-object me and neuter direct-object lo
grammar: Lo represents the answer to the visible time question, rather than a masculine physical object. Me identifies the speaker receiving that information; both attach to di.
register: Familiar family request in Mexican Spanish.
note: Ceremonia = ceremony; organizar mi salida = plan my departure. Dímelo preserves the stress of di.

sentence: Ana, no entiendo por qué el recibo incluye dos cobros por la misma compra; explícamelo con calma, porque necesito saber cuánto debo pagar.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached first-person singular indirect-object me and neuter direct-object lo
grammar: Lo represents the practical issue introduced by por qué: why the purchase appears twice. Me identifies the explanation's recipient; the affirmative command carries both clitics.
register: Familiar Mexican request for a calm explanation.
note: Con calma = calmly; cobros = charges. Explícamelo requests an explanation rather than merely a yes-or-no answer.

sentence: Ana, ayer tu vecino encontró mi cartera y me la devolvió; cuéntaselo a mi mamá de principio a fin, porque ella todavía cree que la perdí.
part_of_speech: adverbial phrase expressing complete narrative coverage
grammar: De principio a fin asks for the complete sequence of the incident. In visible cuéntaselo, Ana is the storyteller, se identifies the speaker's mother as audience, and lo represents the recovery and return of the wallet.
register: Familiar Mexican Spanish.
note: De principio a fin = from beginning to end; cuéntaselo a mi mamá = tell my mother about it; cartera = wallet.

sentence: Hijo, tu hermana y yo queremos comparar las dos fotos de la casa antes de decidir dónde vivir; enséñanoslas en tu teléfono, por favor.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached first-person plural indirect-object nos and feminine plural direct-object las
grammar: Enseñar means show objects here. Nos identifies the parent and the son's sister as viewers; las represents the two photos.
register: Courteous familiar family request in Mexican Spanish.
note: Comparar = compare; decidir dónde vivir = decide where to live. Enséñanoslas means show the two photos to us.

sentence: Luis, ese saco es de tu talla, pero no sabemos si te queda bien; pruébatelo frente al espejo a ver si puedes mover los brazos con comodidad antes de comprarlo.
part_of_speech: construction introducing an exploratory check
grammar: A ver si introduces what the try-on is intended to find out. The following puedes is indicative in this indirect check; the construction does not assert that comfortable movement is already established.
register: Familiar Mexican clothing advice.
note: A ver si puedes mover los brazos = to see whether you can move your arms; pruébatelo = try it on. The command is written pruébatelo, with an accent on é.

sentence: Hermano, este paraguas es mío, pero está lloviendo y tú tienes que regresar a casa; llévatelo y me lo devuelves mañana.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative in pronominal llevarse with attached te and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Llevarse expresses taking an object away with oneself. Te belongs to this pronominal construction; it does not identify someone receiving a delivery from another actor.
register: Familiar Mexican family offer.
note: Paraguas = umbrella; llévatelo = take it away with you. The speaker expects its return tomorrow.

sentence: Ana, tu hermana Clara te prestó su chamarra azul para el viaje; ya regresaste y su dueña la necesita: devuélvesela hoy.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun identifying an owner
grammar: Dueña identifies Clara as the jacket's owner. In visible devuélvesela, se represents Clara receiving her possession back, and la represents the jacket; Ana performs the return.
register: Familiar Mexican instruction.
note: Su dueña = its owner, Clara; devuélvesela hoy = return the jacket to her today.

sentence: Luis, la directora tiene el permiso escrito para nuestra entrada al salón; pídeselo a ella antes de la reunión, porque sin ese documento no podemos pasar.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached singular indirect-object replacement se and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Se identifies the director as the person asked for the permit, not someone receiving the permit. Lo represents permiso; Luis makes the request.
register: Familiar Mexican coordination.
note: Directora = female director or principal; permiso escrito = written permission document; pídeselo = ask her for it.

sentence: Rosa, tú me cortaste el pelo hoy y todavía no te pago el corte; cóbramelo ahora, por favor, tengo el dinero listo.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached first-person singular payer dative me and masculine singular service direct-object lo
grammar: Me identifies the customer who must pay; lo represents the haircut as the service charged for. Me does not identify someone receiving the haircut's payment.
register: Courteous familiar Mexican service request.
note: Cortar el pelo = cut hair; corte = haircut here. Rosa charges, and the speaker pays.

sentence: Hermana, estoy en el trabajo y queda un pedazo de pastel en casa; guárdamelo, porque voy a llegar después de la cena.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached first-person singular beneficiary dative me and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Guardar means setting a portion aside for later consumption here. Me identifies the beneficiary while lo represents pedazo de pastel; no delivery is requested.
register: Familiar Mexican family request.
note: Pastel = cake; guárdamelo = save that piece for me. The speaker is still away at work.

sentence: Ana, mi hermano y yo llegaremos diez minutos después de ti al cine; hay dos butacas junto a tu lugar: resérvanoslas, porque queremos sentarnos contigo.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached first-person plural beneficiary dative nos and feminine plural direct-object las
grammar: Reservar means keeping the available seats for the arriving group. Nos identifies the speaker and their brother; las identifies the two butacas.
register: Familiar Mexican social coordination.
note: Butacas = theater or cinema seats; tu lugar = your seat here; resérvanoslas = save those two seats for us.

sentence: Ana, tengo las dos manos ocupadas con este espejo y no puedo abrir la puerta; sosténmelo un momento mientras saco la llave.
part_of_speech: irregular affirmative tú imperative with attached first-person singular beneficiary dative me and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Sostener means supporting an object's weight here. Its affirmative tú command is sostén; me marks the person helped and lo represents espejo.
register: Familiar Mexican request for practical help.
note: Espejo = mirror; manos ocupadas = hands occupied; sosténmelo = hold the mirror for me.

sentence: Ana, la lámpara está al otro lado de la mesa y aquí no veo bien las letras; acércamela, por favor, para poder leer la carta.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached first-person singular dative me and feminine singular direct-object la
grammar: Acercar moves an object nearer, contrasting with acercarse as moving oneself nearer. La represents the lamp; me marks the speaker as the reference point.
register: Courteous familiar Mexican request.
note: Lámpara = lamp; al otro lado de la mesa = on the other side of the table; letras = letters on the page.

sentence: Papá, mis lentes están en la repisa alta; yo no llego hasta ahí y tú sí: alcánzamelos, por favor, para leer este mensaje.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached first-person singular indirect-object me and masculine plural direct-object los
grammar: Alcanzar means retrieving and handing over something out of the speaker's reach. Los represents lentes; me identifies the person receiving them.
register: Courteous familiar Mexican family request.
note: Lentes = eyeglasses; repisa = shelf; yo no llego hasta ahí = I cannot reach that far.

sentence: Ana, mi falda ya está lista en el taller de costura y el pedido está a mi nombre; yo salgo del trabajo a las ocho y el taller cierra a las seis: recógemela hoy, por favor.
part_of_speech: prepositional phrase identifying the name under which an order is registered
grammar: A mi nombre identifies how the workshop's order is registered. It does not make the speaker the collector: Ana is asked to collect the skirt, and me in recógemela marks the speaker as beneficiary.
register: Courteous familiar Mexican request.
note: El pedido está a mi nombre = the order is under my name; taller de costura = sewing workshop; recógemela = pick it up for me.

sentence: Luis, mi hermano Diego espera mi mensaje con la dirección de la fiesta; tú tienes el texto en tu teléfono y yo no tengo internet: mándaselo de mi parte ahora, por favor.
part_of_speech: prepositional phrase attributing a communication to its source
grammar: De mi parte attributes the message to the speaker even though Luis sends it. In mándaselo, Luis is the instructed sender, se identifies Diego as recipient, and lo represents the message.
register: Courteous familiar Mexican coordination.
note: Mándaselo de mi parte = send it to him from me. The person transmitting the message and the person it is from are different.

sentence: Hija, esas dos sillas son tuyas y tu prima Ana necesita sentar a sus invitados esta tarde; préstaselas para su cena; ella te las trae de vuelta mañana.
part_of_speech: adverbial phrase expressing return movement
grammar: De vuelta marks bringing the borrowed chairs back to their owner. In préstaselas, the daughter lends, se identifies borrower Ana, and las represents the chairs; in te las trae, Ana brings them back to the daughter.
register: Familiar Mexican family coordination.
note: Traer algo de vuelta = bring something back; prima = female cousin; sentar a sus invitados = provide seats for her guests.

sentence: Hermano, mi hija y yo ya tenemos los platos listos y el arroz está caliente; sírvenoslo ahora en dos raciones iguales, por favor, porque ya vamos a comer.
part_of_speech: feminine plural noun naming individual food portions
grammar: Raciones counts individual portions of food. The two equal servings are for the speaker and their daughter; in sírvenoslo, nos identifies those diners and lo represents arroz.
register: Courteous familiar Mexican family request.
note: Dos raciones iguales = two equal servings; sírvenoslo = serve the rice to us.

sentence: Mamá, esta manzana es para mí, pero está muy grande para comerla entera; pártemela en cuatro pedazos, por favor.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached first-person singular beneficiary dative me and feminine singular direct-object la
grammar: Partir means dividing a food item into pieces. Me identifies the person helped; la represents manzana. This is distinct from partir meaning depart.
