register: Courteous familiar Mexican family request.
note: Entera = whole; en cuatro pedazos = into four pieces; pártemela = cut the apple up for me.

sentence: Ana, el caldo de tu hijo Luis está frío y él ya quiere cenar; caliéntaselo antes de servirlo, por favor.
part_of_speech: stem-changing affirmative tú imperative with attached singular beneficiary replacement se and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Calentar is transitive here: Ana warms the broth for Luis. Se identifies Luis as beneficiary; lo represents caldo, and the command uses calienta.
register: Courteous familiar Mexican family coordination.
note: Caldo = broth; caliéntaselo = warm the broth for Luis. Se is not reflexive.

sentence: Hijo, todavía traes puesto el casco de la bicicleta y ya estás sentado a la mesa; desabrocha la correa y quítatelo para comer más cómodo.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative verb
grammar: Desabrochar means undoing a fastening. The son is told to unfasten the helmet strap and remove the helmet; in quítatelo, te identifies the son as wearer and lo represents casco.
register: Familiar Mexican family instruction.
note: Desabrocha la correa = unfasten the strap; quítatelo = take the helmet off; cómodo agrees with the son.

sentence: Ana, vamos a caminar por el patio y hay lodo; tus botas están junto a la puerta: póntelas en lugar de los zapatos de tela para no enlodarlos.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached masculine plural direct-object clitic los
grammar: Enlodar takes the item made muddy as its direct object. Los in enlodarlos represents zapatos de tela; visible póntelas instead has te for Ana as wearer and las for botas.
register: Familiar Mexican practical advice.
note: Lodo = mud; enlodar algo = get something muddy; enlodarlos refers to the fabric shoes. En lugar de = instead of.

sentence: Hermano, estos zapatos son míos y tienen manchas de lodo; límpiamelos con el trapo, por favor, porque yo estoy lavando la ropa.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached first-person singular affected-possessor dative me and masculine plural direct-object los
grammar: Me marks the speaker as affected owner and beneficiary of cleaning. Los represents the shoes; the brother performs the cleaning.
register: Courteous familiar Mexican family request.
note: Trapo = cleaning cloth; manchas de lodo = mud stains; límpiamelos = clean my shoes for me.

sentence: Luis, la bicicleta de mi mamá hace un ruido raro; revísasela antes del paseo, por favor, porque tú sabes reparar bicicletas.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached singular affected-owner replacement se and feminine singular direct-object la
grammar: Revisar means inspecting a possession for a possible defect here. Se identifies the speaker's mother as affected owner; la represents bicicleta, and Luis performs the inspection.
register: Courteous familiar Mexican request.
note: Ruido raro = unusual noise; revísasela = inspect her bicycle for her.

sentence: Ana, este mensaje tiene una falta de ortografía; corrígemelo antes de enviarlo, por favor, porque tú escribes mejor que yo.
part_of_speech: stem-changing affirmative tú imperative with attached first-person singular beneficiary dative me and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Corregir means repairing an error in written content. The affirmative tú command is corrige, with e changing to i; me marks the beneficiary and lo represents mensaje.
register: Courteous familiar Mexican request.
note: Falta de ortografía = spelling error; corrígemelo = correct the message for me.

sentence: Ana, mi papá solo entiende español y este mensaje está en francés; tú hablas los dos idiomas: tradúceselo para que él sepa a qué hora empieza la reunión.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached singular indirect-object replacement se and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Traducir changes a message from one language into another. Se identifies the father as the person receiving the translation; lo represents mensaje.
register: Familiar Mexican request for language assistance.
note: Francés = French; idiomas = languages; tradúceselo = translate the message for the father.

sentence: Ana, mi hermano y yo no oímos bien la última instrucción por el ruido; repítenosla más despacio, por favor, porque no sabemos dónde poner las cajas.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun naming a direction for carrying out a task
grammar: Instrucción names a direction telling people how or where to carry out a task. In repítenosla, la refers to this feminine noun and nos identifies the speaker and their brother as listeners.
register: Courteous familiar Mexican request.
note: La última instrucción = the last instruction; repítenosla más despacio = repeat it to us more slowly. Noise prevented the two listeners from hearing clearly.

sentence: Ana, mi papá nos invitó a comer el domingo y tú y yo ya decidimos que vamos; él espera nuestra respuesta: confírmaselo hoy, por favor.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached singular indirect-object replacement se and neuter direct-object lo
grammar: Confirmar means communicating a settled answer to another person here. Se identifies the father; lo represents the decision that Ana and the speaker will attend.
register: Courteous familiar Mexican family coordination.
note: Confírmaselo = confirm to the father that we are coming. Ana conveys the confirmation rather than merely checking the arrangement herself.

sentence: Hermano, mañana tengo que devolver los libros a la biblioteca, pero ahora estoy cocinando y no puedo anotarlo; recuérdamelo esta noche, por favor.
part_of_speech: stem-changing affirmative tú imperative with attached first-person singular indirect-object me and neuter direct-object lo
grammar: Recordar means causing another person to remember here. Me identifies the person to remind; lo represents the pending task, and the brother gives the reminder later.
register: Courteous familiar Mexican family request.
note: Biblioteca = library; anotarlo = write the task down; recuérdamelo = remind me about that task.

sentence: Ana, ya decidimos que la clase de baile empezará mañana a las seis; tu hermano Luis espera la noticia: anúnciaselo hoy, por favor.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached singular indirect-object replacement se and neuter direct-object lo
grammar: Anunciar communicates news of the settled schedule. Se identifies Luis as the audience; neuter lo represents the announcement's content, not the feminine noun noticia.
register: Courteous familiar Mexican coordination.
note: Clase de baile = dance class; anúnciaselo = announce the starting-time decision to Luis. Ana is the intermediary.

sentence: Luis, Ana todavía no sabe que rompiste su taza; no se lo ocultes, porque ella la está buscando.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Ocultar algo a alguien means concealing something from someone. Se represents Ana and neuter lo represents the fact that Luis broke her cup.
register: Familiar Mexican conversation.
note: The person kept uninformed is Ana; she is also the cup's owner.

sentence: Ana, Clara te dijo en privado que va a cambiar de trabajo; no se lo reveles a sus compañeros durante la comida.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Revelar means making previously private information known. Se identifies Clara's coworkers as the audience; lo represents Clara's planned job change.
register: Familiar Mexican conversation.
note: Clara supplied the information privately to Ana; the coworkers are a different audience.

sentence: Ana, este documento es para Luis, pero Marta todavía tiene que autorizar la entrega; no se lo entregues hasta que ella te dé el visto bueno.
part_of_speech: masculine singular fixed noun phrase
grammar: Dar el visto bueno means giving approval. Marta grants the authorization; Luis is the separate intended document recipient represented by se.
register: Familiar Mexican practical instruction.
note: Hasta que ella te dé el visto bueno = until Marta gives you approval; the authorization is still pending.

sentence: Luis, el libro que tienes es de Clara y ella te lo prestó solo hasta hoy; no se lo retengas, porque lo necesita para su clase de mañana.
part_of_speech: irregular negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Retener means keeping an item instead of allowing its owner to recover it here. Retengas uses the irregular teng- stem; se identifies Clara as the affected owner.
register: Familiar Mexican loan coordination.
note: Clara lent Luis her book only through today and needs it tomorrow.

sentence: Ana, ya acordaste pagarle doscientos pesos a Julia por arreglar tu vestido; no le regatees el precio ahora.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Regatear el precio means trying to negotiate a lower price. Le identifies Julia, whose fee Ana has already agreed to pay.
register: Familiar Mexican conversation about a specific service arrangement.
note: The instruction concerns this already agreed fee, without a general claim about bargaining.

sentence: Luis, vamos a pagarle a Rosa por pintar la sala, pero todavía no sabemos qué día vendrá; no le adelantes el pago hasta que ella confirme la fecha.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb in a payment construction
grammar: Adelantar el pago means paying before the service here, rather than moving an appointment earlier. Rosa must first confirm the service date.
register: Familiar Mexican coordination of a stated household arrangement.
note: Le refers to Rosa as payee; the instruction belongs to this particular arrangement.

sentence: Ana, Pedro pagó con su dinero el gasto de las copias, no Luis; no se lo reembolses a Luis por error.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Reembolsar un gasto means paying back an expense someone covered. Pedro was the original payer; the command excludes Luis as reimbursement recipient.
register: Familiar Mexican expense coordination.
note: Se refers to the proposed but incorrect recipient Luis; lo represents el gasto de las copias.

sentence: Luis, el desayuno es mío y yo voy a pagarlo; no lo cargues a la cuenta de Ana, porque ella solo pidió un café.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb with g-to-gu spelling
grammar: Cargar algo a una cuenta means adding its charge to that account. Lo represents the speaker's breakfast; Ana's account is the excluded billing destination.
register: Familiar Mexican coordination during a restaurant purchase.
note: This is the billing sense of cargar, rather than physically carrying a load.

sentence: Ana, el comentario sobre cambiar la hora lo hizo Clara, no Pedro; no se lo atribuyas a Pedro cuando hables con Luis.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb with stem atribuy-
grammar: Atribuir un comentario a alguien means identifying that person as its source. Clara made the remark; Pedro is the explicitly excluded source.
register: Familiar Mexican correction of speaker attribution.
note: Se refers to Pedro as the proposed source; Luis is the separate future listener.

sentence: Luis, tú ya elegiste dónde poner las camas; no le impongas tu decisión a Ana sin hablar con ella, porque los dos van a compartir el cuarto.
part_of_speech: irregular negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Imponer una decisión a alguien means requiring that person to accept it without participating in the choice. Impongas uses the irregular pong- stem.
register: Familiar Mexican discussion of a shared living arrangement.
note: Luis has chosen the bed positions; Ana is the other person who will share the room.

sentence: Ana, Luis acaba de recibir tu invitación y está revisando su horario; no le exijas una respuesta inmediata, porque todavía no sabe si puede ir.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb with g-to-j spelling
grammar: Exigir una respuesta a alguien means demanding an answer from that person. Exijas has j before a; le identifies Luis as the person being pressed for an answer.
register: Familiar Mexican discussion of an invitation.
note: Luis is checking his availability and has not yet decided whether he can attend.

sentence: Luis, Ana vino para resolver contigo la discusión de hoy; no le reproches otra vez que perdió tu libro hace dos años.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Reprochar algo a alguien means expressing blame to that person for it. The old book loss is distinguished from today's discussion that Ana came to resolve.
register: Familiar Mexican conversation during an interpersonal repair.
note: Le identifies Ana as the person receiving the reproach; perdió states the old mistake being brought up.

sentence: Ana, Luis reprobó el examen anterior y dice que ese recuerdo es muy doloroso; no se lo recuerdes justo antes del examen de hoy.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb
grammar: Reprobar un examen means failing an exam. Reprobó reports Luis's completed earlier result; visible recuerdes asks Ana not to bring that result back to his attention.
register: Familiar Mexican conversation.
note: Anterior = previous; doloroso = painful. Se identifies Luis as the person reminded, and lo represents his earlier exam failure.

sentence: Luis, le prestaste dinero a Ana y ella ya te lo devolvió; no le eches ese favor en cara durante la discusión de hoy.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb component of echar algo en cara
grammar: Echarle algo en cara means reproaching someone with it. Eches is the verbal component of this discontinuous expression; le identifies Ana and ese favor identifies the earlier loan.
register: Familiar Mexican interpersonal conversation.
note: No le eches ese favor en cara = do not throw that favor back in Ana's face.

sentence: Ana, Luis llegó primero a la fila y tiene el número doce; tú tienes el trece, así que no le disputes su lugar.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Disputar un lugar a alguien means contesting that person's claim to the place. Le identifies Luis; su lugar is his earlier position in the service line.
register: Familiar Mexican practical correction.
note: The numbered order makes the contested place explicit; disputar does not mean ordinary conversation here.

sentence: Luis, esta silla está reservada para Clara, que llega en cinco minutos; no se la cedas a Pedro, porque él ya tiene otra junto a la ventana.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Ceder una silla a alguien means letting that person take the seat. Se identifies Pedro as the excluded recipient; la represents the chair reserved for Clara.
register: Familiar Mexican seating coordination.
note: Clara is the reservation holder; Pedro already has a different chair.

sentence: Ana, hoy es lunes y esta bicicleta es mía; no puedo prescindir de ella mañana temprano, y Luis no puede devolverla hasta el viernes: no se la prestes.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb governing de
grammar: Prescindir de algo means doing without it. No puedo prescindir de ella makes the owner's need explicit; ella refers to the bicycle.
register: Familiar Mexican coordination of a proposed loan.
note: The speaker needs the bicycle Tuesday morning, but Luis cannot return it until Friday. Se identifies Luis as the proposed borrower.

sentence: Luis, Clara te prestó su cámara y Pedro ofrece pagarte por usarla en su fiesta; no se la alquiles sin permiso de Clara.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Alquilar means giving someone temporary use in exchange for payment here. Clara owns the camera; Luis would rent it out to Pedro rather than rent it for himself.
register: Familiar Mexican conversation about borrowed property.
note: Se identifies Pedro as the proposed paying user; la represents Clara's camera.

sentence: Ana, ese libro es de Clara y tú lo tienes prestado; no se lo regales a Pedro para su cumpleaños, porque Clara lo necesita mañana.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Regalar means transferring something as a gift rather than lending it. Clara is the owner; Pedro is the proposed gift recipient.
register: Familiar Mexican conversation about a borrowed book.
note: Se represents Pedro and lo the book that Ana has borrowed from Clara.

sentence: Luis, Ana pidió sopa para comer y el restaurante la entrega a la una; no le prepares arroz, porque ya pagó su pedido.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Preparar arroz means making food here, rather than getting study materials ready. Le identifies Ana as the person for whom Luis would cook.
register: Familiar Mexican meal coordination.
note: Ana's different arrangement is explicit: she has ordered and paid for soup delivered at one.

sentence: Ana, Luis avisó de antemano que no quiere pastel y ya eligió fruta para el postre; no le guardes el último pedazo, porque Marta sí quiere comerlo ahora.
part_of_speech: adverbial phrase
grammar: De antemano places Luis's notice ahead of the relevant meal decision. His refusal is already known when the speaker asks Ana not to reserve the cake.
register: Familiar Mexican meal coordination.
note: Avisó de antemano = gave notice beforehand. Le identifies Luis as the proposed beneficiary; Marta wants the remaining cake now.

sentence: Luis, Ana ya rechazó viajar de noche porque quiere ver el paisaje; no le sugieras otra vez el camión de las once de la noche.
part_of_speech: stem-changing negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Sugerir takes a named option directly here, rather than a que-clause. Sugieras is a direct negative command with e changing to ie.
register: Familiar Mexican travel discussion.
note: Le identifies Ana; the eleven-at-night bus repeats the nighttime option she already rejected.

sentence: Ana, Luis trabaja todo el sábado y ya nos dijo que no puede salir; no le propongas el paseo de ese día.
part_of_speech: irregular negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Proponer takes the outing itself as its direct object here. Propongas uses pong- in a negative tú command; le identifies Luis as the person receiving the proposal.
register: Familiar Mexican social planning.
note: Ese día refers to Saturday, when Luis has explicitly said he cannot go out.

sentence: Ana, Luis todavía no ha aceptado arreglar la bicicleta de Clara; no le prometas a Clara la reparación para mañana en nombre de Luis.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Prometer takes an outcome and a recipient here. Ana would make the promise to Clara, while Luis would have to perform the repair and has not committed to it.
register: Familiar Mexican coordination of a proposed favor.
note: En nombre de Luis means on Luis's behalf; the command distinguishes the promiser from the proposed performer.

sentence: Luis, Ana te preguntó si el local abre el domingo, pero tú no has revisado el horario; no le asegures que estará abierto.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Asegurar que presents a claim to someone as dependable. The negative command concerns giving that assurance; Luis has not checked the opening schedule.
register: Familiar Mexican practical conversation.
note: Le identifies Ana as the listener. Estará abierto concerns Sunday's future opening, rather than a conjecture about a current state.

sentence: Ana, tú y yo recordamos horas distintas para la reunión; no me jures que empieza a las seis, porque necesito ver el mensaje original.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Jurar que means emphatically swearing that a claim is true here. Me identifies the speaker as the listener; the request seeks the original message rather than an oath.
register: Familiar Mexican social coordination.
note: Ana's six-o'clock claim is quoted as the content of the proposed assurance, without being endorsed by the speaker.

sentence: Luis, Ana está a tu lado y te oye bien; no le grites que la comida es a las dos: puedes decírselo con tu voz normal.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Gritar specifies loud delivery of the stated information. Le identifies Ana as the listener; the meal time is the content being conveyed.
register: Familiar Mexican household coordination.
note: Ana is nearby and can hear Luis; the instruction changes delivery volume, not the message.

sentence: Luis, estoy anotando tu dirección y no oigo bien tus palabras; no me la susurres, por favor, porque necesito escuchar cada número.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Susurrar specifies speaking in a whisper. Me identifies the listener who is writing, and la represents Luis's address.
register: Courteous familiar Mexican request.
note: The listener requests audible delivery so that every address number can be recorded.

sentence: Ana, tu hijo Luis está aprendiendo a escribir y debe formular su propia respuesta; no se la dictes, porque esta tarea es para practicar.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Dictar una respuesta means saying its wording for someone else to write. Se identifies Luis as the prospective writer, and la represents his answer.
register: Familiar Mexican conversation about a child's learning task.
note: The task calls for Luis to formulate his own answer, rather than transcribe Ana's wording.

sentence: Luis, Ana necesita que le cuentes lo que pasó en la reunión para escribir el informe; no se lo resumas, porque necesita el relato completo.
part_of_speech: negative tú imperative verb
grammar: Resumir means reducing an account to its main points. Se identifies Ana as audience; lo represents the account of what happened at the meeting.
register: Familiar Mexican coordination of an account for a report.
note: Ana asks for the full account because she must write the report.

sentence: Hermana, ya tienes tu bolsa lista, pero todavía quiero darte un abrazo; no te me vayas aún.
part_of_speech: second-person singular pronominal clitic followed by first-person singular expressive dative clitic
grammar: Te belongs to irse and agrees with the sister addressed as tú. Me adds the speaker's affectionate involvement; it is not a recipient of a transferred object. Second-person te precedes first-person me.
register: Affectionate informal Mexican family speech.
note: No te me vayas aún = do not leave just yet, with affectionate personal involvement. The speaker still wants to give their sister a hug.

sentence: Hijo, ya tienes sueño, pero solo necesitamos un minuto para combinar tu camisa con el pantalón de mañana; no te me duermas todavía.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with a direct clothing object and con complement
grammar: Combinar una prenda con otra means matching one garment with another. The shirt is the direct object; con introduces the pants it will be matched with.
register: Affectionate informal Mexican parent-child speech.
note: No te me duermas todavía asks the son not to fall asleep yet; te belongs to dormirse and me expresses the parent's involvement.

sentence: Don Ernesto, ese ruido fue una caja vacía que cayó al piso; no se me asuste, porque nadie está herido.
part_of_speech: usted-agreeing pronominal clitic se followed by first-person singular expressive dative me
grammar: Se belongs to asustarse and agrees with respectfully addressed usted. Me expresses the speaker's personal involvement; se is not replacing le before an object pronoun.
register: Warm respectful Mexican address.
note: No se me asuste = do not get frightened, with personal concern from the speaker.

sentence: Ana y yo somos dueños de este sillón; Diego y Pablo se nos lo llevaron al patio sin pedir permiso y ahora no tenemos dónde sentarnos.
part_of_speech: pronominal se followed by first-person plural affected-source dative nos and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Se belongs to llevarse with Diego and Pablo as actors. Nos marks Ana and the speaker as affected owners and source; lo represents sillón. The order is se, first-person dative, third-person direct object.
register: Informal Mexican complaint.
note: Diego and Pablo took the owners' armchair away to the patio; se is not a replacement recipient clitic.

sentence: Luis, esa bicicleta es tuya y tu hermano Pedro se te la llevó al parque sin consultarte; ahora tú no puedes ir a tu clase en ella.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached second-person singular personal direct-object clitic te
grammar: Consultar a alguien means seeking that person's view before acting here. Attached te identifies Luis as the person Pedro did not consult; the separate visible te in se te la marks Luis as the bicycle's affected owner.
register: Informal Mexican family conversation.
note: In se te la llevó, se belongs to llevarse, te identifies the affected owner Luis, and la represents his bicycle. Pedro is the actor.

sentence: Hermana, ese pan dulce era mío y lo guardé para mi desayuno, pero Pedro se me lo comió todo anoche; hoy solo queda fruta.
part_of_speech: consumptive pronominal se followed by first-person singular affected-owner dative me and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Se belongs to comerse in the completed consumption of the whole item. Me marks the speaker as affected owner; lo represents pan dulce. Pedro is the eater, so se is not a speaker-recipient replacement.
register: Informal Mexican complaint to a sibling.
note: Todo makes complete consumption explicit; the speaker had saved the sweet bread for breakfast.

sentence: Hijo, este dinero es tuyo para toda la semana; no te me lo gastes todo hoy, porque mañana necesitas pagar el camión.
part_of_speech: second-person singular consumptive pronominal te followed by first-person singular expressive dative me and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Te belongs to gastarse with the son as spender; me expresses the parent's personal concern; lo represents dinero. Without se, second person precedes first person, which precedes the third-person direct object.
register: Expressive informal Mexican parent-child speech.
note: The money belongs to the son. Me expresses the parent's involvement rather than ownership or receipt of that money.

sentence: Mi primo Raúl acordó pasar una noche con Ana y conmigo, pero se nos quedó cuatro noches y tuvimos que dormir en la sala.
part_of_speech: third-person singular pronominal se followed by first-person plural affected-host dative nos
grammar: Se belongs to quedarse with Raúl as the visitor who stays. Nos identifies Ana and the speaker as hosts affected by the extended stay; it does not identify a source losing an object.
register: Informal Mexican account of a family visit.
note: Raúl stayed four nights rather than the agreed one, and the hosts had to sleep in the living room.

sentence: Luis, ayer te presté mi reloj y tú me lo perdiste en el parque; ahora necesito que me ayudes a buscarlo.
part_of_speech: first-person singular affected-owner dative me followed by masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Luis is explicitly the subject of perdiste. Me identifies the speaker as the affected owner of the lost watch; lo represents reloj. Me is not a transfer recipient, and there is no accidental se.
register: Informal Mexican conversation about an entrusted possession.
note: The speaker lent Luis the watch and now asks him to help search for it.

sentence: Ana, tú me prestaste tu taza y yo te la rompí mientras lavaba los platos; voy a reponértela mañana.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached second-person singular beneficiary dative te and feminine singular direct-object la
grammar: Reponer means replacing the lost or damaged item here. In reponértela, te identifies Ana as the person receiving the replacement and la represents the cup; the attached form requires an accent.
register: Familiar Mexican acknowledgment of damage and commitment to replace an item.
note: Yo te la rompí explicitly names the speaker as the person who broke Ana's cup. There is no accidental se.

sentence: El contrato es para la directora; prefiero entregárselo en mano y revisar las firmas con ella, en lugar de enviarlo por correo.
meaning: by hand, directly to the recipient
part_of_speech: adverbial locution specifying direct delivery
grammar: Entregar algo en mano means handing it directly to its recipient. In prefiero entregárselo, the recipient and object remain attached to the infinitive; preferir does not categorically prohibit climbing.
register: Neutral Mexican administrative conversation.
note: Contrato = contract; firmas = signatures. Se identifies the director and lo represents the contract.

sentence: Mi hermano no entiende el cambio de horario; insisto en explicárselo yo antes de que salga, porque fui quien habló con la maestra.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached replacement indirect-object se and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Insistir en governs the infinitive here. Both clitics remain attached to explicar: se identifies the brother as listener and lo represents the schedule change.
register: Neutral Mexican family conversation.
note: Insisto en explicárselo yo emphasizes that the speaker insists on personally providing the explanation.

sentence: Las invitaciones ya están listas; Paula se comprometió a enviárselas hoy a su tía Rosa y a su tío Javier y anotó sus direcciones para cumplir.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite pronominal verb phrase with governed preposition a
grammar: Comprometerse a + infinitive expresses taking personal responsibility for an action. The main se belongs to comprometerse; the separate se in enviárselas replaces les for Rosa and Javier.
register: Neutral Mexican account of a family arrangement.
note: Anotó = wrote down; cumplir = fulfill the undertaking here. Las represents the invitations.

sentence: Este libro es de Raúl y él lo necesita para su clase de mañana; hay que devolvérselo hoy.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached replacement indirect-object se and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Impersonal hay que introduces necessity. The infinitive's clitics attach to devolver; they do not climb before hay.
register: Neutral Mexican conversation about a borrowed book.
note: Se identifies Raúl as the person receiving his book back; lo represents libro.

sentence: La reunión cambió al viernes y mis padres todavía creen que es el jueves; conviene contárselo hoy para evitar un viaje en vano.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached replacement indirect-object se and neuter direct-object lo
grammar: Contárselo names the action evaluated by conviene and functions as its infinitival subject. Its audience and content clitics remain attached: se identifies the parents and lo represents the schedule change.
register: Neutral Mexican family planning.
note: Conviene = is advisable; en vano = to no useful effect.

sentence: Estas llaves son de Rosa; a mí me importa entregárselas antes de salir, porque ella necesita entrar a su casa.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached replacement indirect-object se and feminine plural direct-object las
grammar: Me identifies the speaker as the person who cares under importar. Inside the infinitival subject, se identifies Rosa as recipient and las represents the keys; these roles belong to entregar.
register: Neutral Mexican coordination before departure.
note: The speaker cares about completing the handover; Rosa receives the keys.

sentence: El código nuevo tiene ocho números; me cuesta recordarlo sin consultar mi libreta, aunque lo uso todos los días.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb taking a reference source as direct object
grammar: Consultar mi libreta means looking in the notebook for information. Consultar takes the reference source directly, extending its earlier use for seeking a person's view.
register: Neutral Mexican explanation of a memory difficulty.
note: Código = code; libreta = notebook. Me cuesta recordarlo describes difficulty remembering the code; lo uso means I use the code.

sentence: Mi hijo ya reconoce su abrigo, pero todavía pide ayuda para vestirse; le enseño a ponérselo él solo antes de salir.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached third-person reflexive dative se and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: The son is the learner of enseñar a and the understood wearer of poner. Se marks his self-directed dressing, while lo represents abrigo; se does not replace a recipient le here.
register: Neutral Mexican parent-child context.
note: Abrigo = coat; él solo = by himself. The parent teaches, and the son puts the coat on himself.

sentence: Mi hermana quiere su propia comida para mañana; yo la ayudo a preparársela y después cocino la mía.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached third-person reflexive beneficiary se and feminine singular direct-object la
grammar: The sister receives help and is the understood person preparing her own meal. Se marks her self-beneficiary role; attached la represents comida. The separate preverbal la is the personal direct object of ayudo.
register: Familiar Mexican household conversation.
note: Su propia comida = her own food; la mía = mine, referring to the speaker's separate meal.

sentence: Los recibos estaban mezclados y no encontraba el del gas; después de comer me dediqué a ordenarlos por fecha hasta encontrarlo.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached masculine plural direct-object los
grammar: Ordenar los recibos por fecha means arranging the receipts according to their dates. Los represents recibos and attaches to ordenar after dedicarse a.
register: Neutral Mexican household narrative.
note: Me dediqué a = I devoted myself to; mezclados = mixed together; por fecha = by date.

sentence: Ana y yo no entendíamos el problema del agua; el vecino se esforzó por explicárnoslo con un dibujo y al final comprendimos la causa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite pronominal verb phrase with governed preposition por
grammar: Esforzarse por + infinitive expresses deliberate effort toward an action. In the selected explicárnoslo, nos identifies Ana and the speaker as listeners and lo represents the water problem.
register: Neutral Mexican neighborhood narrative.
note: Vecino = neighbor; dibujo = drawing; comprendimos = we understood.

sentence: El proyector es de Luis; pensé en pedírselo, pero él lo necesita toda la semana y renuncié a pedírselo prestado.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite verb phrase with governed preposition a
grammar: Renunciar a + infinitive expresses forgoing a proposed action. The speaker both gives up the idea and is the understood person who would ask Luis for the loan.
register: Neutral Mexican explanation of a forgone request.
note: Proyector = projector. In pedírselo prestado, se identifies Luis as the owner being asked and lo represents the projector.

sentence: El último chocolate era de Luis; podía compartirlo conmigo, pero optó por guardárselo y comerlo después.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite verb phrase with governed preposition por
grammar: Optar por + infinitive expresses choosing an action. Luis chooses keeping the chocolate for himself over the available alternative of sharing it.
register: Neutral Mexican account of an everyday choice.
note: Guardárselo = keep it for himself; compartirlo conmigo = share it with me. Luis owns the chocolate and plans to eat it later.

sentence: Ana, mi chamarra sigue en tu casa y mañana salgo temprano; acuérdate de devolvérmela esta noche.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached first-person singular return-recipient me and feminine singular direct-object la
grammar: Acordarse de + infinitive concerns remembering to perform one's own pending action. Me and la remain attached to devolver inside that complement.
register: Familiar Mexican reminder.
note: Ana must remember the action; the speaker receives their jacket back. Acuérdate is the affirmative tú command of acordarse.

sentence: El mensaje era para mis padres; me olvidé de mandárselo antes de salir y ahora ellos todavía no saben a qué hora llego.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached replacement indirect-object se and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Olvidarse de + infinitive reports forgetting to perform an action. Main me belongs to olvidarse; attached se identifies the parents as recipients and lo represents mensaje.
register: Neutral Mexican acknowledgment of an omission.
note: The speaker explicitly reports their own forgotten sending action. This is not an accidental se construction.

sentence: Luis, no entiendo por qué debemos cambiar la fecha de la fiesta; empieza a explicármelo por esa parte y después vemos los demás detalles.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached first-person singular listener me and neuter direct-object lo
grammar: With affirmative auxiliary command empieza a, the ordinary selected placement attaches the complete block to the final infinitive. Lo represents the stated why issue.
register: Familiar Mexican request for an explanation.
note: Empieza is the affirmative tú command of empezar. Por esa parte identifies the reason for changing the party date as the requested starting point.

sentence: Ana, ya vimos tus fotos del viaje, pero Luis y yo no distinguimos las dos rutas; vuelve a mostrárnoslas en el mapa, por favor.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached first-person plural viewer nos and feminine plural direct-object las
grammar: Mostrar means making something visible to viewers. Nos identifies Luis and the speaker; las represents the two routes. After vuelve a, the selected block attaches to the final infinitive.
register: Familiar Mexican request.
note: No distinguimos = we cannot tell apart here. Vuelve a requests another showing rather than a return to a place.

sentence: La abuela ya escribió el relato de su infancia para sus nietos, pero sigue contándoselo de viva voz cada domingo porque ellos disfrutan sus comentarios.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution specifying spoken delivery
grammar: De viva voz identifies spoken delivery, contrasted here with the written account. It does not specify whether the speaker follows a script. In contándoselo, se identifies the grandchildren and lo represents relato.
register: Neutral Mexican family narrative.
note: Relato = account; nietos = grandchildren; comentarios = comments. Sigue contándoselo expresses continued telling across Sundays.

sentence: Clara me prestó estas dos sillas para la fiesta; ahora estoy devolviéndoselas en su casa y ella revisa si están completas.
part_of_speech: gerund verb with attached replacement indirect-object se and feminine plural direct-object las
grammar: The -er verb devolver preserves o in devolviendo despite present devuelvo. This contrasts with the o-to-u gerund durmiendo of the -ir verb dormir. Attached se identifies Clara and las represents the chairs; the complete form requires an accent.
register: Neutral Mexican update during a return.
note: Revisa si están completas = checks whether the chairs have all their parts. The indirect question presents the condition being checked.

sentence: Mi gato no aparece; desde ayer ando buscándolo de un lado a otro: ya pregunté en la tienda, en el parque y con los vecinos.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution of distributed movement
grammar: De un lado a otro describes searching across different places. The listed stops establish the distribution; andar + gerund supplies the already learned extended-activity frame.
register: Conversational Mexican account of a search.
note: No aparece = has not turned up; buscándolo = looking for him, referring to the male cat.

sentence: El trámite tiene tres partes; voy explicándoselo paso a paso a mi papá: primero la solicitud, luego el pago y al final la entrega.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution of ordered procedural explanation
grammar: Paso a paso specifies an ordered explanation through successive procedural steps. It adds organization to the gradual development already expressed by voy explicándoselo.
register: Neutral Mexican family assistance.
note: Trámite = administrative procedure; solicitud = application; se identifies the father and lo represents the procedure.

sentence: La encargada viene advirtiéndonoslo a Ana y a mí desde enero: el edificio cerrará en noviembre; hoy volvió a recordarnos el cierre.
part_of_speech: stem-changing gerund verb with attached first-person plural audience nos and neuter direct-object lo
grammar: Advertir means communicating a warning here and changes e to i in advirtiendo. Nos identifies Ana and the speaker; lo represents the announced closure.
register: Neutral Mexican account of repeated warnings.
note: Viene + gerund presents warnings repeated from January up to now. Encargada = woman in charge; cierre = closure.

sentence: Ana pintaba un retrato en el taller; los demás visitantes se fueron, pero su amigo Pablo se quedó mirándola hasta que ella terminó.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite pronominal verb governing a gerund
grammar: Quedarse + gerund presents remaining engaged in an activity. Pablo stays watching, while la in mirándola identifies Ana as the person watched.
register: Neutral Mexican narrative about friends.
note: Retrato = portrait; taller = studio here; visitantes = visitors. Ana remains painting while the other visitors leave.

sentence: La mamá continúa repitiéndoselo a Diego: el piso está mojado; él no le hace caso y sigue corriendo por el pasillo.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verbal locution
grammar: Hacer caso a alguien means heeding that person's words. No le hace caso denies that Diego follows his mother's warning; visible le identifies the mother.
register: Ordinary Mexican family narrative.
note: Repitiéndoselo = repeating it to him; se identifies Diego and lo represents the wet-floor warning.

sentence: Yo no quería preocupar a mi hermana con la pérdida de mi empleo; dudé toda la tarde, pero terminé diciéndoselo durante la cena.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite resultative auxiliary governing a gerund
grammar: Terminar + gerund introduces the action eventually reached after hesitation. Terminé diciéndoselo means the speaker ended up telling the sister; it does not mean merely finishing an already ongoing telling.
register: Neutral Mexican personal narrative.
note: Pérdida de mi empleo = loss of my job; dudé = hesitated. Se identifies the sister and lo represents the job loss.

sentence: La señora Vega no tiene teléfono; el aviso es para ella y espero que Luis se lo pueda hacer llegar por medio de la hija de la señora.
part_of_speech: causative verbal locution in the infinitive
grammar: Hacer llegar algo a alguien means arranging for it to reach that person. The intact se lo block precedes pueda; se identifies Mrs. Vega and lo represents aviso.
register: Neutral Mexican coordination using respectful reference.
note: Por medio de = through an intermediary. Mrs. Vega's daughter is the intermediary, and Mrs. Vega is the final recipient.

sentence: Luis dice que quiere decírnoslo cara a cara a Ana y a mí: él perdió el dinero de la renta y quiere explicar qué pasó.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution specifying direct personal interaction
grammar: Cara a cara specifies meeting the listeners directly for the disclosure. Quiere decírnoslo and nos lo quiere decir both permit the same listener-and-content relation.
register: Neutral Mexican report of a sensitive personal conversation.
note: Nos identifies Ana and the speaker; lo represents Luis's loss of the rent money.

sentence: La bicicleta es de Ana; intenté pedírsela prestada para ir al mercado, pero ella la necesitaba y me dijo que no.
part_of_speech: feminine singular predicative participial adjective agreeing with the requested object
grammar: In pedir una bicicleta prestada, prestada agrees with the feminine item. That agreement remains when bicicleta is represented by attached la in pedírsela.
register: Neutral Mexican account of an unsuccessful borrowing request.
note: Se identifies Ana as the owner asked for the loan. Intenté reports an attempt, and Ana's refusal makes the result explicit.

sentence: El informe era para la directora; la oficina estaba cerrada, pero la encontré en el patio y logré entregárselo.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite achievement verb governing an infinitive
grammar: Lograr + infinitive presents successful achievement. The closed office is the obstacle, and finding the director allows the actual handover.
register: Neutral Mexican work narrative.
note: Informe = report; la encontré refers to finding the director. In entregárselo, se identifies her and lo represents the report.

sentence: Los libros son de mi vecino; traté de devolvérselos esta mañana, pero no estaba en casa y todavía los tengo yo.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite verb phrase with governed preposition de
grammar: Tratar de + infinitive expresses attempting an action. Unlike intentar with a bare infinitive, this frame includes de; the outcome shows that the return was not completed.
register: Neutral Mexican explanation about borrowed books.
note: Devolvérselos = return the books to the neighbor; se identifies their owner and los represents libros.

sentence: El juguete era de Tomás; su primo intentó quitárselo a la fuerza, pero la abuela intervino y Tomás lo conservó.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution of coercive manner
grammar: A la fuerza specifies taking against the holder's resistance. In quitárselo, se identifies Tomás as the holder from whom the toy would be removed, not a recipient.
register: Neutral Mexican family narrative.
note: Intervino = intervened; conservó = kept possession of. The attempted taking does not succeed.

sentence: Rosa fue a denunciar el robo de su bicicleta; según una testigo, un desconocido logró robársela mientras Rosa pagaba en la tienda.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with a reported offense as direct object
grammar: Denunciar el robo means reporting the theft to the authorities. In the attributed account, se in robársela identifies Rosa as the affected owner and la represents her bicycle.
register: Neutral Mexican report of an incident.
note: Robo = theft; desconocido = unknown person. Según una testigo attributes the theft account to a witness.

sentence: El dibujo era de Julia y lo sostenía entre las manos; su hermano intentó arrebatárselo de un tirón, pero ella lo guardó antes en su carpeta.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached replacement affected-source se and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Arrebatar means taking abruptly and forcefully from a holder. Se identifies Julia as that holder and lo represents dibujo; her brother is the actor attempting the taking.
register: Neutral Mexican family narrative.
note: De un tirón = with one sudden pull; carpeta = folder. Julia puts the drawing away before her brother succeeds.

sentence: Ese escritorio pertenece a don Raúl y él lo vende; voy a comprárselo para mi casa y el dinero será para él.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached replacement seller/source se and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Se identifies don Raúl as the seller from whom the desk is bought. The buyer is the speaker, and the desk is for the speaker's home; se is not a self-beneficiary.
register: Neutral Mexican purchase conversation with respectful reference to the seller.
note: Escritorio = desk; pertenece a = belongs to. Don Raúl receives the purchase money.

sentence: Mi sobrina necesita este escritorio para estudiar; voy a comprárselo como regalo en la tienda de muebles, y ella no tendrá que pagar nada.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached replacement third-party beneficiary se and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Se identifies the niece as the beneficiary receiving the purchased gift. The furniture store is the seller; the niece does not receive the purchase money.
register: Neutral Mexican family gift planning.
note: Sobrina = niece; tienda de muebles = furniture store. The speaker buys and pays, and the niece receives the desk.

sentence: Mi sobrino no tiene dinero para el boleto de camión; voy a pagárselo yo como regalo y la empresa de autobuses recibirá el pago.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached replacement beneficiary se and masculine singular expense-object lo
grammar: Se identifies the nephew whose ticket expense the speaker covers. Lo represents boleto; the bus company receives the money, so the beneficiary and payment recipient are distinct.
register: Neutral Mexican family offer.
note: Sobrino = nephew; empresa de autobuses = bus company; recibirá = will receive.

sentence: Marta necesita una silla plegable para su fiesta; voy a conseguírsela con mi vecino, que tiene una y acepta prestarla.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb with attached replacement beneficiary se and feminine singular direct-object la
grammar: Se identifies Marta as the person for whom the chair is obtained. The neighbor supplies the borrowed chair, and the speaker arranges it; se is not the speaker acquiring something for themself.
register: Neutral Mexican coordination for a social event.
note: Con mi vecino identifies the person through whom the speaker will obtain the chair. The neighbor accepts lending it.

sentence: El radio de don Ernesto no enciende; yo sé reparar ese modelo y voy a reparárselo gratis, porque él me ayudó con la mudanza.
part_of_speech: adverb specifying absence of a charge
grammar: Gratis states that the repair carries no charge. The speaker performs the repair, and don Ernesto owns the radio and benefits from the service.
register: Neutral Mexican offer with respectful reference.
note: No enciende = does not turn on; modelo = model. In reparárselo, se identifies don Ernesto as owner-beneficiary and lo represents radio.

sentence: Ana, te confié mi reloj y tú lo tienes en la mano; puedes rompérmelo si lo dejas caer, así que guárdalo en su caja.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite transitive verb with a possession object and entrusted-person indirect complement
grammar: Confiar algo a alguien means placing a possession in that person's care here. The entrusted watch remains the speaker's property; in rompérmelo, me identifies that affected owner and Ana is the possible damaging actor.
register: Familiar Mexican warning about an entrusted possession.
note: Dejar caer = drop; así que = so; guárdalo = put it away, addressed to Ana.

sentence: Ana, esto es algo personal mío: voy a cambiar de trabajo; quiero contártelo en confianza y te pido que no lo comentes con nadie.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution specifying confidential communication
grammar: En confianza frames the disclosure as private communication based on trust. The explicit request not to discuss it with anyone establishes the intended confidentiality.
register: Familiar Mexican conversation about personal news.
note: Contártelo = tell you about it; te identifies Ana and lo represents the speaker's planned job change.

sentence: Señor Ortiz, ya revisé el contrato que usted tiene; envíemelo por correo hoy para guardar mi copia.
part_of_speech: affirmative usted imperative with attached speaker-recipient me and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Envíemelo requests action from one respectfully addressed person. Me identifies the speaker receiving the contract, and lo represents contrato. Accented í preserves the stress and hiatus of envíe.
register: Respectful singular request in Mexican Spanish.
note: Contrato = contract; revisé = reviewed. The requested copy is for the speaker.

sentence: Señora, mi hermana dejó una bolsa con usted y ahora voy por ella; descríbamela por teléfono para reconocerla al llegar.
part_of_speech: affirmative usted imperative with attached listener me and feminine singular direct-object la
grammar: Describir identifies an object's characteristics in words. La represents bolsa, the thing described; me identifies the person hearing the description.
register: Respectful singular telephone request.
note: Voy por ella = I am going to collect it; reconocerla = recognize the bag.

sentence: Señor Torres, Ana y Luis no distinguen los detalles de estos dibujos desde sus asientos; muéstreselos de cerca antes de guardarlos.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution specifying viewing proximity
grammar: De cerca specifies a short viewing distance. In the visible muéstreselos, usted is the person showing the drawings, se identifies Ana and Luis, and los represents dibujos.
register: Respectful singular request in Mexican Spanish.
note: No distinguen los detalles = cannot make out the details; asientos = seats.

sentence: Señora Pérez, estos documentos son para la inscripción; reténgalos aquí mientras saco las copias y luego me los llevo.
part_of_speech: irregular affirmative usted imperative with attached masculine plural direct-object los
grammar: Retener here means holding documents temporarily during a procedure. Retenga uses irregular reteng-, and los represents documentos; the speaker explicitly plans to take them afterward.
register: Respectful singular coordination during registration.
note: Inscripción = registration; saco las copias = I make the copies.

sentence: Ana y Pablo, ese mapa es de Clara y mío; devuélvannoslo antes de salir, porque mañana Clara y yo viajamos juntos.
part_of_speech: affirmative ustedes imperative with attached first-person plural return-recipient nos and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Ana and Pablo are the two addressed returners. Nos identifies Clara and the speaker as recipients, and lo represents mapa. The final n of devuelvan remains before nos, producing nn.
register: Ordinary Mexican plural request.
note: The owners and return recipients are Clara and the speaker, independently of the two people addressed.

sentence: Ana y Pablo, don Ernesto no entendió su explicación del nuevo horario; explíquenselo en otras palabras, con un ejemplo.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution requesting reformulation
grammar: En otras palabras requests different wording for the same content after an explanation was not understood. In explíquenselo, Ana and Pablo are the actors, se identifies don Ernesto, and lo represents horario.
register: Ordinary Mexican plural instruction with respectful reference to don Ernesto.
note: Su explicación refers to the explanation Ana and Pablo gave.

sentence: Ana y Pablo, yo tengo la llave del salón; pídanmela sin intermediarios, porque necesito saber quién la tiene después.
part_of_speech: prepositional phrase specifying direct dealings
grammar: Sin intermediarios asks the addressees to deal directly with the key holder. In pídanmela, me identifies the speaker as the person asked for the key, and la represents llave.
register: Ordinary Mexican plural instruction.
note: An intermediario acts between the people involved; the speaker wants to track who takes the key.

sentence: Ana y Pablo, Clara necesita una silla para la cena de hoy; esa es de ustedes y hoy no la usan, así que ofrézcansela en préstamo solo hasta mañana.
part_of_speech: prepositional locution specifying temporary use without transfer of ownership
grammar: En préstamo makes the offer temporary: Ana and Pablo keep ownership of the chair. In ofrézcansela, se identifies Clara and la represents silla.
register: Ordinary Mexican coordination among friends.
note: Solo hasta mañana supplies the loan's endpoint; the chair is not offered as a gift.

sentence: Señor Ruiz, mi hermana y yo estamos aquí en la oficina y nuestra carpeta quedó en su carro; tráiganosla, por favor.
part_of_speech: affirmative usted imperative with attached first-person plural recipient nos and feminine singular direct-object la
grammar: Traiga addresses one person. Nos identifies the speaker and sister waiting at the destination; la represents carpeta. Its single n begins nos and does not make the command plural.
register: Respectful singular request in Mexican Spanish.
note: Carpeta = folder; quedó en su carro = was left in your car.

sentence: Ana y Pablo, su abuela no puede leer sin sus lentes y hoy no los encuentra; este mensaje es de su tía, así que léanselo en voz alta.
part_of_speech: affirmative ustedes imperative with attached replacement listener se and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Leer algo a alguien means reading content aloud to a listener here. Lean addresses Ana and Pablo; se identifies their grandmother and lo represents mensaje. The accent preserves the stress of lean.
register: Ordinary Mexican family request.
note: Lentes = eyeglasses; tía = aunt; en voz alta = aloud.

sentence: Ana, tú y yo necesitamos un diccionario cada uno; estos dos cuestan menos que los otros, así que comprémonoslos para estudiar en casa.
part_of_speech: first-person plural affirmative hortative with attached self-beneficiary nos and masculine plural direct-object los
grammar: The suggestion includes the speaker and Ana as both buyers and beneficiaries. Los represents the two dictionaries. Compremos loses its final s before nos.
register: Familiar Mexican suggestion to a study partner.
note: Diccionario = dictionary. Each person needs one, and the selected pair costs less.

sentence: Luis, tú y yo vamos a pintar la sala y tenemos cuatro brochas; repartámonoslas: dos para ti y dos para mí.
part_of_speech: first-person plural affirmative hortative with attached reciprocal-allocation nos and feminine plural direct-object las
grammar: Repartir means allocating portions of a set. Nos keeps the allocation within the speaker–Luis pair; las represents the four brushes. Final s is dropped before nos.
register: Familiar Mexican coordination of a shared household task.
note: Brochas = paintbrushes. The following two allocations explicitly identify both beneficiaries.

sentence: Ana, tú y yo estudiamos dos horas sin parar y ya estamos cansados; démonos un descanso de diez minutos antes de continuar.
part_of_speech: first-person plural affirmative hortative with attached self-beneficiary nos
grammar: Démonos proposes granting a break to the same speaker-inclusive group that has been studying. Demos loses final s before nos, and the attached form requires an accent.
register: Familiar Mexican suggestion between study partners.
note: Un descanso de diez minutos = a ten-minute break; continuar = continue.

sentence: Ana, tú tienes el libro de historia que necesito y yo tengo el de ciencias que te falta; prestémonos los libros hasta el viernes.
part_of_speech: first-person plural affirmative hortative with attached reciprocal indirect-object nos
grammar: Nos is reciprocal: Ana lends her book to the speaker, and the speaker lends the other book to Ana. It does not identify a single outside loan recipient.
register: Familiar Mexican suggestion between classmates.
note: Historia = history; ciencias = science. The loans last through Friday.

sentence: Ana, las dos tenemos puestas las chamarras con la etiqueta por fuera; pongámonoslas al derecho antes de salir, con la etiqueta hacia dentro.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution specifying garment orientation
grammar: Al derecho specifies the intended orientation when putting the jackets on: their labels face inward. In pongámonoslas, the speaker and Ana are both actors and wearers, and las represents chamarras.
register: Familiar Mexican suggestion between two women.
note: Etiqueta = label; hacia dentro = toward the inside.

sentence: Luis, tú y yo llevamos un sombrero cada uno; aquí adentro hace calor, así que quitémonoslo.
part_of_speech: first-person plural affirmative hortative with attached reflexive wearer nos and distributive masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Lo refers distributively to each participant's own sombrero, not to one hat shared between two heads. Nos marks the two wearers removing their own hats.
register: Familiar Mexican suggestion indoors.
note: Sombrero = hat; aquí adentro = in here. Cada uno establishes one hat per wearer.

sentence: Ana, esta bolsa es de los dos y ya terminó la comida en el parque; llevémonosla sin falta, porque ayer olvidamos otra aquí.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution emphasizing that an intended action must not be omitted
grammar: Sin falta reinforces the proposal as something the participants must make sure to do. In llevémonosla, nos belongs to llevarse and la represents their shared bag.
register: Familiar Mexican reminder after an outdoor meal.
note: Olvidamos otra aquí = we left another bag here by forgetting it.

sentence: Ana, quedan dos pedazos de pastel y Rosa y Luis van a llegar después de la cena; guardémoselos en el refrigerador.
part_of_speech: first-person plural affirmative hortative with attached replacement beneficiary se and masculine plural direct-object los
grammar: The speaker and Ana reserve the cake for Rosa and Luis. Se identifies those outside beneficiaries, and los represents pedazos. The final s of guardemos and initial s of se are written as a single s in guardémoselos.
register: Familiar Mexican coordination between hosts.
note: Refrigerador = refrigerator. The absent guests will arrive after dinner.

sentence: Ana, este libro es de los dos y ya lo leímos; Mateo nos ayudó con la mudanza, así que démoselo en señal de agradecimiento.
part_of_speech: prepositional phrase specifying a gift's symbolic social meaning
grammar: En señal de agradecimiento presents the gift as an expression of thanks for Mateo's help. In démoselo, the two owners propose giving the book to Mateo; se identifies him and lo represents libro.
register: Familiar Mexican gift planning.
note: Agradecimiento = gratitude; en señal de introduces what an action symbolically expresses.

sentence: Ana, tú y yo rompimos el vaso de Julia y ella todavía no lo sabe; digámoselo sin rodeos antes de que se entere por otra persona.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution specifying direct, unambiguous communication
grammar: Sin rodeos requests direct wording rather than an evasive approach. The visible digámoselo proposes telling Julia about the breaking incident; lo represents that fact.
register: Familiar Mexican discussion of taking responsibility.
note: Antes de que se entere por otra persona = before she finds out from someone else.

sentence: Ana, tú y yo ya firmamos las cartas para Rosa y Clara; enviémoselas con acuse de recibo, porque necesitamos una prueba de la entrega.
part_of_speech: prepositional phrase specifying a requested delivery acknowledgment
grammar: Con acuse de recibo requests acknowledgment that the letters reached their recipients. In enviémoselas, the speaker and Ana act jointly, se identifies Rosa and Clara, and las represents cartas.
register: Mexican administrative correspondence.
note: Acuse de recibo = acknowledgment of receipt; prueba de la entrega = proof of delivery.

sentence: Ana, tú y yo vimos cómo empezó la discusión; contémoslo de principio a fin, porque Julia solo conoce la última parte.
part_of_speech: first-person plural affirmative hortative with attached neuter direct-object lo
grammar: Contar means recounting an event here, rather than counting objects. Lo represents the argument's development. Contemos keeps o without the diphthong of cuento and retains s before lo.
register: Familiar Mexican proposal for a complete account.
note: Discusión = argument; de principio a fin = from beginning to end.

sentence: Ana, tú y yo no estamos de acuerdo sobre la hora de salida; este desacuerdo retrasa el viaje, así que resolvámoslo comparando nuestros horarios.
part_of_speech: first-person plural affirmative hortative with attached masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: Resolver un desacuerdo means settling a disagreement between people. The command commits the speaker and Ana to a joint action; lo represents desacuerdo.
register: Familiar Mexican discussion between travel companions.
note: Desacuerdo = disagreement; comparando nuestros horarios = by comparing our schedules.

sentence: Ana, nuestra mesa no cabe en la cocina; cambiémosla por la de repuesto, que es plegable y sí cabe.
part_of_speech: adjectival prepositional locution identifying an item kept as a replacement
grammar: De repuesto identifies a table kept available to replace another. La de repuesto omits the recoverable noun mesa; the visible cambiémosla proposes replacing their unsuitable current table.
register: Familiar Mexican household suggestion.
note: Plegable = folding; sí cabe explicitly confirms that the spare table fits.

sentence: Ana, don Raúl tiene el mapa de la ruta que necesitamos para nuestro viaje; pidámoselo prestado y se lo devolvemos mañana.
part_of_speech: first-person plural affirmative hortative with attached replacement person-asked se and masculine singular direct-object lo
grammar: The speaker and Ana make the request; don Raúl is the source being asked. Lo represents mapa. Pidamos retains the raised i in this first-plural form of pedir.
register: Familiar Mexican suggestion with respectful reference to the lender.
note: Prestado makes this a loan; se lo devolvemos mañana states the planned return.

sentence: Ana, tú y yo acordamos empezar el ensayo a las seis; no lo adelantemos a las cinco, porque Luis sale del trabajo a las cinco y media.
part_of_speech: first-person plural negative hortative verb with visible preverbal direct-object lo
grammar: No lo adelantemos proposes keeping the jointly agreed start time. In a negative inclusive command, the object clitic precedes the verb rather than attaching.
register: Familiar Mexican coordination among rehearsal participants.
note: Ensayo = rehearsal; acordamos = agreed. Moving it to five would exclude Luis at the start.

sentence: Ana, tú y yo reservamos este lugar para vender nuestras artesanías en la feria; Pedro pidió usarlo él solo, pero no se lo cedamos en exclusiva, porque también lo necesitamos.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution restricting granted use to one party
grammar: En exclusiva would give Pedro sole use of the reserved place, excluding the two holders. In no se lo cedamos, se identifies Pedro and lo represents lugar.
register: Familiar Mexican coordination between fair participants.
note: Artesanías = handicrafts; feria = fair; él solo makes the requested exclusivity explicit.

sentence: Ana, tú y yo no sabemos si el horno funciona después de la reparación; no le prometamos a Julia un pastel para mañana a la ligera.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution describing action without adequate consideration
grammar: A la ligera describes making a commitment without adequately considering whether it can be fulfilled. The oven's unverified condition supplies the reason for the negative proposal.
register: Familiar Mexican planning between would-be bakers.
note: Horno = oven. Julia is the proposed promise recipient.

sentence: Ana, tú y yo necesitamos la respuesta de Luis a nuestra invitación; no se la exijamos en el acto, porque él no recibe su horario de trabajo hasta mañana.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution specifying immediate timing
grammar: En el acto specifies giving the answer immediately, without a waiting period. In no se la exijamos, se identifies Luis as the person pressed and la represents respuesta.
register: Familiar Mexican discussion between joint hosts.
note: Luis receives his work schedule tomorrow; the proposal allows him time to check it.

sentence: Ana, tú y yo preferimos salir a las seis, pero Clara también va en nuestro carro y trabaja hasta las siete; no le impongamos nuestro plan sin darle voz en la decisión.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun with the figurative sense of participation in a decision
grammar: Voz in darle voz en la decisión means an opportunity to participate and have one's views considered. It does not refer to Clara's physical speaking voice.
register: Familiar Mexican discussion of a shared ride.
note: Darle voz = give her a say. Clara is affected by the departure choice because she shares the ride and works until seven.

sentence: El aviso de hoy dice: «Aquí se venden mesas usadas; cada una cuesta quinientos pesos».
part_of_speech: passive se marker with a plural inanimate patient subject
grammar: Passive se leaves the human sellers unnamed. Mesas usadas is the grammatical subject, so venden is plural. This differs from reciprocal people acting on each other and from objects changing through natural causes.
register: Neutral Mexican sales notice.
note: Mesas usadas = used tables; cada una = each table; quinientos pesos = five hundred pesos.

sentence: El aviso aclara: «Se vende solo la mesa de la entrada; las otras son para las clases».
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb in a se passive
grammar: The passive subject is singular la mesa de la entrada, so the verb is vende. The other tables are explicitly excluded from the sale, unlike a notice offering several tables.
register: Neutral posted notice at a community classroom.
note: Aclara = makes clear; solo = only. The table by the entrance is the sole sale item.

sentence: Después de reparar las goteras, ayer se habilitaron los dos cuartos del fondo para recibir a los invitados; ya no entra agua.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Habilitar means making a space fit for its intended use. The completed action affects los dos cuartos, which controls plural habilitaron; the people doing the work remain unnamed.
register: Neutral Mexican household update.
note: Cuartos del fondo = rooms at the back; invitados = guests. The repaired leaks make receiving guests possible.

sentence: Antes, se acondicionaba el salón del barrio con mesas y sillas para las comidas del domingo; ahora cada familia come en su casa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Acondicionar means arranging or equipping a place for a particular use. The imperfect presents the former recurring preparation, and singular salón controls acondicionaba.
register: Neutral Mexican recollection of neighborhood meals.
note: The tables and chairs identify the preparation for shared Sunday meals.

sentence: Mañana se distribuirán los cuadernos donados entre los niños del taller; hay uno para cada niño, así que nadie necesita comprar otro.
part_of_speech: third-person plural simple future indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Distribuir means allocating supplies across recipients. Los cuadernos is the plural passive subject, and entre los niños identifies the receiving group.
register: Neutral Mexican announcement for a children's workshop.
note: Cuadernos donados = donated notebooks. One notebook is available for each child.

sentence: El aviso de la feria de intercambio del barrio dice: «No se admiten muebles grandes ni aparatos descompuestos; no hay espacio para guardarlos».
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a negative se passive
grammar: Admitir means accepting items for participation in the exchange event. The coordinated item categories control plural admiten; no excludes both categories.
register: Neutral notice for a fictional neighborhood exchange fair.
note: Muebles grandes = large furniture; aparatos descompuestos = broken appliances or devices; intercambio = exchange.

sentence: En la campaña del barrio, ¿se recogen los libros donados en las casas de los vecinos o hay que llevarlos a la biblioteca?
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in an interrogative se passive
grammar: Recoger here means collecting contributions from their donors' homes. Los libros donados is the plural passive subject; the neighbors are identified as donors at the collection locations, rather than people being picked up.
register: Neutral Mexican inquiry about a neighborhood collection.
note: Campaña = organized campaign; vecinos = neighbors; biblioteca = library.

sentence: Los dibujos que hicieron las niñas se exhiben este fin de semana en el salón del barrio; sus familias pueden entrar gratis.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Exhibir means displaying objects for people to view. The fronted subject is los dibujos, not las niñas; exhiben agrees with the drawings, and se does not describe the girls presenting themselves.
register: Neutral announcement for a fictional community art event.
note: Que hicieron las niñas explicitly identifies the girls as the artists; gratis means without an entrance charge.

sentence: Según el acuerdo del salón del barrio, las sillas prestadas para fiestas se devuelven en buen estado: limpias y con todas sus piezas.
part_of_speech: prepositional collocation specifying an item's condition
grammar: En buen estado specifies the condition required on return. The visible passive devuelven agrees with las sillas; the colon explains the condition rather than introducing another recipient.
register: Neutral description of a fictional community lending arrangement.
note: Acuerdo = agreement; piezas = component parts. The chairs must be clean and complete.

sentence: Para la venta del domingo, se reúnen ropa y libros en el salón del barrio; el dinero de la venta será para comprar mesas nuevas.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive with coordinated inanimate subjects
grammar: Reunir here means collecting materials together. Ropa y libros is the coordinated passive subject and takes plural reúnen. This differs from people meeting through reunirse.
register: Neutral Mexican explanation of a community fundraiser.
note: Ropa = clothing; venta = sale. The proceeds will fund new tables.

sentence: El aviso del taller dice: «Las cajas se etiquetan con su contenido antes de guardarlas; así no hace falta abrirlas para buscar material».
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Etiquetar means putting identifying information on an item. Cajas controls plural etiquetan; the people applying the labels remain unnamed.
register: Neutral notice in a fictional community workshop.
note: Cajas = boxes; contenido = contents. The labels identify what is inside each box.

sentence: Los vasos vendidos se embalan en cajas con papel para protegerlos durante el viaje.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Embalar means packing goods for transport, here with protective paper. Vasos vendidos is the plural subject receiving the packing action.
register: Neutral explanation of preparations after a community sale.
note: Vendidos = sold; protegerlos = protect the glasses. The boxes and paper provide the transport packing.

sentence: Los libros donados se clasifican en dos grupos, infantiles y para adultos; así las familias encuentran más rápido algo para leer.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Clasificar means organizing items by category. En introduces the two categories, and libros donados controls plural clasifican.
register: Neutral explanation at a community book collection.
note: Grupos = groups or categories. The categories distinguish children's books from books intended for adults.

sentence: En nuestro club de lectura se registran las devoluciones de libros en un cuaderno; una marca junto al título indica la fecha.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Registrar means entering information into a record. Devoluciones is the plural passive subject; the notebook is where the returns are recorded.
register: Neutral description of a fictional reading club's procedure.
note: Devoluciones = returns; marca = mark; título = book title; indica = shows or specifies.

sentence: Los formularios completos del club contienen datos personales y se archivan bajo llave; solo la encargada tiene la llave del cajón.
part_of_speech: fixed prepositional expression describing secure storage
grammar: Bajo llave specifies storage in a locked place. Here the documents are filed in a locked drawer, and only the woman in charge has its key.
register: Neutral explanation of a fictional club's handling of personal information.
note: Formularios completos = completed forms; datos personales = personal information; encargada = woman in charge; cajón = drawer.

sentence: En casa se conservan las tazas de mi abuela por su valor familiar; ya no las usamos, pero tampoco queremos tirarlas.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Conservar here means retaining possessions despite no longer using them. The family value supplies the reason, and tazas controls plural conservan.
register: Neutral household explanation.
note: Valor familiar = significance to the family; tirarlas = throw the cups away.

sentence: Los platos rotos del salón se desechan porque ya no sirven; los platos completos se lavan para usarlos otra vez.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Desechar means deliberately discarding items judged unusable. It does not describe accidentally losing them. Platos rotos controls plural desechan.
register: Neutral explanation of sorting household supplies in a community hall.
note: Rotos = broken; ya no sirven = they are no longer usable; completos = intact here.

sentence: El aviso de la campaña del barrio dice: «Las hojas usadas se reciclan para hacer papel nuevo; esta caja es solo para papel».
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Reciclar here means recovering material to make new paper. Hojas usadas is the plural passive subject.
register: Original notice for a fictional neighborhood collection campaign.
note: Hojas usadas = used sheets of paper. The stated purpose distinguishes material recycling from simply using an object again.

sentence: En el salón, los frascos vacíos de café se reutilizan para guardar lápices; así no compramos otros recipientes.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Reutilizar means using the same objects again, here for a different purpose. The jars become pencil containers rather than material for manufacturing new jars.
register: Neutral explanation of a community hall's everyday practice.
note: Frascos vacíos de café = empty coffee jars; recipientes = containers.

sentence: Ayer no quedó jabón ni papel en el baño compartido; hoy se reponen ambos productos con las compras de la semana.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Reponer here means replenishing exhausted supplies, rather than replacing someone's damaged possession. Ambos productos refers to the soap and toilet paper and controls plural reponen.
register: Neutral update about shared household supplies.
note: Baño compartido = shared bathroom; papel here means toilet paper; compras de la semana = the week's purchased supplies.

sentence: Con las donaciones de las familias se abastecen los dos comedores del barrio; hay arroz y frijoles para toda la semana.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Abastecer means supplying a place with needed resources. Los dos comedores is the receiving passive subject; the families' donations provide the food.
register: Neutral description of a fictional community food arrangement.
note: Donaciones = donations; comedores del barrio = neighborhood dining facilities.

sentence: Antes de pagar el pedido, se verifican la dirección de entrega y el precio con el vendedor; el paquete aún está en la tienda.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Verificar means checking specified information. The coordinated subjects dirección de entrega and precio require plural verifican; checking them does not itself guarantee the later delivery.
register: Neutral description of a purchase check.
