note: Pedido = order; dirección de entrega = delivery address; vendedor = seller; aún = still here.

sentence: El registro del club decía «doce libros recibidos», pero solo llegaron diez; hoy se rectifica esa cantidad.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Rectificar here means correcting an erroneous written entry. Esa cantidad refers to the recorded twelve, contradicted by the actual delivery of ten.
register: Neutral correction of a fictional club's record.
note: Registro = written record; libros recibidos = books received. The error concerns the recorded quantity.

sentence: En el grupo de vecinos se difunde un aviso con propuestas para la feria; compartirlo no significa apoyar todas esas ideas.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Difundir means spreading information among people. The singular notice is circulated; its circulation does not imply agreement with its proposals.
register: Neutral explanation in a neighborhood discussion group.
note: Propuestas = proposed ideas; apoyar = support or endorse. Compartirlo refers to sharing the notice.

sentence: Según el acuerdo de nuestro club, mañana se publicará el horario de lectura en la página del club; hasta hoy solo existe un borrador.
part_of_speech: third-person singular simple future indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Publicar means making the club's schedule publicly available. Horario controls singular publicará, and mañana places the release in the future.
register: Neutral announcement about a fictional reading club.
note: Página del club = the club's web page; existe = exists. The current version is still a draft.

sentence: La solicitud de préstamo del salón se tramita en la oficina del club; recibirla inicia el proceso, pero no significa aprobarla.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Tramitar means handling a request through its procedure. Solicitud is the singular passive subject; receiving and processing it do not amount to approval.
register: Neutral administrative wording for a fictional club arrangement.
note: Solicitud de préstamo del salón = request to borrow the hall; inicia el proceso = starts the process; aprobarla = approve the request.

sentence: Después de la discusión, el plan de la comida del club se aprueba por mayoría: ocho votos a favor y dos en contra.
part_of_speech: prepositional collocation specifying the basis of approval
grammar: Por mayoría means that more votes support the plan than oppose it. The visible approval follows discussion and a vote; discussion alone is not approval.
register: Neutral report of a fictional club decision.
note: Votos a favor = votes for; votos en contra = votes against. Eight supporting votes exceed two opposing votes.

sentence: Para la reunión del club se rechazan dos sedes por inviables: una está muy lejos y la otra no tiene espacio para veinte personas.
part_of_speech: plural adjective predicated of two proposed meeting venues
grammar: Inviables evaluates both proposed venues as impractical for this meeting. Por introduces that reason for rejecting them; distance and insufficient space supply the evidence.
register: Neutral explanation of a fictional club's choice.
note: Sedes = proposed meeting venues; se rechazan = are rejected. Inviable concerns practical feasibility here.

sentence: En la colecta de nuestro club se aceptan donativos en especie: hacen falta cuadernos y lápices, y no vamos a recibir dinero.
part_of_speech: fixed prepositional expression specifying the form of a donation
grammar: En especie specifies that donations consist of useful goods. The notebooks and pencils identify the goods, while the final clause explicitly excludes money.
register: Neutral announcement for a fictional club collection.
note: Colecta = organized collection of donations; donativos = donations. Se aceptan means that these donations are accepted.

sentence: El acuerdo de la casa dice: «Se permite practicar guitarra de cuatro a seis; por la noche necesitamos silencio».
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb in a se passive with an infinitival activity subject
grammar: Practicar guitarra names the permitted activity and functions as the passive subject. That infinitival activity takes singular permite; no person is expressed as a direct object.
register: Neutral wording of a fictional household agreement.
note: Practicar guitarra = practice guitar; de cuatro a seis = from four to six; silencio = quiet.

sentence: El aviso de la sala de lectura dice: «Se prohíben las llamadas en altavoz; otras personas vienen aquí a leer en silencio».
part_of_speech: prepositional collocation specifying how telephone calls are conducted
grammar: En altavoz identifies calls whose sound is played aloud. Llamadas is the plural passive subject of prohíben; the people making calls are not the expressed subject.
register: Original posted message in a fictional reading room.
note: Sala de lectura = reading room; se prohíben = are forbidden. The other readers explain the restriction on audible calls.

sentence: El aviso del club dice: «Se necesitan voluntarios para repartir veinte cajas de libros; por ahora solo hay dos personas para la tarea».
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative verb in a se passive with a bare plural human subject
grammar: Voluntarios is a bare plural human passive subject, so necesitan is plural. There is no personal a, and the notice is not addressing volunteers as ustedes.
register: Neutral recruitment notice for a fictional club activity.
note: Voluntarios = volunteers. Twenty boxes and only two available people explain the need for more help.

sentence: El taller del club anuncia: «Se buscan personas con experiencia en reparación de bicicletas; hay diez bicicletas con problemas en los frenos».
part_of_speech: prepositional recruitment collocation modifying the people sought
grammar: Con experiencia identifies a required background in bicycle repair; en introduces the skill area. Personas remains a bare plural passive subject of buscan.
register: Neutral recruitment wording for a fictional club workshop.
note: Reparación = repair work; frenos = brakes. The bicycles' brake problems identify why repair experience is wanted.

sentence: Para la feria del barrio se espera una afluencia de unas doscientas personas; por eso habrá dos mesas para recibir a los visitantes.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun referring to expected event attendance
grammar: Afluencia names the arrival or attendance of people at an event. The singular noun controls espera; doscientas personas measures the expected turnout.
register: Neutral event-planning language.
note: Unas doscientas personas = about two hundred people; visitantes = visitors. The reception tables are preparation for the expected attendance.

sentence: En la feria se prevén filas largas a la entrada; por eso habrá dos mesas para entregar los boletos.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative lexical verb in a se passive
grammar: Prever means anticipating something before it happens. Its plural present form is prevén, with an accent; filas largas controls the plural agreement.
register: Neutral explanation of preparations for a fictional fair.
note: Filas largas = long lines. Two ticket tables are the planned response to the anticipated queues.

sentence: Aquí se camina mucho: la tienda y la parada quedan lejos.
meaning: impersonal marker for people in general
part_of_speech: impersonal se marker with an intransitive verb and no grammatical subject
grammar: Impersonal se leaves the human walkers unspecified and has no grammatical subject. Camina stays singular. La tienda y la parada are subjects only of the separate clause with quedan.
register: Neutral Mexican description of everyday life in a place.
note: Parada = bus stop here. The distant shop and bus stop explain the amount of walking.

sentence: En estos talleres se trabaja a destajo: el pago es por cada pieza terminada, no por las horas de trabajo.
part_of_speech: fixed adverbial expression specifying a payment arrangement for work
grammar: Trabajar a destajo means working for payment based on completed units. It does not merely mean working quickly. Talleres belongs to a location phrase; impersonal trabaja remains singular.
register: Neutral description of a work-payment arrangement.
note: Pago = pay; pieza terminada = completed item. Payment is calculated by output rather than time.

sentence: En este barrio se vive al día: muchas familias gastan en renta y comida todo lo que ganan.
meaning: from day to day, without money left to save
part_of_speech: fixed adverbial expression in vivir al día describing financial circumstances
grammar: Vivir al día here describes using current earnings for immediate needs. It does not express the frequency 'daily'; the explanation says that rent and food consume all earnings.
register: Neutral social description of a neighborhood's financial circumstances.
note: Gastar = spend; ganar dinero = earn money; renta = rent. The assessment concerns limited financial room.

sentence: En la fonda del barrio se come a gusto: hay sillas cómodas y nadie apura a los clientes.
part_of_speech: adverbial expression evaluating the experience of eating
grammar: A gusto evaluates diners' comfort, supported by comfortable chairs and unhurried service. Impersonal se come evaluates eating there generally; no food object is a passive subject.
register: Everyday Mexican evaluation of a modest restaurant.
note: Fonda = modest restaurant serving meals; apurar a alguien = hurry someone; clientes = customers.

sentence: En casa de mis padres se madruga incluso los domingos: a las cinco ya hay café y todos están despiertos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative intransitive lexical verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Madrugar means getting up early. Impersonal madruga stays singular; todos is the subject of the separate clause with están.
register: Neutral description of a household habit.
note: Incluso = even; despiertos = awake. Five o'clock and the prepared coffee make the early routine explicit.

sentence: En el taller del barrio se depende de las donaciones para comprar materiales; no se cobran las clases.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb with a governed de complement in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Depender de identifies the resource on which an activity relies. Donaciones follows governed de and is not a subject, so impersonal depende remains singular.
register: Neutral explanation of a fictional community workshop's funding.
note: The classes have no fees, so donations provide the money for materials. No se cobran las clases = no fees are charged for the classes.

sentence: En la biblioteca del barrio se carece de computadoras; para buscar información solo hay libros impresos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb with a governed de complement in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Carecer de means lacking a resource. Computadoras is introduced by de and does not control agreement; impersonal carece is singular.
register: Moderately formal wording for a resource shortage.
note: Computadoras = computers; información = information; libros impresos = printed books.

sentence: En el salón del barrio se dispone de dos mesas libres; no hace falta traer otras para la clase.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb with a governed de complement in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Disponer de means having resources available for use. It does not mean arranging the tables physically. Dos mesas follows de, so impersonal dispone stays singular.
register: Neutral explanation of available community resources.
note: Mesas libres = tables available for use. Otras refers to additional tables.

sentence: En la campaña de libros se cuenta con el apoyo de las familias: ellas prestan sus carros para recoger las donaciones.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb with a governed con complement in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Contar con means being able to rely on support. Con el apoyo is a prepositional complement; this is neither numerical counting nor narrating a story.
register: Neutral description of a neighborhood book campaign.
note: Apoyo = support. The families provide that support by lending their cars for collecting donations.

sentence: En el chat del club se opina que la cuota es demasiado alta; la tesorera aún no ha explicado los gastos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb introducing a que clause in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Opinar que introduces an opinion attributed generally to discussion in the club chat. The indicative clause reports that opinion's content without making it the narrator's endorsed conclusion.
register: Neutral report of an informal club discussion.
note: Cuota = membership fee here; demasiado alta = too high; tesorera = female treasurer; gastos = expenses.

sentence: En las reuniones del club se discrepa sobre la cuota: hay propuestas distintas, de cincuenta y de ochenta pesos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb with a sobre topic complement in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Discrepar sobre identifies a topic of disagreement. Reuniones is inside a location phrase, and cuota is a topic complement; neither is the subject of singular discrepa.
register: Neutral, moderately formal description of differing opinions.
note: Ochenta = eighty. The competing fee proposals make the disagreement concrete.

sentence: En el círculo de lectura se conversa sobre cada capítulo; nadie tiene que estar de acuerdo con las opiniones de los demás.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative intransitive lexical verb with a sobre topic complement in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Conversar sobre introduces an exchange about a topic. Sobre cada capítulo is not a direct object, and impersonal conversa remains singular.
register: Neutral description of a reading group's conversational practice.
note: Círculo de lectura = reading group; capítulo = chapter; los demás = the others. Agreement is not required for participation in the discussion.

sentence: En nuestro club se participa en la elección del libro con un voto por persona; la coordinadora no decide sola.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical verb with a governed en complement in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Participar en identifies the activity in which people take part. The vote makes their active role clear, rather than merely stating that they attend a meeting.
register: Neutral description of a fictional club's shared choice procedure.
note: Elección = selection by voting here; voto = vote; coordinadora = female coordinator; sola = alone.

sentence: En la campaña de libros se colabora con la biblioteca del barrio: cada familia ayuda a ordenar las donaciones.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative intransitive lexical verb with a con partner complement in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Colaborar con identifies a partner in a shared task. La biblioteca follows con and is not the grammatical subject; the impersonal clause describes people's cooperation.
register: Neutral community-activity description.
note: The families' concrete contribution is helping sort donated books. The library is their partner organization.

sentence: Mis hermanos no llevan maletas; en esta excursión se viaja ligero, con una mochila pequeña por persona.
part_of_speech: adverbial adjective of manner modifying viajar
grammar: Ligero describes traveling with little baggage, not a traveler's body weight. Impersonal viaja is singular; mis hermanos is the subject only of the preceding clause.
register: Neutral practical description of a group outing.
note: Maletas = suitcases; excursión = group outing; mochila = backpack. One small backpack per person defines the light baggage arrangement.

sentence: En la radio del barrio se entrevista a Julia y a Raúl sobre su trabajo como maestros; cada uno habla de su clase.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Entrevistar a alguien sobre algo means interviewing someone about something. Julia and Raúl are personal direct objects introduced by a; they do not make impersonal entrevista plural.
register: Neutral description of a neighborhood radio interview.
note: Radio = radio; maestros = teachers; cada uno = each person individually.

sentence: En el paseo del club se acompaña a don Manuel hasta una banca del parque; él pidió compañía para caminar ese tramo.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Compañía names the presence of someone accompanying Manuel. The first clause uses singular impersonal acompaña with Manuel as its personal direct object.
register: Respectful reference to a club member; don does not establish his age.
note: Don is a respectful title before a man's given name; banca = park bench; pidió compañía = requested companionship.

sentence: En la entrada de la biblioteca se orienta a Ana y a Luis con un mapa: ellos buscan la sala de lectura.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Orientar a alguien can mean helping someone find their way. A Ana y a Luis names two personal direct objects; impersonal orienta stays singular.
register: Neutral visitor-assistance description.
note: Mapa = map; sala de lectura = reading room. The map supplies the means of giving directions.

sentence: En mi casa se recibe a los primos de Ana con un abrazo; vienen de visita y van a cenar con nosotros.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Recibir a alguien con un abrazo means welcoming someone with a hug. Los primos de Ana is a personal direct object and does not control impersonal agreement.
register: Warm, ordinary family description.
note: Primos = cousins; con un abrazo = with a hug; de visita = visiting.

sentence: En el aviso del club se invita a Julia y a sus hermanos a la cena del sábado; cada familia lleva algo para compartir.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Invitar a alguien a un evento distinguishes the invited people from the event. A Julia y a sus hermanos is the personal direct object; a la cena identifies the invitation's destination or occasion.
register: Neutral club invitation.
note: Invitar = invite. Each family brings something to share at the dinner.

sentence: Aquí se atiende a Nora y a Luis, los clientes de hoy, por la mañana; las solicitudes escritas se revisan por la tarde.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Atiende stays singular because Nora and Luis are personal direct objects. In the separate passive clause, solicitudes escritas is the plural subject and controls plural revisan.
register: Neutral explanation of a fictional office's service arrangements.
note: Clientes = customers; solicitudes escritas = written requests; se revisan = are reviewed.

sentence: En el barrio se ayuda a don Félix y a doña Rosa a salir adelante después de perder su casa; cada familia les ofrece un lugar para dormir.
part_of_speech: infinitive verbal expression naming recovery from hardship
grammar: Salir adelante means overcoming hardship or managing to continue. In this selected transitive use of ayudar, Félix and Rosa are personal direct objects; les belongs separately to ofrece and identifies the offer's recipients.
register: Respectful neighborhood account of practical support.
note: Doña is a respectful title before a woman's given name. The offered sleeping places make the help concrete.

sentence: En este club se respeta a Julia y a Ana aunque opinan distinto: nadie las interrumpe.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Respetar a alguien means treating someone with respect. Julia and Ana are personal direct objects, also represented by las in the separate interruption clause; impersonal respeta remains singular.
register: Neutral description of considerate club discussion.
note: Opinan distinto = hold different opinions; interrumpir a alguien = interrupt someone who is speaking.

sentence: En la radio se reconoce a don Emilio por su voz inconfundible; fue nuestro maestro y nadie habla como él.
part_of_speech: singular adjective modifying voz
grammar: Inconfundible describes a voice that is readily distinguished from others. The former teacher is already familiar; reconocer does not mean meeting him for the first time.
register: Neutral social recognition of a former teacher.
note: Voz = voice. Nadie habla como él supplies the reason his voice is unmistakable.

sentence: En el comedor del barrio se valora a Inés y a Raúl por su paciencia al enseñar a cocinar; ellos explican cada paso sin prisa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Valorar a alguien por algo expresses appreciating someone for a specified quality or contribution. The named people are personal direct objects; por introduces the reason for the appreciation.
register: Neutral appreciation of community contributions.
note: Comedor del barrio = neighborhood dining space; al enseñar a cocinar = when teaching cooking; sin prisa = without rushing.

sentence: Los hermanos Luis y Raúl son alumnos nuevos; aquí se les trata con respeto, sin bromas sobre su acento.
part_of_speech: third-person plural clitic with personal direct-object function after impersonal se
grammar: Les represents Luis and Raúl as the people treated, a personal direct-object role. This use of dative-form les after impersonal se is documented in Mexican Spanish; se los trata is also used. Se leaves the human agent unspecified and is not recipient-replacement se.
register: Neutral Mexican-compatible statement about respectful treatment of newcomers.
note: Alumnos = students; tratar con respeto = treat respectfully; bromas sobre su acento = jokes about their accent.

sentence: Julia y Marta son las dos invitadas de hoy; al llegar se las saluda de mano, con un apretón breve y sin abrazos.
part_of_speech: prepositional manner expression modifying saludar
grammar: Saludar de mano specifies greeting with a handshake. Las represents Julia and Marta as direct objects; singular saluda has an unspecified human agent.
register: Ordinary Mexican description of a greeting arrangement.
note: Invitadas = female guests; apretón breve = brief squeeze, here of the hand; abrazos = hugs.

sentence: En recepción se le habla a Nora del horario: «La clase empieza a las ocho».
part_of_speech: third-person singular communication-recipient dative clitic
grammar: Hablar is intransitive here. Le identifies Nora as the person addressed, while del horario introduces the topic. The topic is prepositional, so there is no content direct object that could serve as a passive subject; se is impersonal.
register: Neutral reception-desk explanation.
note: Recepción = reception desk or reception area; horario = schedule; hablar a alguien de algo = speak to someone about something.

sentence: En el patio se puede jugar hasta las ocho; después hay que entrar para no molestar a los vecinos.
meaning: impersonal marker for people in general
part_of_speech: impersonal se marker before a finite modal auxiliary
grammar: Se precedes finite puede in the modal construction puede jugar. The understood players are people in general; no named person acts on themself, and puede remains singular.
register: Neutral explanation of a household play arrangement.
note: Patio = courtyard or patio; molestar a los vecinos = disturb the neighbors. Eight o'clock is the limit for outdoor play.

sentence: El aviso de la casa dice: «No se grita a deshoras; de once de la noche a siete de la mañana hay gente durmiendo».
part_of_speech: adverbial expression of inappropriate timing
grammar: A deshoras evaluates the hours as unsuitable for the activity. The sleeping period makes those hours explicit. Gritar has no expressed object here, so no se grita supplies an impersonal prohibition.
register: Direct wording in a fictional household notice.
note: Grita = shouts; gente = people. The notice links unsuitable shouting hours to other residents' sleep.

sentence: Ayer se auxilió a don Pablo después de su caída; dos vecinos lo ayudaron a sentarse y llamaron a su hija.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an impersonal se construction
grammar: Auxiliar a alguien means assisting someone in difficulty. Auxilió reports completed assistance yesterday; don Pablo is the personal direct object, and the later clause identifies the neighbors' concrete actions.
register: Neutral, somewhat formal reporting verb in an ordinary neighborhood account.
note: Caída = fall; ayudaron a sentarse = helped him sit down; llamaron a su hija = called his daughter.

sentence: En el pueblo de mi abuela, antes del teléfono, se avisaba a las familias de las reuniones de boca en boca; ahora hay un chat.
part_of_speech: adverbial expression of oral transmission
grammar: De boca en boca describes information passing orally from person to person. Imperfect avisaba presents the former practice; the sentence separately identifies the current chat.
register: Neutral family recollection of an earlier community practice.
note: Pueblo = town or village; avisar a alguien de algo = notify someone about something. The families are the people notified.

sentence: Hoy es domingo y la reunión es el viernes; se avisará a Ana y a Luis de la reunión con antelación, mañana lunes.
part_of_speech: adverbial expression of advance timing
grammar: Con antelación places notification before the relevant event. Monday's notification precedes Friday's meeting. In avisar a alguien de algo, Ana and Luis are personal direct objects, so impersonal avisará is singular.
register: Neutral planning language.
note: Avisará = will notify; de la reunión identifies what Ana and Luis will be notified about.

sentence: ¿Cómo se procede aquí para devolver un paquete con la dirección incorrecta: se llena una hoja o se llama a la tienda?
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative intransitive verb in an impersonal procedural question
grammar: Cómo se procede asks what procedure people follow. Proceder is intransitive here, has no expressed human subject, and does not describe someone acting on themself.
register: Courteous, moderately formal practical inquiry.
note: Dirección incorrecta = incorrect address; llenar una hoja = fill out a sheet. The question offers two possible procedural steps.

sentence: —¿Cómo funciona este taller? —Aquí se trabaja por turnos y se reparan sillas de madera.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative intransitive verb with impersonal agreement
grammar: Impersonal trabaja is singular because no grammatical subject is expressed. In the neighboring passive clause, sillas de madera is the plural subject and therefore takes reparan.
register: Neutral exchange about a workshop's operation.
note: Cómo funciona este taller = how this workshop operates; sillas de madera = wooden chairs.

sentence: Ayer se me olvidó la cita con el dentista: no fui y tuve que pedir otra fecha.
part_of_speech: pronominal event marker se followed by first-person singular affected-experiencer dative me
grammar: La cita is the singular grammatical subject of olvidó; me identifies the speaker who forgot. This event framing differs from me olvidé de la cita and does not erase the speaker's responsibility for missing it.
register: Ordinary personal explanation of a missed appointment.
note: Dentista = dentist. The speaker missed the appointment and had to request another date.

sentence: Luis, comprar el pan para la cena era tu responsabilidad, pero se te olvidó el encargo y ahora no tenemos pan.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun serving as the forgotten event subject
grammar: Encargo names a task entrusted to someone. El encargo is the singular subject of olvidó; te identifies Luis as the person who forgot his stated responsibility.
register: Direct familiar address about a household responsibility.
note: Responsabilidad = responsibility. The entrusted task is explicitly buying bread for dinner.

sentence: A Julia se le olvidó avisar a su hermana de la nueva hora de la cena; su hermana llegó a la hora anterior y tuvo que esperar.
part_of_speech: infinitive verb heading the forgotten action as grammatical subject
grammar: Avisar heads the infinitival action that was forgotten, so olvidó is singular. Le identifies Julia as the affected forgetter; a su hermana is separately the personal direct object of avisar, with de introducing the notification topic.
register: Neutral explanation of a family scheduling mistake.
note: Hora anterior = previously scheduled time. Julia omitted the notification, and her sister arrived at the previously scheduled time and had to wait.

sentence: A Ana y a mí se nos olvidaron dos tareas al salir de la casa vieja: cerrar las ventanas y entregar las llaves; por eso tuvimos que regresar.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative verb agreeing with the forgotten tasks
grammar: Dos tareas is the plural grammatical subject and controls olvidaron. Nos identifies Ana and the speaker as the affected forgetters; it does not control agreement. The two infinitives specify the forgotten tasks.
register: Ordinary account of a shared household omission.
note: Al salir = when leaving; casa vieja = old house; tuvimos que regresar = we had to return.

sentence: A Julia y a Pablo se les olvidó el plazo para entregar su solicitud conjunta y la llevaron dos días tarde.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb agreeing with the forgotten deadline
grammar: El plazo is the singular grammatical subject and controls olvidó. Plural les identifies Julia and Pablo as affected forgetters; two forgetters do not require a plural verb when the forgotten subject is singular.
register: Neutral account of a joint administrative omission.
note: Solicitud conjunta = joint application; la refers to that application; dos días tarde = two days late.

sentence: A Elena se le cayó el vaso de la mano mientras lo llevaba a la mesa; ella limpió el agua del piso.
part_of_speech: pronominal event marker se followed by third-person singular affected-holder dative le
grammar: El vaso is the subject of cayó. Le identifies Elena as the holder affected when it falls from her hand; Elena is not the grammatical subject of cayó and is not receiving a gift.
register: Ordinary household mishap account.
note: De la mano = from her hand; mientras lo llevaba = while she was carrying it; limpió = cleaned up.

sentence: A Elena se le cayeron los platos que llevaba a la mesa; los dos quedaron en el piso y ella los recogió.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative transitive verb
grammar: Recoger here means picking fallen objects up from the floor, extending beyond collecting an order or picking up a passenger. In the preceding event, cayeron agrees with los platos and le identifies their affected carrier.
register: Ordinary household mishap account.
note: Cayeron = fell, with plural agreement; los dos refers to both plates; quedaron en el piso = ended up on the floor.

sentence: Tomás lavaba el vaso que Ana le prestó cuando se le rompió en las manos; él compró otro para Ana.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-person breakage construction
grammar: Rompió presents the glass as undergoing breakage. The understood subject is el vaso; le identifies Tomás as affected while handling Ana's loan. The framing does not assert that Tomás bears no responsibility.
register: Neutral account of damage to an entrusted possession.
note: Lavaba = was washing; le prestó = lent him. The final clause states that Tomás bought Ana a replacement glass.

sentence: Rosa cocinaba y fue a contestar el teléfono; se le quemó el arroz y tuvo que preparar otra cosa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-person food-burning construction
grammar: El arroz is the subject of quemó; le identifies Rosa as the affected cook. This differs from an active statement that Rosa burned the rice, while the stated distraction still leaves her role visible.
register: Ordinary cooking-mishap account.
note: Cocinaba = was cooking; fue a contestar el teléfono = went to answer the phone.

sentence: A Iván se le perdió la llave del cuarto durante la mudanza; él era responsable de guardarla y tuvo que buscarla entre las cajas.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-person loss construction
grammar: La llave is the subject of perdió; Iván is identified by affected le. This differs from active Iván perdió la llave and from tú me lo perdiste, where the losing actor is the subject.
register: Neutral explanation of a misplaced possession.
note: Cuarto = room; responsable de guardarla = responsible for keeping the key safe; cajas = boxes.

sentence: A Irene se le mojaron los papeles con la lluvia mientras los llevaba sin bolsa y ahora no puede leer una página.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative verb in an affected-person wetting construction
grammar: Los papeles is the plural event subject, so the verb is mojaron. Le identifies Irene as the affected carrier; the rain supplies the external cause.
register: Ordinary account of rain damage to personal papers.
note: Mojar = wet; se mojaron = got wet; página = page. The papers were being carried without a bag.

sentence: Paula llevaba dos tazas a la mesa cuando se le manchó la blusa con café; tuvo que ponerse otra.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-person staining construction
grammar: La blusa is the subject undergoing staining; le identifies Paula as the affected wearer. The clause presents the resulting mishap rather than an intentional act of staining clothing.
register: Ordinary household mishap account.
note: Tazas = cups; con café identifies what stained the blouse; ponerse otra = put on another blouse.

sentence: Beto escribía un correo en su computadora cuando se le descompuso de la nada; no hubo golpes ni avisos y tuvo que usar otra.
part_of_speech: adverbial expression of unexpected occurrence without an apparent cause
grammar: De la nada presents the breakdown as unexpected and without an apparent cause in Beto's account. It does not claim that the device literally had no cause of failure.
register: Conversational account of an unexpected computer problem.
note: Golpes = knocks or impacts; avisos = warnings here. Le marks Beto as the affected owner and user of the computer.

sentence: Miriam hablaba por su teléfono cuando se le apagó; ella no tocó el botón y la pila ya no tenía carga.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-user device-shutdown construction
grammar: The phone is the understood subject of apagó; le marks Miriam as its affected user. The explicit lack of button contact and battery charge establish an unexpected shutdown rather than deliberate switching off.
register: Ordinary explanation of an interrupted phone activity.
note: Botón = button; carga = battery charge; tocó = touched.

sentence: Nuria llevaba su bolsa con cierre cuando se le abrió de repente; las llaves cayeron al piso y ella las recogió.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun naming a bag fastening
grammar: Cierre names the bag's zipper fastening. The bag is the understood subject of abrió, and le identifies Nuria as the affected owner carrying it.
register: Ordinary Mexican description of a bag mishap.
note: Bolsa con cierre = bag with a zipper. The opening is unexpected, and the falling keys supply its concrete consequence.

sentence: Omar sujetaba una cuerda para bajar la caja; se le soltó de las manos y la caja cayó al piso.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-holder release construction
grammar: The rope is the understood subject of soltó; le identifies Omar as the holder from whose hands it slipped. This differs from active Omar soltó la cuerda, which makes Omar the releasing subject.
register: Neutral account of an ordinary handling mishap.
note: Sujetar = hold securely; cuerda = rope; bajar la caja = lower the box.

sentence: Lucía quería guardar el secreto del regalo, pero se le escapó la palabra «bicicleta» frente a su hijo; él adivinó la sorpresa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb describing unintended speech in an affected-speaker construction
grammar: La palabra is the subject of escapó; le identifies Lucía as the speaker whose intended silence failed. Escapar here describes unintended speech, not the physical escape of a person or animal.
register: Ordinary family account of an accidental disclosure.
note: Guardar el secreto = keep the secret; regalo = gift; bicicleta = bicycle; adivinó = guessed.

sentence: A Diego se le acabó el hilo mientras cosía su camisa; no pudo terminarla y fue a comprar más.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb expressing resource exhaustion in an affected-person construction
grammar: El hilo is the subject of acabó: the supply ran out on Diego. This does not mean Diego completed sewing the shirt; the following clause explicitly states that he could not finish it.
register: Ordinary explanation of an interrupted household task.
note: Hilo = thread; cosía = was sewing; terminarla refers to finishing the shirt.

sentence: Estela quería cerrar la ventana de su cuarto, pero se le trabó el mecanismo y la ventana quedó a medio cerrar.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb describing a mechanical obstruction in an affected-user construction
grammar: El mecanismo is the subject of trabó; Estela is the affected user marked by le. The mechanism stops moving during her attempt, rather than Estela deliberately obstructing it.
register: Ordinary description of a household mechanical problem.
note: Mecanismo = mechanism; a medio cerrar = only partly closed. Cuarto means room.

sentence: Bruno usaba su impresora para sacar una copia de una receta de sopa cuando se le atoró una hoja; el papel ya no avanzaba y tuvo que parar.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb describing an item becoming lodged during an affected user's activity
grammar: Una hoja is the subject of atoró; le identifies Bruno as the affected printer user. The stopped paper movement makes the physical jam explicit. This illustrates an item lodged in a device, without claiming that atorar and trabar have mutually exclusive uses.
register: Ordinary Mexican-compatible description of a printer problem.
note: Impresora = printer; hoja = sheet of paper; avanzaba = was moving forward; parar = stop.

sentence: A Elisa se le secó la planta de su balcón durante los diez días que estuvo fuera; al volver, encontró todas las hojas secas.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-owner change construction
grammar: La planta undergoes drying and controls singular secó. Le identifies Elisa as its affected owner, not as an agent deliberately drying it.
note: Balcón = balcony; hojas = leaves; estuvo fuera = was away; secas = dry.

sentence: Mateo se preparó un café y tomó solo la mitad; lo dejó a medio tomar para atender la llamada de su hermana y se le enfrió durante la conversación.
part_of_speech: prepositional phrase with an infinitive describing incomplete consumption
grammar: A medio tomar describes the coffee as partly consumed and left unfinished. Mateo drank only half before setting it aside for the call.
note: Mitad = half; tomó = drank; se preparó = prepared for himself; se le enfrió = went cold on him.

sentence: A Nora se le derritieron las dos paletas de hielo que compró para sus hijos mientras esperaba el camión; solo quedó líquido en las bolsas.
part_of_speech: feminine plural compound noun phrase
grammar: Paletas de hielo names the frozen treats. The visible derritieron agrees with the two paletas; singular le identifies Nora as the affected buyer.
register: Paleta de hielo is ordinary Mexican vocabulary for an ice pop.
note: Líquido = liquid; solo quedó = only ... remained.

sentence: A Laura se le echó a perder la sopa que preparó para la cena; olía mal y tuvo que tirar todo el contenido de la olla.
part_of_speech: fixed complement completing the food-spoilage expression echarse a perder
grammar: Echarse a perder describes food spoiling. La sopa is the subject; le identifies Laura as the household cook affected by its loss.
note: Se echó a perder = went bad; olía mal = smelled bad; olla = cooking pot; contenido = contents.

sentence: Luis le confió su reloj a Beto para llevarlo al taller, pero a Beto se le extravió durante el trayecto y llegó sin él.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-keeper loss construction
grammar: The entrusted watch is the understood subject of extravió. Beto is its affected keeper; this reports a loss during handling rather than a passive search announcement.
note: Extraviarse = go missing; taller = workshop or repair shop; sin él refers to the watch.

sentence: A Marisa se le desprendió el botón de su chamarra mientras la guardaba; lo encontró en el piso junto al armario.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb describing accidental detachment
grammar: El botón is the detached subject. Le identifies Marisa as the affected owner handling her jacket; she is not presented as deliberately removing the button.
note: Botón = button; armario = wardrobe or cupboard; guardaba = was putting away.

sentence: A Raúl se le perdió el recibo de la compra compartida y salió mal parado del reparto: pagó todo y nadie le devolvió su parte.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjectival locution completing salir mal parado
grammar: Salir mal parado describes the person being left disadvantaged after an event. Masculine parado agrees with Raúl; the unpaid shared expense establishes the financial disadvantage.
note: Compra compartida = shared purchase; reparto = division or allocation here; su parte = their share of the cost.

sentence: A Daniela se le torció el plan de celebrar en el patio cuando empezó a llover; tuvo que acomodar a todos dentro de la casa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in a figurative affected-person construction
grammar: El plan is the subject of figurative torció. Le identifies Daniela as the planner affected when rain prevents her intended outdoor celebration.
note: Torcerse un plan = a plan goes awry; acomodar a todos = find room for everyone.

sentence: A Hugo se le traspapeló el permiso de su hija mientras ordenaba los recibos; lo encontró después entre dos facturas.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-handler document-loss construction
grammar: El permiso is the misplaced subject, and le marks Hugo as the affected person sorting the papers. The later discovery among invoices establishes misplacement rather than permanent loss.
note: Permiso = permission document here; facturas = invoices; ordenaba = was organizing.

sentence: A Irene se le borró la nota que escribía en su teléfono cuando lo guardó en la bolsa; al abrirla otra vez, no quedaba ninguna palabra.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-user erasure construction
grammar: La nota is the subject undergoing erasure. Le identifies Irene as its affected author and phone user; the account does not attribute deliberate deletion to her.
note: Nota = short written note; no quedaba ninguna palabra = no words remained.

sentence: A Fabián se le dobló la regla de plástico dentro de su mochila cuando puso los libros encima; ahora tiene una curva en medio.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-owner bending construction
grammar: La regla undergoes bending and controls singular dobló. Fabián is its affected owner, although his placement of the books explains the pressure.
note: Regla = ruler; mochila = backpack; curva = curve; en medio = in the middle.

sentence: A Teresa se le despegó la etiqueta del frasco mientras lo lavaba; quedó flotando en el agua y ya no pudo leer el nombre.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb describing loss of adhesion
grammar: La etiqueta is the subject losing adhesion. Le marks Teresa as the affected handler; the label and washing context select coming unstuck rather than an aircraft taking off.
note: Etiqueta = label; frasco = jar; flotando = floating.

sentence: A Samuel se le rasgó la cortina al jalarla para cerrar la ventana; él solo quería moverla y ahora la tela tiene una abertura larga.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb describing an accidental fabric tear
grammar: La cortina is the subject undergoing tearing. Samuel performs the pulling but did not intend the tear; affected-person framing remains compatible with his causal involvement.
register: Jalar is ordinary Mexican-compatible vocabulary for pulling.
note: Cortina = curtain; jalar = pull; tela = fabric; abertura = opening.

sentence: A Celia se le agrietó su caja de plástico con el peso de los libros; ahora tiene una línea abierta en un costado.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-owner cracking construction
grammar: Su caja identifies Celia's box as the subject developing a crack. Le marks Celia as its affected owner, and the books' weight supplies the stated condition.
note: Peso = weight; línea abierta = open line or crack here; costado = side.

sentence: A Iván se le desinfló el balón mientras jugaba con su hija; perdió tanto aire que ya no rebotaba y dejaron el juego.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-user deflation construction
grammar: El balón is the deflating subject, while le marks Iván as the player affected by the loss of air. The event is not presented as deliberate deflation.
note: Balón = sports ball; rebotaba = bounced; tanto aire que... = so much air that...; dejaron el juego = stopped playing.

sentence: A Rosa se le volteó el recipiente de sopa que llevaba a la mesa; todo el contenido cayó en su charola y ella se quedó sin cena.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-holder tipping construction
grammar: El recipiente is the tipping subject. Le marks Rosa as its affected carrier; the spilled contents establish an unintended overturning.
register: Charola is ordinary Mexican vocabulary for a tray.
note: Recipiente = container; charola = tray; se quedó sin cena = was left without dinner.

sentence: A Pilar se le resbaló el vaso de las manos mientras lo lavaba con jabón; ella intentó sostenerlo, pero cayó al fregadero.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb with an inanimate slipping subject
grammar: El vaso slips; Pilar does not slip herself. Le identifies the holder, and de las manos gives the point from which the glass slips.
note: Sostenerlo = hold or support it; fregadero = kitchen sink.

sentence: A Inés se le salpicó la camisa de salsa mientras mezclaba la comida; quedaron varias gotas rojas en la tela y tuvo que cambiarse.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative verb in an affected-wearer spattering construction
grammar: La camisa is the spattered subject, and le marks Inés as its affected wearer. The separate drops establish spattering rather than simply becoming wet.
note: Mezclaba = was mixing; gotas = drops; cambiarse = change clothes here.

sentence: Bruno, cierra la llave del agua antes de salir: se te olvida al menor descuido, sobre todo cuando suena tu teléfono, y hoy sigue abierta.
meaning: at the slightest lapse of attention
part_of_speech: adverbial expression specifying a minimal trigger
grammar: Al menor descuido presents even a small lapse of attention as sufficient to trigger the recurring forgetting. The pending action is closing the tap, which remains open now.
register: Familiar singular household reminder addressed to Bruno.
note: Descuido = lapse of attention; sobre todo = especially; sigue abierta refers to the tap.

sentence: Luis dijo: «Se me olvidó recoger a Ana porque decidí terminar la película antes de salir; asumo la responsabilidad por la espera de Ana».
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative verb in the accountability collocation asumir la responsabilidad
grammar: Asumir la responsabilidad explicitly accepts responsibility. The earlier affected-forgetting frame does not cancel Luis's acknowledgment of his distracting choice.
register: Direct acknowledgment of responsibility in a personal explanation.
note: Decidí = I decided; asumir la responsabilidad por = accept responsibility for; espera = wait or waiting period.

sentence: Luis se lava las manos antes de lavar su camisa; esa prenda se lava a mano, sin lavadora, porque tiene un bordado delicado.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution specifying manual washing
grammar: A mano specifies manual washing rather than machine washing. Luis se lava is self-directed; la prenda se lava describes how the garment is washed.
note: Prenda = garment; lavadora = washing machine; bordado delicado = delicate embroidery.

sentence: Julia se peina sola, pero hoy su hermana le desenreda el pelo sin dar tirones: mueve el peine despacio para no jalarle el cabello.
part_of_speech: negative infinitival manner phrase
grammar: Dar tirones means making abrupt pulling movements. Julia performs the visible self-combing, while her sister actively untangles Julia's hair without those pulls.
register: Ordinary family hair-care explanation; jalar is Mexican-compatible.
note: Pelo and cabello = hair; peine = comb; tirón = tug; desenredar = untangle.

sentence: Después de discutir por los planes del domingo, Ana y Sergio se reconciliaron: acordaron salir juntos y luego se abrazaron el uno al otro.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite indicative pronominal verb phrase with reciprocal meaning
grammar: Reconciliarse describes restoring a relationship after disagreement. Ana and Sergio are both participants in making peace; the following mutual hug reinforces that relationship.
note: Discutir = argue here; acordaron = agreed; se abrazaron = hugged each other.

sentence: Marta y Joel se turnan para cuidar a su abuela: ella la acompaña por la mañana y él por la tarde, así ambos pueden descansar.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Turnarse para introduces an activity distributed across alternating participants. Marta and Joel do not act on themselves; each takes a different period of their shared task.
note: Cuidar a alguien = look after someone; ambos refers to Marta and Joel.

sentence: Elena y Mario fijaron juntos la hora y el lugar; se reunieron de común acuerdo en el parque para hablar sin interrumpir a su familia.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution expressing mutual consent
grammar: De común acuerdo states that both participants accepted the arrangement. Se reunieron describes Elena and Mario meeting, not materials being gathered passively.
note: Fijar la hora y el lugar = set the time and place; común = shared here.

sentence: Eva se queja de que la tienda cierra antes de la hora anunciada; quiere comprar pan al salir del trabajo, pero siempre la encuentra cerrada.
meaning: that, introducing what she complains about
part_of_speech: governed preposition followed by a finite-clause complementizer
grammar: Quejarse retains de before a finite que-clause. Se belongs to the complaint verb; it is neither passive nor impersonal. The indicative reports the condition Eva complains about.
note: Hora anunciada = advertised time; al salir del trabajo = when leaving work.

sentence: Clara canceló la visita a su abuela para ir de compras; ahora se arrepiente de esa decisión porque no la ve desde hace un mes.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Arrepentirse de introduces regret over a prior choice. Se belongs to the lexical pronominal verb, and de introduces the decision regretted.
note: Ir de compras = go shopping; esa decisión refers to canceling the visit.

sentence: Elena tiene miedo de hablar frente al grupo, pero hoy se atreve a pedir una explicación porque necesita entender la tarea antes de empezar.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Atreverse a takes an infinitive naming the action requiring courage. Se belongs to the lexical verb; Elena intentionally asks rather than experiencing an accidental event.
note: Frente al grupo = in front of the group; atreverse a pedir = dare to ask.

sentence: Sofía se enteró de la cancelación de primera mano: Marta, la organizadora de la fiesta, la llamó para explicarle por qué decidió cancelarla.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution specifying a direct information source
grammar: De primera mano identifies information obtained directly from a participant: Marta organized and canceled the party. Se belongs to enterarse, not to a passive construction.
note: Cancelación = cancellation; organizadora = female organizer; la llamó refers to Sofía.

sentence: Tomás se aprovecha del trabajo de Ana: ella prepara todos los pedidos, pero él no ayuda, cobra todo el dinero y no le paga nada.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative lexical pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Se belongs to aprovecharse de, which describes exploiting another's contribution here. Del introduces Ana's work; Tomás benefits while doing none of the preparation and paying her nothing.
note: Pedidos = orders; cobra todo el dinero = collects all the money; le paga refers to paying Ana.

sentence: Carla se leyó las veinte páginas del cuento en una tarde; no dejó ninguna sin leer y después pudo contarle el final a su hermano.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite verb phrase with aspectual se emphasizing complete reading
grammar: Se emphasizes Carla's complete consumption of the bounded text. It does not make Carla the thing read or identify a listener; ordinary leyó can also describe completed reading.
note: Cuento = short story; el final = the ending; ninguna refers to a page.

sentence: Lalo se comió la única fresa de un bocado; no se le cayó ni quedó nada en el plato, porque la tomó y se la metió entera en la boca.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution specifying single-bite consumption
grammar: De un bocado specifies how Lalo consumed the entire small item. Visible consumptive se contrasts with the explicitly denied accidental falling construction se le cayó.
note: Fresa = strawberry; entera = whole; boca = mouth; se la metió = put it into his own mouth.

sentence: Después de caminar, Irene se bebió el vasito de agua de un trago; lo terminó completo y lo dejó vacío sobre la mesa.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution specifying single-swallow drinking
grammar: De un trago specifies a single swallow. Visible se bebió presents consumption of the bounded drink; se is not obligatory for every completed drinking event.
note: Vasito = small glass; trago = swallow of a drink; vacío = empty.

sentence: Los regalos se llevaron al salón en bolsas, pero Pablo se llevó el regalo de cumpleaños de Ana a escondidas de ella; lo ocultó bajo su chamarra para no revelar la sorpresa.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution specifying intentional concealment
grammar: A escondidas de ella identifies Ana as the person from whom Pablo conceals his action. Se llevaron first describes passive transport; Pablo se llevó names the actor taking a gift with him.
note: Salón = event room here; bajo su chamarra = under his jacket; ella refers to Ana.

sentence: Nadia se quedó con las ganas de bailar: llegó con su hermana al salón para el baile, pero ya estaba cerrado y tuvieron que regresar a casa.
part_of_speech: fixed prepositional complement in quedarse con las ganas de plus infinitive
grammar: Quedarse con las ganas de describes wanting to do something without getting to do it. Nadia's intended dancing and the closed venue establish the unfulfilled desire.
note: Bailar = dance; baile = dance event; salón = dance hall here.

sentence: El encargado le dijo a Óscar: «Por favor, salga; vamos a cerrar». Óscar se fue por las buenas y entregó la llave sin discutir.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution specifying noncoercive compliance
grammar: Por las buenas characterizes Óscar's voluntary compliance with the departure request. Se fue names his departure; se does not mark an accidentally lost object.
register: Conversational description of compliance after a courteous usted request.
note: Encargado = person in charge; sin discutir = without arguing.

sentence: El paquete se entrega en la puerta de la casa de Luis; Ana se lo da a él, el destinatario del envío, y Luis firma al recibirlo.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun identifying a delivery recipient
grammar: Destinatario identifies Luis as the intended receiver. In se lo da, se replaces le for Luis and lo represents paquete; the earlier se entrega is passive.
register: Neutral delivery vocabulary.
note: Envío = shipment; firma = signs; al recibirlo = upon receiving it.

sentence: En este barrio se camina mucho; Julia se fue rumbo a la plaza para comprar pan y todavía no llega a la tienda.
part_of_speech: directional prepositional locution
grammar: Rumbo a gives Julia's direction of travel without asserting arrival. Julia is the named actor of se fue; se camina is singular impersonal usage about people generally.
note: Barrio = neighborhood; plaza = public square; todavía no llega = has not arrived yet.

sentence: En el taller se reparan sillas; Ana y Leo se ayudan mutuamente: ella sostiene las piezas para él y él le alcanza las herramientas a ella.
part_of_speech: adverb explicitly marking a reciprocal relation
grammar: Mutuamente explicitly makes the helping reciprocal, as shown by the two directions of help. Passive reparan agrees with inanimate sillas; ayudan agrees with Ana y Leo.
register: Neutral explanatory wording for reciprocal activity.
note: Piezas = parts; herramientas = tools; sostiene = holds or supports; alcanza = hands something within reach here.

sentence: Marta explicó: «Borré mi nota deliberadamente porque ya no quería conservarla»; a Diego, en cambio, se le borró la suya mientras escribía y él quería recuperarla.
part_of_speech: adverb marking intentional agency
grammar: Deliberadamente marks Marta's acknowledged intentional deletion. Diego's note is the subject of se le borró, and his wish to recover it establishes an unwanted event.
note: La suya refers to Diego's own note; conservar = keep; recuperar = recover.

sentence: En nuestra casa, quien prepara la cena elige la música; hoy cocino yo.
part_of_speech: singular personal relative pronoun introducing a free relative subject
grammar: Quien has no explicit noun antecedent. Quien prepara la cena is the subject of elige; within that relative, quien is the singular subject of prepara.
register: Everyday explanation of a household arrangement.
note: Elige = chooses; cocino = I cook.

sentence: Al final de la clase, les devuelvo los cuadernos a quienes los entregaron al principio; hoy son Ana y Luis.
part_of_speech: recipient preposition and plural personal relative pronoun introducing a free relative
grammar: A quienes introduces the recipients without a preceding people noun. Les doubles those recipients, while los cuadernos is the direct object of devuelvo.
register: Neutral classroom explanation.
note: Cuadernos = notebooks; entregaron = handed in; devuelvo = I return.

sentence: Mañana puede abrir el salón quienquiera que tenga la llave; no hace falta elegir a una persona desde hoy.
part_of_speech: indefinite personal pronoun followed by relative que
grammar: Quienquiera is written as one word and is followed here by que tenga. It allows any person meeting the key requirement; separate quien quiera means the person who wants.
register: Careful but ordinary explanation of an open practical choice.
note: Elegir = choose; salón = shared room here; no hace falta elegir = there is no need to choose.

sentence: El camión no pasó a las ocho, lo cual nos obligó a caminar hasta la escuela.
part_of_speech: neuter relative sequence referring to a preceding proposition
grammar: Lo cual refers to the complete fact that the bus did not pass at eight. Its visible consequence is the group's forced walk; it does not introduce previously unspecified content.
register: Neutral written explanation.
note: Nos obligó a caminar = forced us to walk.

sentence: Mis tres hermanos, que viven en Toluca, vienen a cenar hoy; los tres salen de allá juntos.
part_of_speech: invariant relative pronoun introducing an explanatory clause
grammar: The commas make que viven en Toluca added information about all three already identified siblings. This clause does not select a subset; que remains unchanged with a plural antecedent.
register: Neutral written family description.
note: Allá = there, referring to Toluca.

sentence: Compramos seis vasos, de los cuales dos llegaron rotos; conservamos los otros cuatro para la cena.
part_of_speech: partitive preposition and masculine plural relative sequence
grammar: De los cuales links the subset dos to the previously quantified six glasses. Los cuales agrees with vasos; dos remains outside the blank.
register: Careful written account of a purchase.
note: Rotos = broken; conservamos = we keep here.

sentence: La vecina a quien vi ayer en la tienda vive arriba; la reconocí por su voz.
part_of_speech: personal direct-object preposition and singular relative pronoun
grammar: The neighbor is the direct object of vi, and the speaker is its understood subject. A is personal a here; it does not identify a recipient receiving an item.
register: Neutral conversation about a neighbor.
note: Voz = voice; arriba = upstairs here.

sentence: Ernesto, de quien recibí esta carta ayer, vive en Puebla; él la escribió y me la mandó por correo.
part_of_speech: source preposition and singular personal relative pronoun
grammar: De marks Ernesto as the source of the received letter. It belongs to recibir algo de alguien, rather than hablar de alguien about a person.
register: Neutral written personal account.
note: Carta = letter; recibí = I received; por correo = by mail here.

sentence: La razón por la que no fui a la cena fue el retraso del camión; sí quería ir, pero llegué a casa a medianoche.
part_of_speech: causal preposition with a feminine singular article and relative pronoun
grammar: Por la que relates the missed dinner to the explicit antecedent razón. La agrees with razón; por expresses a reason rather than a physical route.
register: Everyday explanation of a missed social event.
note: Razón = reason here; sí quería ir emphasizes that the speaker did want to go.

sentence: La biblioteca cerró antes de las seis, por lo que Ana y yo estudiamos en casa esa tarde.
part_of_speech: relative connective expressing a consequence of a preceding proposition
grammar: Por lo que refers back to the library's closing before six and introduces its consequence. It is not accented interrogative por qué asking a motive.
register: Neutral explanation of a changed study plan.
note: Estudiamos is past here because esa tarde anchors the completed account.

sentence: Para mí, lo que propuso Ana es más práctico: comer en casa cuesta menos y podemos hablar sin ruido.
part_of_speech: neuter relative sequence introducing a free relative subject
grammar: Lo que propuso Ana is the subject of es más práctico. Within that relative, Ana is the subject of propuso and lo que represents her proposal as its direct object.
register: Reasoned opinion between people choosing a meal location.
note: Propuso = proposed; práctico = practical.

sentence: Podemos preparar la cena con lo que hay en casa: arroz, frijoles y dos huevos; no necesitamos comprar nada.
part_of_speech: means preposition and neuter free-relative sequence
grammar: Con lo que hay en casa denotes the available resources for making dinner. There is no named feminine instrument antecedent, unlike con la que.
register: Everyday household planning.
note: The food list makes the available resources explicit.

sentence: Ana, pon la mesa en lo que yo termino de preparar la sopa; ya estoy cocinando y luego comemos juntas.
part_of_speech: temporal locution introducing a bounded concurrent interval
grammar: En lo que marks the interval during which the speaker finishes cooking and Ana can set the table. It has a temporal function in this sentence.
register: Conversational Mexican household coordination between familiar speakers.
note: Juntas refers to Ana and the female speaker; luego = afterward.

sentence: En una carta a mi hermana conté cuanto recordaba del viaje, sin dejar fuera ningún detalle.
part_of_speech: unaccented nominal relative pronoun with a totalizing meaning
grammar: Cuanto means everything that and introduces the complete remembered content. It is not a quantity question or a determiner modifying a following noun.
register: Compact written narrative; somewhat more formal than todo lo que.
note: Conté = I recounted; dejar fuera = leave out.

sentence: Hay sol en el patio y sombra bajo el árbol; vamos a comer donde hay sombra para no tener calor.
part_of_speech: locative relative adverb introducing a free relative
grammar: Donde hay sombra supplies the eating location without modifying an explicit place noun. This is a location decision, not a dónde question.
register: Everyday choice of a comfortable eating location.
note: Patio = courtyard or patio; sombra = shade; bajo el árbol = under the tree.

sentence: Mañana iremos adonde Ana decida; todavía está comparando dos lugares para la reunión.
part_of_speech: destination relative adverb introducing a free relative
grammar: Adonde supplies the destination of iremos without an explicit place antecedent. Decida is present subjunctive because Ana's selection is still pending.
register: Neutral planning among meeting participants.
note: Iremos = we will go; decida = chooses in this pending-choice clause.

sentence: Dejé de cocinar justo cuando llegó mi hermana; ella terminó la cena y yo puse la mesa.
part_of_speech: adverb emphasizing exact temporal coincidence before cuando
grammar: Justo emphasizes that stopping coincided precisely with the sister's arrival. Cuando introduces an actual completed occasion; that previously introduced temporal use remains visible.
register: Everyday account of sharing meal preparation.
note: Justo cuando = right when; dejé de cocinar = I stopped cooking; ella refers to the sister.

sentence: Preparo el arroz como me enseñó mi mamá: uso dos tazas de agua por cada taza de arroz.
part_of_speech: relative adverb of manner
grammar: Como me enseñó mi mamá specifies the method used to prepare the rice. It does not ask how or supply the second term of an equality comparison.
register: Everyday explanation of a learned cooking method.
note: Taza = cup; por cada taza = for each cup.

sentence: Ordené los libros según me indicó Rosa: primero los infantiles y después los de cocina; ella me enseñó ese orden esta mañana.
part_of_speech: conjunction introducing manner or conformity with instructions
grammar: Según me indicó Rosa presents Rosa's actual instructions as the model followed. The stated book order makes the conformity concrete.
register: Neutral explanation of following another person's instructions.
note: Ordené = I arranged; indicó = instructed or indicated here; infantiles = intended for children.

sentence: La tapa del recipiente, la cual tiene una grieta, no cierra bien; el recipiente está intacto.
part_of_speech: feminine singular explanatory relative sequence
grammar: La cual agrees with feminine tapa, distinguishing it from nearby masculine recipiente. The commas introduce an explanatory clause; intacto confirms that the container itself is undamaged.
register: Careful written description; la cual is more formal than que here.
note: Tapa = lid; recipiente = container; grieta = crack; intacto = undamaged.

sentence: La duda que necesito resolver es si el precio incluye la entrega; voy a llamar a la tienda antes de pagar.
part_of_speech: transitive infinitive in the collocation resolver una duda
grammar: Resolver una duda means clearing up an unanswered question. The visible relative identifies that question; the target is the lexical collocation, rather than relative que.
register: Ordinary customer inquiry.
note: Duda = unanswered question here; incluye = includes.

sentence: Marta es la vecina que va a coordinar la comida del domingo; ella decide quién cocina cada platillo y a qué hora lo lleva.
part_of_speech: transitive infinitive
grammar: Coordinar means organizing the contributions and timing of several participants. The visible relative identifies Marta through that organizing responsibility.
register: Everyday organization of a shared neighborhood meal.
note: Platillo = prepared dish; decide = decides; quién and a qué hora introduce the decisions being organized.

sentence: Óscar es el vecino que va a supervisar la reparación del techo: revisará cada etapa, pero los albañiles harán el trabajo.
part_of_speech: transitive infinitive
grammar: Supervisar means overseeing and checking the work. Óscar checks the stages, while the builders carry out the repair.
register: Neutral discussion of a household repair.
note: Techo = roof here; albañiles = builders; reparación = repair; revisará = will check.

sentence: La mesa que nos prestó Irene va a sustituir a la nuestra durante la reparación; el sábado, el carpintero nos devolverá la nuestra.
part_of_speech: transitive infinitive expressing replacement
grammar: Sustituir means taking another item's place. The repair interval and promised return establish a temporary substitution here; the verb itself does not always imply temporary replacement.
register: Everyday household arrangement.
note: Carpintero = carpenter; la nuestra = our table; devolverá = will return.

sentence: El dibujo que hizo Lidia va a complementar la receta: el texto explica los pasos y la imagen muestra cómo debe quedar el pan.
part_of_speech: transitive infinitive
grammar: Complementar means adding a useful function to an existing resource. The drawing supplies the expected appearance while the written recipe supplies the procedure.
register: Ordinary discussion of making a recipe easier to use.
note: Dibujo = drawing; texto = written text; imagen = image; pasos = procedural steps.

sentence: El horario que ofrece este curso parece encajar con mis necesidades: las clases son de noche y yo trabajo de día.
part_of_speech: infinitive with con expressing suitability
grammar: Encajar con mis necesidades means fitting the speaker's practical requirements. The complementary class and work times establish suitability rather than physical fit.
register: Everyday evaluation of a study option.
note: Necesidades = needs; ofrece = offers; de día = during the day; de noche = at night.

sentence: En la cena de hoy, recoger los platos es la tarea que le va a corresponder a Luis; Ana sirve el agua y yo cocino.
part_of_speech: infinitive with an indirect-person complement introduced by a
grammar: Corresponder a alguien assigns the responsibility to a person. Que represents la tarea as the subject of va a corresponder; le and a Luis identify the person to whom the task falls.
register: Everyday allocation of shared household duties.
note: Recoger los platos = clear the plates; sirve el agua = serves the water.

sentence: Elegir la fecha de nuestra mudanza es un asunto que nos incumbe a Ana y a mí; vamos a elegirla nosotros, no nuestros vecinos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb with an indirect-person complement
grammar: Incumbe identifies the matter as a concern or responsibility of Ana and the speaker. Nos and a Ana y a mí identify those concerned; singular asunto, represented by que, controls incumbe.
register: Careful explanatory language about responsibility for a personal decision.
note: Asunto = matter; elegirla refers to choosing the moving date.

sentence: El plan que propone Ana puede abarcar las necesidades de toda la familia: incluye tiempo para estudiar, trabajar y descansar.
part_of_speech: transitive infinitive expressing scope
grammar: Abarcar means covering a range within a single plan. The listed needs establish that range rather than one isolated purpose.
register: Neutral discussion of a shared family plan.
note: Propone = proposes; toda la familia = the whole family.

sentence: La tarea que aceptó Rosa va a consistir en revisar los nombres de la lista; no tiene que llamar a nadie.
part_of_speech: infinitive with its governed preposition en
grammar: Consistir en introduces the action that makes up the task. En is retained before revisar, whose object remains visible.
register: Neutral explanation of a limited practical responsibility.
note: Aceptó = agreed to take on here; revisar los nombres = check the names; lista = list.

sentence: Ayer, Luis dijo que estaba en casa cuando llegó el paquete; yo no estuve allí y solo puedo repetir su versión.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite reporting verb followed by complementizer que
grammar: Dijo que introduces Luis's indirectly reported assertion rather than quoting his exact words. Estaba locates his claimed presence at the package's arrival; the narrator explicitly identifies the information as Luis's account.
register: Neutral retelling of another person's statement.
note: No estuve allí = I was not there; allí refers to the house; su versión = Luis's account.

sentence: Marta explicó que canceló la comida por falta de agua; esa es la razón que ella nos dio y yo no estuve en su casa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite reporting verb followed by complementizer que
grammar: Explicó que attributes an explanation to Marta. The water shortage is the reason she supplied; the narrator does not present a personal inspection of her home.
register: Neutral account of a canceled social arrangement.
note: Canceló la comida = canceled the planned meal.

sentence: En una charla entre vecinos, Leo comentó que su hermana vende pan los sábados; yo no comprobé el dato.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite reporting verb followed by complementizer que
grammar: Comentó que presents the information as a casual remark by Leo. The narrator explicitly leaves it unverified.
register: Casual conversation among neighbors.
note: Charla = informal conversation; dato = piece of information.

sentence: La vendedora aseguró que la mesa es de madera; habló con mucha seguridad, pero yo no he comprobado el material.
part_of_speech: feminine singular abstract noun in a prepositional expression of manner
grammar: Seguridad means confidence in con mucha seguridad, describing the seller's manner of speaking. Her confidence does not establish that the narrator has verified the claim.
register: Neutral report of a seller's confident statement.
note: Vendedora = female seller; con mucha seguridad = very confidently; material = substance an object is made from.

sentence: Raúl admitió que olvidó mandar las invitaciones; aceptó que el retraso fue responsabilidad suya.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite acknowledgment verb followed by complementizer que
grammar: Admitió que introduces acknowledgment of an inconvenient fact. Raúl's own acceptance of responsibility is explicit in the sentence.
register: Neutral report of accepting a personal mistake.
note: Responsabilidad suya = his responsibility; olvidó mandar = forgot to send.

sentence: Ana dice que Raúl tiene la llave del salón; él niega que la tenga y pide ayuda para buscarla.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative denial verb followed by complementizer que
grammar: Niega que presents Raúl's current rejection of Ana's claim. Present-subjunctive tenga is inside the denied content; neither speaker's claim is independently endorsed by the narrator.
register: Neutral account of a disagreement about a missing key.
note: La and buscarla refer to the key; él refers to Raúl.

sentence: Claudia afirma que el camión sale a las siete; yo todavía no he consultado el horario y no puedo confirmarlo.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative reporting verb
grammar: Afirma attributes the asserted schedule to Claudia. Indicative sale expresses the content she asserts; the narrator explicitly has not checked it.
register: Neutral attribution of a current statement.
note: Confirmarlo = confirm that information; no he consultado = I have not checked a reference source.

sentence: Elena reconoce que su plan no deja tiempo para descansar; por eso va a quitar una actividad.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative acknowledgment verb
grammar: Reconoce means accepting the stated limitation of her own plan. It does not mean identifying a familiar person.
register: Neutral discussion of revising a practical plan.
note: No deja tiempo = leaves no time; quitar una actividad = remove an activity from the plan.

sentence: Conozco el incidente de oídas: Marta vio cómo se cayó Bruno y me lo contó, pero yo no estuve ahí.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution marking indirect information
grammar: De oídas marks knowledge obtained from another person's account rather than direct observation. Marta is the named witness and source; the narrator was absent.
register: Neutral explanation of the limits of one's knowledge.
note: Incidente = incident; se cayó = fell; me lo contó = told me what happened.

sentence: Según Nora, el salón estará abierto mañana; yo todavía no he hablado con el encargado y no puedo confirmar ese dato.
part_of_speech: preposition attributing information to a named source
grammar: Según Nora attributes the opening information to Nora. The narrator's lack of confirmation remains explicit; this is source attribution rather than conformity with instructions.
register: Neutral attribution of unconfirmed practical information.
note: Encargado = person in charge; ese dato = that piece of information.

sentence: Hoy es miércoles: el lunes Clara dijo que iba a vender su carro el martes, pero el comprador canceló y ella todavía lo tiene.
part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect prospective auxiliary followed by a
grammar: Iba a presents Clara's intended sale as future relative to her Monday statement. The canceled purchase and her continued ownership establish that the plan did not happen.
note: Comprador = buyer; canceló = canceled the purchase.

sentence: El lunes, el pronóstico de la radio decía que llovería el jueves; hoy es miércoles y todavía no sabemos si lloverá.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Pronóstico names the forecast attributed to the radio. Visible llovería places the predicted rain after Monday without establishing that it will occur.
note: Decía = said or stated; llovería = would rain; lloverá = will rain.

sentence: El martes, Julia me dijo «Estoy mareada»; hoy jueves explico que estaba mareada durante aquella llamada, pero que ahora se siente bien.
