part_of_speech: third-person singular imperfect indicative copular verb
grammar: Estaba locates Julia's reported dizziness at Tuesday's call. The narrator explicitly contrasts that condition with Julia's current wellbeing.
note: Mareada = dizzy, describing Julia; aquella llamada = that earlier call.

sentence: El lunes, Pablo me dijo que vive en Toluca; hoy es viernes, lo visité ayer y sigue en la misma casa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative verb
grammar: Vive retains present reference after past dijo because Pablo's residence is presented as continuing now. Yesterday's visit supports that continuing fact.
note: Lo visité = I visited him; sigue en la misma casa = he is still in the same house.

sentence: Julia llamó desde Puebla y dijo «Aquí llueve»; yo estoy en Toluca y le cuento a Luis que ahí llovía durante la llamada.
part_of_speech: deictic adverb of place
grammar: Ahí refers to Julia's location in Puebla. Her quoted aquí is re-anchored when a narrator located in Toluca reports the statement.
note: Aquí belongs to Julia's quoted viewpoint; ahí in the report still identifies Puebla.

sentence: Hoy, miércoles 6, lo cuento así: Inés anunció el lunes 4 que entregaría el libro al día siguiente, es decir, el martes 5; sus palabras fueron «Mañana lo entrego».
part_of_speech: temporal adverbial locution
grammar: Al día siguiente re-expresses Inés's Monday mañana as Tuesday. It is anchored to her announcement, not to the narrator's Wednesday.
note: Entregaría = would hand over; es decir = that is.

sentence: Hoy es viernes 8 y repito el mensaje de Eva del miércoles 6: dijo que devolvió la llave el día anterior, el martes 5; sus palabras fueron «Ayer la devolví».
part_of_speech: noun phrase functioning as a temporal adjunct
grammar: El día anterior refers to the day before Eva's Wednesday message. It preserves her quoted ayer as Tuesday rather than Thursday, the day before the narrator speaks.
note: Anterior = previous; devolvió = returned the key.

sentence: Hoy es viernes y repito el aviso de Leo del miércoles: dijo que no abriría la tienda ese día; sus palabras fueron «Hoy no abro».
part_of_speech: demonstrative noun phrase functioning as a temporal adjunct
grammar: Ese día preserves Wednesday as the reference of Leo's quoted hoy. The narrator's current Friday does not replace the source's day.
note: Abriría = would open; abro = I open.

sentence: Elena me dijo «Mi bolsa está en el carro»; ahora le cuento a Luis que su bolsa estaba en el carro, la de Elena, no la mía.
part_of_speech: singular possessive determiner with a third-person singular possessor
grammar: Su shifts Elena's quoted first-person mi to third-person possession in the narrator's report. La de Elena explicitly identifies the owner.
note: La de Elena = Elena's bag; la mía = mine, referring to the narrator's bag.

sentence: Marta dijo a sus hijas «Ustedes tienen permiso para usar mi carro»; yo no estaba con ellas y ahora cuento que Marta les dio permiso para usarlo.
part_of_speech: third-person plural indirect-object clitic pronoun
grammar: Les represents Marta's daughters as the recipients of permission in the narrator's report. They were the original ustedes audience; the narrator explicitly was not among them.
note: Usarlo refers to using Marta's car.

sentence: Anoche, Sara le preguntó a Iván si tenía la llave; él respondió que no, y hoy yo cuento esa conversación.
part_of_speech: completive conjunction introducing an indirect yes-or-no question
grammar: Si introduces what Sara asked Iván. Indicative tenía belongs to an indirect yes-or-no question; this si does not set a condition.
note: Anoche = last night; tenía la llave = had the key; respondió = answered.

sentence: Elena le preguntó a Bruno dónde guardaba la llave; él señaló el cajón donde suele dejarla.
part_of_speech: accented interrogative adverb in an indirect question
grammar: Dónde retains its interrogative accent inside Elena's reported question. Visible unaccented donde instead modifies the explicit location antecedent cajón.
note: Guardaba = kept; señaló = pointed to; dejarla refers to leaving the key there.

sentence: El lunes, Ana le preguntó a Mario cuándo volvería él a casa; Mario respondió «El viernes», una fecha todavía futura en esa conversación.
part_of_speech: accented interrogative adverb in an indirect question
grammar: Cuándo retains the interrogative accent in Ana's reported timing question. Volvería places Mario's return after the Monday conversation.
note: Volvería = would return; él refers to Mario; futura = still in the future.

sentence: La maestra quiere saber qué material necesitan sus alumnos Ana y Luis para el cartel; ahora se lo pregunta a los dos.
part_of_speech: accented interrogative determiner in an indirect question
grammar: Qué modifies material inside the current indirect inquiry introduced by quiere saber. The teacher is seeking information from Ana and Luis, rather than asserting what they need.
note: Alumnos = students; material = supplies here; cartel = poster; se lo pregunta = asks them that question.

sentence: Rosa me preguntó si Luis podía ir por las tortillas; la pregunta fue para mí, aunque Luis era quien tenía que salir.
part_of_speech: first-person singular indirect-object clitic pronoun
grammar: Me identifies the narrator as Rosa's question recipient. Luis is separately identified as the potential actor inside the question.
note: Ir por las tortillas = go get the tortillas; para mí confirms who received the question.

sentence: La propuesta de Nora es que usemos el patio para la reunión; ella la presenta hoy y todavía no hay un acuerdo.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Propuesta labels Nora's suggested arrangement. Visible subjunctive usemos gives its proposed content without asserting that the group has adopted it.
note: Presenta = puts forward here; un acuerdo = an agreement.

sentence: El coordinador hace una petición a Eva: le pide que llegue media hora antes de la reunión para abrir el salón; ella todavía no responde.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Petición names the coordinator's request to Eva. Pide que llegue gives the requested action without asserting its completion; Eva has not yet answered.
register: Neutral account of a group coordinator's practical request.
note: Coordinador = person organizing the group's activity; media hora antes de la reunión = half an hour before the meeting.

sentence: La recomendación de mi amiga Julia es que yo descanse esta tarde; es un consejo, no una obligación, y ella no promete una mejoría para mañana.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Recomendación labels Julia's advice. The sentence explicitly distinguishes advice from obligation and from a promise of improvement.
register: Advice between friends.
note: Consejo = advice; yo descanse = that I rest; mejoría = improvement in one's condition.

sentence: Nora prometió que pagaría el arreglo de mi silla el viernes; hoy es jueves y el cumplimiento de esa promesa sigue pendiente, porque todavía no he recibido el dinero.
part_of_speech: masculine singular abstract noun
grammar: Cumplimiento names carrying out the promise. The Thursday update leaves fulfillment pending without claiming that Nora has missed Friday's deadline.
note: Arreglo = repair here; promesa = promise; pagaría = would pay.

sentence: Raúl dice que ya devolvió la silla, pero esa devolución no consta en la lista de entregas que revisé; todavía no puedo confirmarla.
part_of_speech: negated third-person singular present indicative verb
grammar: No consta states that the return is absent from the record inspected. This limits the available evidence without proving that Raúl's claim is false.
register: Neutral practical record checking.
note: Devolución = return of an item; lista de entregas = handover list; confirmarla refers to confirming the return.

sentence: Tú y yo ya tenemos los boletos del concierto; vamos directo a la entrada, ya que no necesitamos pasar a la taquilla.
part_of_speech: causal subordinating conjunctive locution
grammar: Ya que introduces an accepted practical reason for going directly to the entrance. The reason follows from the tickets already held by both speakers.
register: Ordinary planning between familiar companions.
note: Taquilla = ticket office; vamos directo = let's go straight.

sentence: El salón tiene solo diez sillas, como vimos juntos; puesto que somos quince, la reunión será en el patio.
part_of_speech: causal subordinating conjunctive locution
grammar: Puesto que introduces the shared attendance premise used to explain the location decision. It supplies reasoning in a written message rather than directly answering a why question.
register: Neutral written explanation to fellow meeting participants.
note: Como vimos juntos = as we saw together; será en el patio = will take place in the patio.

sentence: Como ya sabíamos que no había agua en la cocina, llevamos los platos a casa de mi hermana para lavarlos.
part_of_speech: causal subordinating conjunction
grammar: Initial como supplies the known reason before the completed response. It explains why the dishes were taken elsewhere, rather than describing how they were carried.
note: Sabíamos = we knew; lavarlos = wash them, referring to the dishes.

sentence: Aviso a los vecinos: el elevador no funciona debido a una avería; por ahora hay que usar las escaleras.
part_of_speech: causal prepositional locution
grammar: Debido a introduces the breakdown as a noun-phrase cause of the interruption. It does not introduce an intended purpose or a beneficiary.
register: Neutral building notice addressed to residents.
note: Elevador = elevator; escaleras = stairs.

sentence: Cancelamos el paseo a causa de la lluvia; el parque quedó lleno de agua y no podíamos caminar por ahí.
part_of_speech: causal prepositional locution
grammar: A causa de identifies rain as the external cause of an unwanted cancellation. The flooded park makes the practical connection explicit.
note: Quedó lleno de agua = ended up full of water; por ahí = through that area.

sentence: Mi vecina me prestó una mesa; gracias a ese préstamo, todos pudimos cenar sentados y nadie tuvo que comer de pie.
part_of_speech: causal prepositional locution
grammar: Gracias a presents the loan as a helpful cause. The beneficial result is explicit: everyone was able to eat seated.
note: Préstamo = loan; sentados = seated; de pie = standing.

sentence: Mi amigo Luis me dice «Llegamos tarde por culpa de tu demora»; yo le recuerdo que el camión también salió tarde.
meaning: because of, with blame assigned to
part_of_speech: causal prepositional locution expressing attributed blame
grammar: Por culpa de presents Luis's attribution of blame. The narrator's reply supplies another relevant delay rather than endorsing his explanation as the complete account.
register: A reproach between friends.
note: Tu demora = your delay; le recuerdo = I remind him.

sentence: La reunión del club requiere al menos diez socios; solo llegaron seis y se canceló por falta de cuórum.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Cuórum names the minimum attendance required for this club meeting. Known por falta de introduces its absence as the cause of cancellation.
register: Ordinary club meeting organization.
note: Socios = club members; requiere = requires; al menos = at least.

sentence: Perdí mi lugar en la cena por no responder a la invitación antes del viernes; yo leí la fecha, pero olvidé contestar.
part_of_speech: causal preposition followed by infinitival negation
grammar: Por no introduces the narrator's omitted response as the cause of losing the dinner place. No negates responder, whose understood actor is the narrator.
note: Mi lugar en la cena = my place at the dinner; responder a la invitación = reply to the invitation.

sentence: Te ayudo a ordenar los papeles porque quiero terminar pronto, no porque seas incapaz; tú ya hiciste esta tarea sin ayuda ayer.
part_of_speech: negated causal conjunction
grammar: No porque rejects the proposed explanation of the help and introduces subjunctive seas. The actual motive is stated separately: the speaker wants to finish soon.
register: Reassurance to a familiar person while sharing a task.
note: Incapaz = unable or incapable; seas incapaz is the explanation being rejected.

sentence: Le mando a mi mamá una foto del recibo para que la amplíe en su pantalla y lea el número; todavía no sé si podrá leerlo.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present subjunctive transitive verb
grammar: Amplíe means enlarging the image for closer reading. Its present subjunctive belongs to the mother's intended action after para que; successful reading remains unconfirmed.
note: Ampliar una foto = enlarge a photo; la refers to the photo; lea = read in the purpose clause.

sentence: Mensaje al grupo: mañana revisaré las direcciones a fin de evitar otra entrega equivocada; todavía no he empezado la revisión.
part_of_speech: purpose prepositional locution governing an infinitive
grammar: A fin de introduces the aim of the planned address check. The narrator has not started the check, so the message does not claim that another error has been prevented.
register: Neutral written message to a group.
note: Revisaré = I will check; entrega equivocada = incorrect delivery; revisión = checking.

sentence: En nuestra tienda compramos menos fruta con el fin de reducir la merma, pero ayer se echaron a perder dos cajas.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Merma names the loss of saleable fruit through spoilage. Con el fin de gives the purpose of buying less, while yesterday's spoiled boxes show that the purpose does not guarantee the outcome.
register: Ordinary discussion of a small shop's purchasing decisions.
note: Reducir = reduce; con el fin de = with the aim of; dos cajas = two boxes of fruit.

sentence: Fui a casa de mi hermano con la intención de hablar del préstamo, pero no estaba y regresé sin hablar con él.
part_of_speech: prepositional purpose expression governing an infinitive
grammar: Con la intención de identifies the narrator's own intended conversation. The brother's absence and the narrator's return without speaking establish a different actual outcome.
note: Regresé = I returned; sin hablar con él = without speaking with my brother.

sentence: Los vecinos formamos un grupo con el objetivo de mantener limpio el parque; cada familia va a recoger la basura de una zona el sábado.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Objetivo names the neighbors' shared goal. The assigned Saturday cleanup is a concrete measure toward that goal rather than proof that the park is already clean.
register: Ordinary community project discussion.
note: Formamos un grupo = we formed a group; mantener limpio = keep clean; zona = area.

sentence: Envolví los platos en una cobija para amortiguar los golpes durante el viaje, pero la tela mojada los manchó.
part_of_speech: transitive infinitive
grammar: Amortiguar means reducing the force of the bumps affecting the plates. Visible para gives the intended protection; staining is a separate, unintended effect.
note: Envolví = I wrapped; cobija = blanket; golpes = bumps or impacts; tela mojada = wet fabric.

sentence: Ana, puedes usar mi carro con tal de que pagues la gasolina; yo acepto quedarme sin él el sábado.
part_of_speech: conditional subordinating conjunctive locution
grammar: Con tal de que introduces the condition the owner accepts for lending the car. Present subjunctive pagues expresses Ana's required action; the owner's Saturday inconvenience is explicit.
register: A practical agreement with a familiar addressee.
note: Gasolina = gasoline; quedarme sin él = be left without my car.

sentence: Luis, te doy permiso para usar mi mesa a condición de que la traigas de vuelta hoy; ya aceptaste ese trato y yo la necesito mañana.
part_of_speech: conditional subordinating conjunctive locution
grammar: A condición de que states the explicitly agreed restriction on permission. Present subjunctive traigas refers to Luis's required return of the owner's table.
register: An explicit personal borrowing agreement.
note: Trato = agreement; ya aceptaste = you already accepted; de vuelta = back.

sentence: Ana, puedes estudiar en mi casa mañana, siempre que uses audífonos para la música; mi hermano necesita dormir y esa es mi condición.
part_of_speech: conditional subordinating conjunctive locution
grammar: Siempre que limits a specific offer for tomorrow. Present subjunctive uses expresses the proviso; the phrase does not mean habitual whenever here.
register: A household offer to a familiar addressee.
note: Audífonos = headphones; uses = you use, present subjunctive; condición = condition.

sentence: Mañana voy a llevar la mesa al patio, a menos que llueva; en ese caso vamos a comer en la cocina.
part_of_speech: exceptive conditional subordinating conjunctive locution
grammar: A menos que identifies rain as the exception that blocks taking the table outside. Present subjunctive llueva marks the pending exception; the kitchen is the alternative in that case.
note: En ese caso = in that case, referring to rain.

sentence: El camión no pasó y tuve que caminar, así que llegué tarde a clase.
part_of_speech: consecutive conjunctive locution
grammar: Así que connects the transport problem and resulting walk with the actual consequence: arriving late.
register: Ordinary explanation of a delay.
note: No pasó means the bus did not come by; llegué tarde = I arrived late.

sentence: Mensaje al grupo: tenemos doce sillas y ya confirmaron doce personas; por lo tanto, no podemos aceptar más participantes.
part_of_speech: consecutive connective locution
grammar: Por lo tanto presents the attendance limit as a conclusion drawn from the equal numbers of available chairs and confirmed participants.
register: Neutral written message to a group.
note: Confirmaron means the twelve people confirmed their participation; aceptar más participantes = admit additional participants.

sentence: En mi familia solo tenemos una botella de agua para todo el camino; por eso vamos a racionar el agua hasta llegar al pueblo.
part_of_speech: transitive infinitive
grammar: Racionar means controlling how much of a limited supply is used. Visible por eso links that action to the family's shortage.
register: Ordinary family travel planning.
note: Todo el camino = the entire journey; pueblo = town.

sentence: La vecina abrió las dos ventanas, de modo que entró aire y la cocina dejó de oler a humo.
part_of_speech: consecutive subordinating conjunctive locution
grammar: De modo que introduces an actual result, expressed with indicative entró. The sentence reports what happened after the windows were opened.
register: An everyday account of a household problem.
note: Oler a humo = smell of smoke; dejó de oler = stopped smelling.

sentence: La fila era tan larga que perdí el camión de las seis; no alcancé a subir.
part_of_speech: degree adverb in a consecutive construction
grammar: Tan modifies larga and pairs with que to introduce the consequence of the queue's length. This is a degree-and-result construction, rather than tan ... como equality.
register: Ordinary explanation of missed transport.
note: Fila = queue; no alcancé a subir = I did not manage to board in time.

sentence: Ayer caminamos tanto que hoy nos duelen los pies; hicimos todo el recorrido a pie.
part_of_speech: invariable quantity adverb in a consecutive construction
grammar: Tanto measures the amount of walking and pairs with que to introduce its result. It modifies caminamos and does not agree with pies.
register: An everyday account of a shared outing.
note: A pie = on foot; caminamos is past here because of ayer.

sentence: Recibimos tanta ayuda de los vecinos que terminamos la limpieza antes del mediodía; solos no podíamos hacerlo tan rápido.
part_of_speech: feminine singular quantity determiner in a consecutive construction
grammar: Tanta agrees with feminine singular ayuda. The quantity of help makes the early completion possible, and que introduces that result.
register: Appreciative discussion of neighborhood help.
note: Solos = on our own; tan rápido = so quickly.

sentence: Aviso del paseo: el camión tiene veinte asientos; por consiguiente, el cupo será de veinte personas.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Cupo names the participation limit, rather than the people already registered. Visible por consiguiente presents that limit as a consequence of seating capacity.
register: An ordinary formal announcement about an outing.
note: Por consiguiente = consequently; será de veinte personas = will be twenty people.

sentence: Fui al cumpleaños de mi hermana a pesar de la lluvia; tomé un taxi para no mojarme.
part_of_speech: concessive prepositional locution
grammar: A pesar de introduces the acknowledged obstacle as a noun phrase. The completed visit shows that the rain did not prevent attendance.
register: Ordinary family conversation.
note: Lluvia = rain; mojarme = get wet myself.

sentence: Aunque rechazaron mi primera propuesta, no desisto: mañana voy a presentar otra.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative intransitive verb
grammar: Under visible no, desisto expresses refusing to abandon the effort. Indicative rechazaron presents the rejection as an acknowledged event.
register: A determined response to a rejected proposal.
note: Presentar otra propuesta = put forward another proposal.

sentence: El curso me ayudó a leer mejor; sin embargo, todavía necesito ayuda para escribir mensajes largos.
part_of_speech: adversative connective locution
grammar: Sin embargo adds a limitation without denying the course's benefit: reading improved, while writing still requires help.
register: Neutral assessment of a learning experience.
note: Me ayudó a leer = helped me read; mensajes largos = long messages.

sentence: Hoy estoy cansada y el parque queda lejos; aun así, voy a caminar con mi hermana porque quiero pasar tiempo con ella.
part_of_speech: concessive connective locution
grammar: Aun así introduces a decision maintained despite the previously stated tiredness and distance. Aun has no written accent in this locution.
register: Ordinary personal explanation.
note: Cansada identifies the speaker as female; ella refers to her sister.

sentence: El camión directo tarda cuarenta minutos; en cambio, la ruta con transbordo tarda una hora. Hoy prefiero llegar antes.
part_of_speech: contrastive connective locution
grammar: En cambio compares two travel alternatives on the same dimension: journey time. The second duration is not caused by the first.
register: Ordinary choice between transport options.
note: Tarda = takes, referring to travel time; ruta = route.

sentence: Mi hermana prefiere la ruta más barata, mientras que yo prefiero la más rápida; no estamos de acuerdo.
part_of_speech: contrastive conjunctive locution
grammar: Mientras que contrasts the speaker's preference with the sister's preference. It does not describe two actions occurring during the same time interval.
register: Ordinary discussion between family members.
note: La más rápida refers to the fastest route.

sentence: No necesito dinero, sino ayuda para limpiar el patio; el problema es que no puedo hacerlo todo yo.
part_of_speech: corrective adversative coordinating conjunction
grammar: No ... sino rejects dinero as the needed resource and replaces it with ayuda. The alternatives share necesito.
register: An ordinary clarification of a request.
note: Hacerlo todo yo = do everything myself; patio = patio or yard.

sentence: No cancelé la visita, sino que la pospuse hasta el sábado; todavía quiero ver a mi abuela.
part_of_speech: corrective adversative conjunctive locution introducing a finite clause
grammar: Sino que introduces the replacement finite proposition la pospuse. The denial concerns cancellation, not the narrator's wish to visit.
register: A practical correction about family plans.
note: Pospuse = I postponed, irregular preterite of posponer; la refers to la visita.

sentence: El cuarto es pequeño, pero por lo demás me conviene: está cerca del trabajo y cuesta poco.
part_of_speech: discourse connective locution
grammar: Por lo demás limits the favorable evaluation to the room's other features after its small size has been acknowledged.
register: An ordinary assessment of a housing choice.
note: Cuarto = room; me conviene = suits my needs here.

sentence: Por más que reviso el recibo una y otra vez, no encuentro el cobro doble; la suma coincide con el precio acordado.
part_of_speech: concessive subordinating conjunctive locution
grammar: Por más que introduces repeated effort that is actually occurring, expressed with indicative reviso. That effort does not produce the expected discovery.
register: An ordinary explanation during a billing check.
note: La suma = the total; coincide con = matches; precio acordado = agreed price.

sentence: Aunque mañana llueva, voy a recibir a mis vecinos; comeremos a cubierto en el patio techado.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution
grammar: A cubierto identifies protection from the possible rain. The sheltered location explains why the future visit can proceed despite that obstacle.
register: Ordinary planning for a social meal.
note: Patio techado = roofed patio; recibir a los vecinos = welcome the neighbors.

sentence: —¿Te molestó mi pregunta? —Al contrario, me ayudó a aclarar el malentendido; gracias por hacerla.
part_of_speech: corrective discourse locution
grammar: Al contrario rejects the suggested negative evaluation and supplies its opposite: the question was helpful.
register: A reassuring exchange between familiar speakers.
note: Molestó = bothered; hacerla refers to asking the question.

sentence: Si mañana llega la mesa que compré, invitaremos a mis padres a comer; la tienda todavía no confirma la entrega.
part_of_speech: conditional subordinating conjunction
grammar: Si introduces an open future condition with present indicative llega. Future invitaremos gives the consequence without asserting that the delivery is confirmed.
register: Ordinary household planning.
note: Invitaremos = we will invite; compré = I bought.

sentence: Le digo a mi amiga Ana: «Si te sobra una silla, apártame una para la comida; llegaré tarde».
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached first-person singular indirect-object clitic
grammar: Apártame asks Ana to set a chair aside for the speaker. The request applies only if Ana has a spare chair; me marks the beneficiary.
register: A practical request to a friend addressed with tú.
note: Una refers to una silla; llegaré tarde = I will arrive late.

sentence: Si mi hermana trabaja de noche, duerme por la mañana; ese es su horario de cada semana.
part_of_speech: conditional subordinating conjunction in a habitual construction
grammar: Both clauses use present indicative for a recurring relationship in the sister's weekly schedule, rather than one pending future possibility.
register: An everyday explanation of a family member's routine.
note: De noche = at night; horario = schedule.

sentence: Ana, puedes abrir la ventana si prefieres aire fresco; yo no tengo frío.
part_of_speech: conditional subordinating conjunction qualifying a permission offer
grammar: Si makes the offered permission depend on Ana's preference. The speaker does not assert that Ana prefers fresh air or that the window will be opened.
register: An accommodating offer to a familiar addressee.
note: Aire fresco = fresh, cool air; prefieres = you prefer.

sentence: Ana, trae tu llave; si no la encuentras, yo te prestaré la mía para que puedas entrar.
part_of_speech: conditional conjunction followed by clause negation
grammar: Separate si no negates finding Ana's key and triggers the alternative loan. It is not corrective sino.
register: A practical arrangement with a familiar addressee.
note: La mía refers to the speaker's key; prestaré = I will lend.

sentence: El último camión sale a las ocho. Tenemos que llegar antes; de lo contrario, tendremos que caminar hasta casa.
part_of_speech: conditional-consequence connective locution
grammar: De lo contrario supplies the consequence of not meeting the preceding requirement: failing to arrive before departure means walking home.
register: Ordinary shared travel planning.
note: Tendremos que = we will have to; último camión = last bus.

sentence: Tal vez mi hermano venga mañana; en ese caso, cocinaré para dos, pero todavía no voy a comprar la comida.
part_of_speech: anaphoric conditional connective locution
grammar: En ese caso refers specifically to the possible visit. Cooking for two depends on that circumstance, which is still unconfirmed.
register: Ordinary planning for a possible family visit.
note: Cocinaré = I will cook; para dos = for two people.

sentence: Anoté el número de mi hermana en un papel en caso de perder mi teléfono durante el viaje; ella conoce el itinerario.
part_of_speech: conditional prepositional locution governing an infinitive
grammar: En caso de introduces a contingency through perder. The narrator is both the person who wrote the number down and the possible loser of the phone.
register: Ordinary precautionary travel planning.
note: Anoté = I wrote down; the sister knows the travel itinerary.

sentence: Ana, dejaré una llave de mi casa con mi hermano en caso de que tú llegues antes que yo; él vive al lado y estará ahí toda la tarde.
part_of_speech: conditional subordinating conjunctive locution
grammar: En caso de que introduces Ana's possible earlier arrival through present subjunctive llegues. Its finite clause gives the contingency a different actor from dejaré.
register: A practical arrangement with a familiar visitor.
note: Dejaré = I will leave; al lado = next door; ahí refers to the brother's home.

sentence: Mañana recogeré a mi hermana a las seis, salvo que ella salga antes del trabajo; entonces iré por ella más temprano.
part_of_speech: exceptive conditional subordinating conjunctive locution
grammar: Salvo que marks an exception to the six o'clock pickup time. Present subjunctive salga gives the pending exception; an earlier pickup is the alternative.
register: Ordinary family transport planning.
note: Recogeré = I will pick up; iré por ella = I will go to collect her.

sentence: En nuestra casa cenamos juntos todos los días, excepto si mi papá trabaja de noche; esos días le guardamos su comida.
part_of_speech: exceptive conditional conjunctive expression
grammar: Excepto si identifies the sole stated exception to the family routine. Present indicative trabaja describes the recurring condition.
register: Everyday discussion of a household routine.
note: Le guardamos su comida = we save his meal for him; esos días means the nights when he works.

sentence: Ana, me sumo al paseo del domingo, siempre y cuando regresemos antes de las seis; esa tarde voy a cuidar a mi sobrino.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Me sumo al paseo expresses agreement to join the activity. The commitment is limited by the stated return-time condition.
register: A practical agreement with a familiar addressee.
note: Siempre y cuando = provided that; regresemos = we return, present subjunctive; sobrino = nephew.

sentence: Con una compañera de cuarto, podría compartir gastos y ahorrar dinero; todavía vivo sola.
part_of_speech: masculine plural noun
grammar: Gastos names the living expenses that could be shared. Visible con introduces a contemplated living arrangement, rather than a current companion.
register: Ordinary consideration of a housing choice.
note: Compañera de cuarto = female roommate; ahorrar dinero = save money; sola identifies the narrator as a woman currently living alone.

sentence: Sin la clave, no podré acceder al archivo de la clase; el maestro va a mandármela mañana.
part_of_speech: intransitive infinitive governing a
grammar: Acceder a names gaining access to a digital file. The absence introduced by sin blocks that projected action until the teacher supplies the password.
register: An ordinary explanation about access to class material.
note: Clave = password here; archivo = digital file; mandármela = send it to me, referring to the password.

sentence: Quizá la reparación termine hoy; de ser así, recogeré mi bicicleta mañana. El mecánico todavía no me lo confirma.
part_of_speech: conditional infinitival locution
grammar: De ser así makes the next step depend on the explicitly uncertain proposition that the repair will finish today.
register: Neutral practical planning.
note: Mecánico = mechanic; lo refers to completion of the repair today.

sentence: Quizá el salón esté libre a las ocho; de no ser así, nos reuniremos en el patio.
meaning: if that is not the case
part_of_speech: negative conditional infinitival locution
grammar: De no ser así negates the preceding possibility that the room will be available at eight and introduces the alternative meeting location.
register: Neutral planning for a group meeting.
note: Libre = available or unoccupied here; nos reuniremos = we will meet.

sentence: No sé si la biblioteca abrirá mañana; si abre, estudiaré ahí, y si no, estudiaré en casa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular simple future indicative verb
grammar: Abrirá belongs to an indirect yes-or-no question after no sé si. The later conditional si abre uses present indicative for its future condition.
register: An ordinary explanation of alternative study plans.
note: Biblioteca = library; estudiaré = I will study; ahí refers to the library.

sentence: Si ya pagué el boleto y aquí está el recibo, ¿por qué me cobra otra vez, señor?
part_of_speech: conditional conjunction introducing an asserted factual premise
grammar: Si presents the speaker's completed payment as a factual premise supporting the question. The visible receipt supplies evidence; the payment is not an unreal hypothesis.
register: A respectful but questioning service interaction with usted.
note: Me cobra = you charge me, addressing señor; ya pagué = I already paid.

sentence: Voy a llevar una chamarra por si refresca durante el paseo; ahora hace calor, pero vamos a volver de noche.
part_of_speech: precautionary subordinating conjunctive locution
grammar: Por si introduces a possible circumstance motivating an advance precaution. The jacket will be taken before anyone knows whether cooler weather will occur.
register: Ordinary preparation for an outing.
note: Refresca = the weather gets cooler; de noche = at night.

sentence: Ya guardé el boleto en mi teléfono, pero también imprimí una copia por si acaso; puede fallar la pantalla al entrar.
part_of_speech: adverbial precautionary locution
grammar: Por si acaso presents the printed copy as a backup. The following statement identifies the possible problem without asserting that the screen will fail.
register: Ordinary preparation for showing a ticket at an entrance.
note: Imprimí = I printed; al entrar = when entering; una copia is a paper copy here.

sentence: Ana es lista: usó un espejo para leer la etiqueta detrás del mueble; todavía no está preparada para salir.
part_of_speech: feminine singular adjective
grammar: Lista with ser describes resourcefulness demonstrated by Ana's solution. The separate estar preparada clause concerns readiness.
note: Espejo = mirror; etiqueta = label; detrás del mueble = behind the piece of furniture; preparada = ready.

sentence: Luis es inteligente, pero todavía no está listo para afrontar su primera entrevista de trabajo: necesita practicar las respuestas.
part_of_speech: transitive infinitive
grammar: Afrontar names dealing with a challenging event. Visible estar listo para concerns preparation for that event, independently of intelligence.
note: Entrevista de trabajo = job interview; practicar las respuestas = rehearse the answers.

sentence: Mi sobrina es muy viva: entiende las bromas enseguida y siempre inventa otra para responder.
part_of_speech: feminine singular adjective
grammar: Viva characterizes the niece's mental quickness, illustrated by understanding and answering jokes.
note: Sobrina = niece; broma = joke; inventa otra = invents another one.

sentence: El rosal parecía muerto después del viaje, pero está vivo: hoy tiene una hoja nueva.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Vivo with estar describes the plant's living state. Its new leaf contradicts the earlier appearance of death.
note: Rosal = rosebush; muerto = dead; hoja = leaf.

sentence: Esta caja es segura para transportar vasos: su tapa queda fija con dos cierres.
part_of_speech: feminine singular adjective
grammar: Segura characterizes the box's suitability for carrying glasses. The secured lid supplies the practical basis.
note: Transportar = transport; tapa = lid; queda fija = stays secured; cierres = clasps here.

sentence: Estoy seguro de que Ana ya llegó: la veo en la entrada junto a su bicicleta.
part_of_speech: governed preposition and complementizer after seguro
grammar: Estar seguro de que retains de before the finite proposition expressing what the speaker is certain about.
note: Seguro here means certain. The speaker directly sees Ana at the entrance.

sentence: Mi vecino es atento: siempre le ofrece una silla a mi abuela y le pregunta si necesita ayuda.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Atento with ser characterizes considerate treatment through the neighbor's repeated actions.
note: Both instances of le refer to the grandmother, who receives the offer and the question.

sentence: Ana está atenta a la señal del maestro: tiene la mano sobre el botón y espera la luz verde para empezar.
part_of_speech: feminine singular adjective
grammar: Estar atento a directs attention toward a specified signal. Ana's hand position and waiting activity establish the current focus.
note: Señal = signal; botón = button; la luz verde is the signal to begin.

sentence: Raúl es interesado: solo le hace favores a Julia cuando necesita pedirle dinero; el resto del tiempo ni la saluda.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Interesado with ser evaluates motivation. The favor-for-benefit pattern and lack of other contact establish the intended criticism.
register: A critical description of someone's social behavior.
note: Hacerle favores a alguien = do someone favors; pedirle dinero = ask that person for money.

sentence: Estoy interesada en el taller de cerámica porque quiero hacer mis propias tazas; no espero vender nada.
part_of_speech: feminine singular adjective
grammar: Estar interesado en names interest directed toward an activity. The en complement identifies the pottery workshop.
note: Taller de cerámica = pottery workshop; mis propias tazas = my own cups.

sentence: El discurso del director es aburrido: repite las mismas cifras y nadie del público sigue el tema.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Aburrido describes the speech as causing lack of interest. The speech is not an experiencer of boredom.
note: Discurso = speech; cifras = figures; público = audience; seguir el tema = follow the topic.

sentence: Mis amigos se ríen con mis historias, pero ahora estoy aburrido: espero solo en una sala sin libros ni teléfono.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative copular verb
grammar: Estoy aburrido presents the speaker as experiencing boredom during this wait. It does not characterize him as someone who bores his friends.
note: Se ríen con mis historias = they laugh at my stories; solo = alone; sala = room here.

sentence: Este juego es entretenido: mis primos y yo nos reímos y nadie quiere dejar de jugar.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Entretenido characterizes the game as producing enjoyment, supported by the participants' reactions.
note: Primos = cousins; nos reímos = we laugh; dejar de jugar = stop playing.

sentence: La tele está encendida, pero mi papá está entretenido con un rompecabezas: busca una pieza azul y no mira la pantalla.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Estar entretenido con describes the father's current absorption in an activity. The search for a piece makes that activity explicit.
register: Tele is an everyday shortening of televisión.
note: Encendida = switched on; rompecabezas = jigsaw puzzle; pieza azul = blue piece.

sentence: Mi hermano es orgulloso: reconoce sus errores en privado, pero nunca pide disculpas porque dice que eso lo hace parecer débil.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Orgulloso characterizes a disposition that prevents apologies. The brother's stated reason establishes pride rather than satisfaction with an achievement.
register: A critical personal description.
note: En privado = privately; pedir disculpas = apologize; eso lo hace parecer débil = that makes him seem weak, with lo referring to the brother.

sentence: Estoy orgullosa de mi hija: aprendió a leer y hoy nos leyó un cuento completo.
part_of_speech: feminine singular adjective
grammar: Estar orgulloso de expresses satisfaction concerning a specified person or achievement. The daughter's reading achievement supplies the reason.
note: Orgullosa identifies the speaker as a woman; cuento completo = complete story; nos includes the speaker and other listeners.

sentence: Mi tío es rico: vive de las rentas de cinco casas y no necesita trabajar.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Rico has a financial interpretation established by income from several houses. This selected ser construction characterizes the uncle's wealth.
note: Vivir de las rentas = live on rental income.

sentence: Ana, tu mole está rico, como para chuparse los dedos; lo acabo de probar y ya quiero más.
part_of_speech: infinitive with attached reflexive affected-possessor clitic
grammar: Chuparse los dedos supplies an idiomatic image of licking one's own fingers to praise delicious food. Se identifies the fingers as the eater's own.
register: Informal enthusiastic food praise.
note: Como para chuparse los dedos = good enough to lick your fingers; mole is the prepared dish being tasted.

sentence: Dormir con la tele prendida es malo para mi descanso: me despierta varias veces durante la noche.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Malo para evaluates the practice's unfavorable effect on the speaker's rest. It does not describe someone's illness or moral character.
register: Prendida is ordinary Mexican-compatible wording for switched on.
note: Me despierta = it wakes me; descanso here means rest.

sentence: El control está malo: ayer funcionaba y hoy no responde, ni con pilas nuevas.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative copular verb
grammar: Está malo describes the remote's current malfunction. Yesterday's operation and today's failure establish the intended device-state interpretation.
register: An everyday household complaint.
note: Control = remote control here; no responde = does not respond; pilas = batteries.

sentence: Mi vecina es buena: encontró una cartera con dinero y buscó a su dueño para devolvérsela completa.
part_of_speech: feminine singular adjective
grammar: Buena evaluates the neighbor's character through an act benefiting someone else. It does not evaluate food flavor.
note: Cartera = wallet; devolverla completa means return it with all its contents.

sentence: Acabo de probar el arroz: está bueno y en su punto, suave pero no deshecho.
part_of_speech: predicative prepositional locution
grammar: En su punto evaluates the achieved cooking state. The visible contrast between soft and mushy identifies what is just right here.
note: Suave = soft; deshecho = mushy or falling apart in this food context.

sentence: Esta caja de libros es pesada: pesa veinte kilos y el carrito solo admite diez.
part_of_speech: feminine singular adjective
grammar: Pesada describes physical weight. The box's weight exceeds the cart's stated capacity.
note: Pesa = weighs; carrito = small cart; diez refers to ten kilos of carrying capacity.

sentence: Hoy estás pesado, Luis: interrumpes cada respuesta y repites la misma broma; normalmente escuchas con paciencia.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Pesado evaluates Luis's behavior during this interaction. The usual patient behavior makes the current departure explicit.
register: Familiar tú address with a direct, mildly critical complaint.
note: Interrumpes = you interrupt; repites = you repeat; con paciencia = patiently.

sentence: Esta variedad de pera es verde incluso madura: conserva ese color cuando ya está dulce y suave.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative transitive verb
grammar: Conserva describes retaining a property through ripening. Visible verde identifies the variety's color, independently of ripeness.
note: Variedad de pera = pear variety; madura = ripe; suave = soft.

sentence: Este aguacate está verde: sigue duro y todavía no sirve para hacer guacamole; el otro ya maduró aunque tiene la cáscara del mismo color.
part_of_speech: singular adjective
grammar: Verde with estar describes insufficient ripeness. The equally colored but ripe comparison fruit prevents a simple color interpretation.
note: Aguacate = avocado; duro = hard; maduró = ripened; cáscara = peel.

sentence: Mi hija es madura: antes de gastar sus ahorros comparó los precios y reservó dinero para el camión.
part_of_speech: feminine singular adjective
grammar: Madura characterizes sound personal judgment, illustrated by comparing prices and protecting money needed for transportation.
note: Ahorros = savings; reservó dinero = set money aside; camión = bus here.

sentence: El mango está maduro: su pulpa está suave y dulce, así que ya puedo cortarlo para la ensalada.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Maduro with estar identifies the fruit's ripeness for the stated use. Softness and sweetness establish the intended interpretation.
note: Pulpa = fruit flesh; cortarlo = cut it; ensalada = salad.

sentence: El mueble es blanco de fábrica; esa capa gris que ves es polvo, no pintura.
part_of_speech: prepositional locution of manufacturing origin
grammar: De fábrica identifies white as the manufactured finish. The gray surface layer is a later deposit of dust.
note: Capa gris = gray layer; polvo = dust; pintura = paint.

sentence: Pablo está blanco del susto; su hermana acaba de salir de detrás de la puerta con una máscara y él aún no recupera el color de la cara.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Blanco describes visible loss of facial color following a surprise. It does not identify skin color or diagnose a condition.
note: Susto = fright; máscara = mask; recuperar el color de la cara = regain one's facial color.

sentence: Este colchón es nuevo de paquete; el otro está impecable, pero ya tuvo dueño.
part_of_speech: adjectival prepositional locution
grammar: De paquete reinforces that the mattress is genuinely new, contrasting with a preowned mattress whose clean condition only looks new.
register: Everyday emphatic description of a genuinely new item.
note: Colchón = mattress; impecable = spotless or in excellent condition; tuvo dueño = had an owner.

sentence: Este sillón tiene diez años, pero está nuevo: no tiene manchas ni la tela gastada; casi nunca lo usamos.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Nuevo with estar evaluates condition despite the armchair's stated age. It does not claim recent manufacture.
register: Conversational praise of an older item's condition.
note: Sillón = armchair; tela gastada = worn fabric; casi nunca = hardly ever.

sentence: Este reloj es viejo: mi bisabuelo lo compró hace cien años, pero funciona bien y no tiene daños.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Viejo characterizes the timepiece's chronological age. Its good operation and lack of damage separately establish its condition.
note: Bisabuelo = great-grandfather; daños = damage; reloj can mean a clock or a watch.

sentence: Mi mochila apenas tiene seis meses, pero ya está vieja: la tela tiene agujeros y las correas están gastadas.
part_of_speech: feminine singular adjective
grammar: Vieja with estar evaluates deterioration despite the backpack's stated age of only six months. Holes and worn straps establish the condition reading.
note: Apenas = only here; mochila = backpack; agujeros = holes; correas = straps.

sentence: Mi maestra es abierta: escucha propuestas distintas a la suya y cambia de opinión cuando un alumno le da una buena razón.
part_of_speech: feminine singular adjective
grammar: Abierta describes willingness to consider other people's ideas. Listening and revising an opinion make the interpretation visible.
note: La suya refers to the teacher's own proposal; cambiar de opinión = change one's mind.

sentence: La biblioteca normalmente exige credencial, pero hoy está abierta al público: cualquier vecino puede entrar a ver la exposición.
part_of_speech: prepositional complement with contracted a plus el
grammar: Abierta al público specifies who currently has access. The normal credential requirement contrasts with today's admission of any neighbor.
note: Credencial = membership card here; exposición = exhibition; cualquier vecino = any neighbor.

sentence: Mi compañero es cerrado: solo acepta su propio plan y ni siquiera escucha la alternativa que le propone el grupo.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Cerrado characterizes refusal to consider alternatives. The specific planning exchange supplies the basis for the evaluation.
register: A critical description of someone's behavior in a planning disagreement.
note: Su propio plan = his own plan; ni siquiera = not even; alternativa = alternative.

sentence: El acuerdo sobre el precio ya está cerrado: el comprador y la vendedora lo aceptaron y no van a negociar más.
part_of_speech: masculine singular participial adjective
grammar: Cerrado describes the settled state of the price agreement. Both parties have accepted it and plan no further negotiation.
note: Comprador = buyer; vendedora = female seller; negociar = negotiate.

sentence: Mi sobrino es despierto: notó una gota bajo la llave y buscó la fuga antes que los adultos.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Despierto characterizes perception of a relevant clue and a prompt response. The nephew noticed the drop and looked for the leak before the adults did.
note: Gota = drop; llave = faucet here; fuga = leak. Antes que los adultos compares when they looked for the leak.

sentence: Mi hermano es muy perceptivo, pero anoche no estaba despierto: roncaba en el sillón mientras yo contaba un chiste.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Despierto with estar describes a wakefulness state. Snoring establishes that the brother was asleep, independently of his perceptive character.
note: Perceptivo = perceptive; roncaba = was snoring; contar un chiste = tell a joke.

sentence: Este florero es delicado: el vidrio es muy delgado, así que lo guardo separado de las ollas para evitar golpes.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Delicado characterizes an object's fragility. Thin glass and protection from knocks establish the handling interpretation.
register: Neutral household explanation.
note: Florero = vase; vidrio delgado = thin glass; guardo = I store or put away here; ollas = cooking pots; golpes = knocks.

sentence: Mi abuelo está delicado estos días: se cansa al conversar y hoy prefirió una visita corta; normalmente platica durante horas.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Delicado with estar describes the grandfather's current fragile wellbeing. His usual long conversations provide the comparison.
register: A restrained family account of someone's wellbeing.
note: Platicar = chat; se cansa al conversar = gets tired while talking.

sentence: La explicación de Julia es clara: presenta los pasos en orden y muestra un ejemplo de cada uno; pude seguirla sin hacer preguntas.
part_of_speech: feminine singular adjective
grammar: Clara evaluates how understandable the explanation is. Ordered steps and examples establish the wording-related interpretation.
register: Neutral praise of an explanation.
note: Presenta = sets out here; seguirla = follow it, referring to the explanation.

sentence: El recibo marca dos boletos y solo tengo uno; está claro que falta un boleto, aunque todavía no sé dónde quedó.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective in an impersonal evaluative frame
grammar: Está claro que presents the missing ticket as evident from the receipt and the actual count. Its location remains unknown.
register: Neutral reasoning about a purchase discrepancy.
note: Marca = indicates here; dónde quedó = where it ended up.

sentence: La explicación de Raúl es oscura: usa palabras que no define y cambia de tema sin explicar la relación; voy a pedirle un ejemplo.
part_of_speech: feminine singular adjective
grammar: Oscura describes an explanation whose meaning is hard to follow. Undefined terms and unexplained topic changes supply the evidence.
register: A critical evaluation of an explanation.
note: Define = defines; cambiar de tema = change the subject; relación = connection here.

sentence: Anoche el cuarto estaba oscuro y no veía el apagador; lo busqué a tientas, pasando los dedos por la pared junto a la puerta.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution of manner
grammar: A tientas describes searching through touch because sight is insufficient. The room's darkness explains why touch is needed.
register: Everyday account of a household action.
note: Apagador = light switch in Mexican usage; no veía = I couldn't see; pasando los dedos por la pared = running one's fingers along the wall.

sentence: Mi primo es muy fresco: llega a comer sin avisar, pide el plato más caro y espera que yo pague su parte.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Fresco criticizes the cousin's presumptuous behavior. Arriving unannounced and expecting someone else to pay establish this personal sense.
register: Familiar, disapproving description of a relative's behavior.
note: Sin avisar = without letting anyone know; su parte = his share of the bill.

sentence: El pan todavía está fresco: lo horneé hace una hora y la miga sigue suave, nada reseca.
part_of_speech: feminine singular adjective
grammar: Reseca describes a dried-out texture and agrees with miga. Nada denies that condition emphatically; the bread's soft interior supports its current freshness.
register: Everyday description of recently baked bread.
note: Hornear = bake; miga = the soft inner part of bread; suave = soft here; nada reseca = not at all dried out.

sentence: Mi tío es frío con la familia: cuando le contamos una buena noticia, responde «Está bien» y cambia de tema sin mostrar alegría.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Frío characterizes emotional distance in a recurring family response. It does not describe physical temperature.
register: A critical but restrained description of family interaction.
note: Tío = uncle; mostrar alegría = show happiness.

sentence: Hoy el trato entre mi vecino y yo está frío: apenas nos saludamos, aunque normalmente platicamos mucho; ayer discutimos por el ruido.
meaning: interaction; manner of treating one another
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Trato names how the neighbors interact. Frío evaluates that interaction today; their usual conversations and yesterday's argument establish the contrast.
register: Everyday account of tension between neighbors.
note: Apenas nos saludamos = we barely greet each other; discutimos = we argued here.

sentence: Mi hermana es decidida: compara las opciones, elige una y empieza a actuar sin esperar la aprobación de todos.
part_of_speech: feminine singular adjective
grammar: Decidida characterizes a person's readiness to make choices and act. It does not identify a matter as already settled.
register: Neutral positive description of someone's character.
note: Opciones = options; actuar = act; aprobación = approval.

sentence: El lugar de la fiesta ya está decidido: todos aceptamos el patio de Rosa y ella confirmó que podemos usarlo.
part_of_speech: masculine singular participial adjective
grammar: Decidido describes the settled state of the venue choice. Agreement and Rosa's confirmation that the patio can be used establish the decision.
register: Neutral coordination of a social event.
note: Lugar = venue here; usarlo refers to Rosa's patio.

sentence: Soy consciente de que llegar tarde afecta al grupo: todos tienen que esperarme, así que hoy voy a salir más temprano.
part_of_speech: singular adjective
grammar: Consciente de que introduces an implication the speaker recognizes. The group must wait when the speaker arrives late.
register: A personal acknowledgment of the effect of one's behavior.
note: Afectar al grupo = affect the group; esperarme = wait for me.

sentence: Después de la siesta, Luis está plenamente consciente: ya sigue la conversación y contesta con atención, aunque todavía tiene sueño.
part_of_speech: singular adjective
grammar: Consciente with estar describes present mental alertness. Following the conversation and answering attentively distinguish this from merely knowing an implication.
register: An everyday observation after a nap.
note: Siesta = nap; plenamente = fully; seguir la conversación = follow the conversation.

sentence: Marta, eres libre de elegir tu carrera; tu familia puede aconsejarte, pero la decisión te corresponde.
meaning: free to make your own choice
part_of_speech: singular adjective
grammar: Libre de elegir expresses autonomy over a choice. The family's advisory role does not transfer the decision to them.
register: Supportive familiar address to a person choosing a field of study.
note: Carrera = degree program here; aconsejarte = advise you; te corresponde = falls to you.

sentence: El puesto de tesorero del club está libre desde que Raúl renunció; todavía no elegimos a otra persona.
part_of_speech: singular adjective
grammar: Libre describes an unoccupied role available to another person. Raúl's departure and the absence of a replacement establish the vacancy.
register: Neutral discussion of a club responsibility.
note: Puesto = position; tesorero = treasurer; renunció = stepped down.

sentence: Estoy pendiente de la respuesta de mi vecina: aún no confirma si puede cuidar al gato y reviso el teléfono cada rato.
part_of_speech: singular adjective with governed preposition
grammar: Estar pendiente de describes active attention to an unresolved response. The speaker repeatedly checks the phone.
register: Everyday coordination between neighbors.
note: Cada rato = frequently; gato = cat; si introduces what the neighbor has not confirmed.

sentence: Estoy conforme con el reparto de tareas que propuso mi hermana: ella cocina y yo lavo los platos; así trabajamos lo mismo.
part_of_speech: singular adjective
grammar: Conforme con expresses acceptance of a specified arrangement. The speaker considers the proposed division of work balanced.
register: Neutral agreement in household planning.
note: Reparto de tareas = division of tasks; trabajamos lo mismo = we do equal amounts of work.

sentence: Estoy dispuesto a ayudar con la mudanza el sábado, aunque tendré que cancelar mi paseo; todavía no empezamos.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Dispuesto a plus infinitive expresses willingness to undertake an action. The move has not started, and the willingness involves a stated sacrifice.
register: A personal offer of help.
note: Tendré que = I will have to; paseo = leisure outing here.

sentence: La elección del menú es ajena a mis funciones: yo acomodo las mesas y la cocinera decide qué se sirve.
part_of_speech: feminine singular adjective
grammar: Ajena a excludes menu selection from the speaker's duties. The cook's decision-making role remains explicit.
register: Neutral clarification of responsibilities.
note: Elección = selection; funciones = duties; acomodo = arrange here.

sentence: Ana me autorizó a hablar por ella en la reunión: puedo comunicar su rechazo al horario, pero no aceptar cambios en su nombre.
part_of_speech: preposition marking represented speaker
grammar: Hablar por alguien represents that person's position. Ana authorizes communication of her rejection but withholds authority to accept changes.
register: Explicitly limited representation in a group discussion.
note: Autorizó = authorized; rechazo = rejection; en su nombre = on her behalf.

sentence: Tenemos doscientos pesos; el dinero nos da para comprar los cuatro boletos de cincuenta que necesitamos.
part_of_speech: preposition introducing the capacity complement of dar
grammar: Dar para plus infinitive expresses resource sufficiency. Two hundred pesos covers exactly four tickets costing fifty each.
register: Everyday calculation for a shared purchase.
note: El dinero nos da = the money is enough for us; de cincuenta = costing fifty pesos each.

sentence: Tenía a mi vecino por antipático: nunca saludaba; hoy conversamos y descubrí que solo es tímido.
part_of_speech: preposition introducing an attributed property with tener
grammar: Tener a alguien por plus adjective means considering someone to have that quality. Conversation leads the speaker to revise the judgment.
register: Everyday correction of a personal impression.
note: Antipático = unfriendly; tímido = shy; tenía a mi vecino por = I considered my neighbor to be.

sentence: Clara dijo para sus adentros, sin hablar ni mover los labios: «Esto va a costar más».
part_of_speech: prepositional locution of internal speech
grammar: Para sus adentros locates the words in Clara's private thought. Sus refers to Clara; nobody is addressed.
register: A narrative expression for unspoken thought.
note: Adentros is a plural noun referring to inner thought; mover los labios = move one's lips.

sentence: El club de lectura La Esquina pide la solicitud por duplicado: una copia para quien la entrega y otra para el archivo del club.
part_of_speech: adverbial prepositional locution
grammar: Por duplicado requires two copies of the same document. Their separate destinations explain the two-copy requirement.
register: An administrative arrangement at a fictional reading club.
note: Solicitud = application form; archivo = records or files here.

sentence: Este papel es apto para imprimir por ambos lados: la tinta no pasa de una cara a la otra.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective
grammar: Apto para identifies suitability for a task. The explicit criterion is that ink does not pass through the paper.
register: Neutral evaluation of a material for a practical task.
note: Imprimir = print; tinta = ink; cara = side or surface here.

sentence: Di mi anillo por perdido tras buscarlo toda la tarde, pero apareció dentro de un zapato.
part_of_speech: prepositional predicative complement with masculine singular participial adjective
grammar: Dar algo por perdido treats it as presumed irrecoverable. Finding the ring afterward shows that the presumption was not confirmation.
register: Everyday account of a reversed assumption.
note: Anillo = ring; tras = after; apareció = turned up.

sentence: Por acuerdo del club, tenemos mil pesos presupuestados para pintar el salón el próximo enero; la cantidad aparece en el presupuesto, pero todavía no la gastamos.
part_of_speech: masculine plural participial adjective
grammar: Presupuestados agrees with pesos and identifies budget inclusion. Para names the future use; por acuerdo identifies the basis for the arrangement.
register: Neutral discussion of a club budget.
note: Presupuesto = budget; salón = hall; gastar = spend; la refers to the amount.

sentence: El club nos presta el salón por tiempo indefinido: no fijamos una fecha de devolución, pero el club puede pedirlo de vuelta.
meaning: for an unspecified length of time
part_of_speech: temporal prepositional locution
grammar: Por tiempo indefinido leaves the end date unspecified. The club's right to request the hall back excludes guaranteed permanence.
register: Neutral explanation of a fictional club arrangement.
note: Fijar una fecha = set a date; devolución = return.

sentence: Reparar la silla toma dos horas, pero acordé con su dueña devolverla a más tardar el viernes a las seis.
part_of_speech: adverbial deadline locution
grammar: A más tardar sets the latest agreed return time. Two hours separately measures the repair's duration.
register: A practical agreement with an item's owner.
note: Toma dos horas = takes two hours; acordé con = agreed with; dueña = female owner.

sentence: Buscamos al gato por los alrededores de la casa, solo en las dos calles cercanas; todavía no revisamos el resto del barrio.
part_of_speech: locative prepositional phrase
grammar: Por los alrededores identifies the surrounding search area. The two nearby streets bound the search without naming an exact spot.
register: Everyday account of a neighborhood search.
note: Alrededores = surrounding area; resto del barrio = rest of the neighborhood.

sentence: Yo estoy en la entrada del parque; Ana ya camina para acá desde la fuente, pero todavía está lejos.
part_of_speech: directional prepositional phrase
grammar: Para acá directs movement toward the speaker's area. The stated distance shows that Ana has not arrived.
register: Everyday coordination at a public meeting place.
note: Parque = park; fuente = fountain; acá refers to the entrance where the speaker is.

sentence: Para salir del jardín, pasamos por entre las mesas y las sillas; había muebles a ambos lados de nuestro camino.
part_of_speech: combined route-preposition sequence
grammar: Por entre describes a route among intervening objects. Furniture on both sides establishes movement through the gaps.
register: Neutral account of a walking route.
note: Jardín = garden; muebles = furniture items; camino = path here.

sentence: Para mi gusto, el mural tiene demasiados colores; prefiero diseños más sencillos, aunque a mis vecinos les encanta.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Gusto names the speaker's aesthetic preference in para mi gusto. The neighbors' different reaction keeps the evaluation explicitly subjective.
register: An ordinary opinion about neighborhood art.
note: Mural = mural; diseños sencillos = simple designs; demasiados = too many.

sentence: A juzgar por las sillas mojadas del patio, parece que llovió durante la noche; yo estaba dormido y no vi la lluvia.
part_of_speech: evidential locution
grammar: A juzgar por identifies indirect evidence supporting an inference. Parece and the lack of direct observation preserve its inferential status.
register: Neutral evidence-based conjecture.
note: Mojadas = wet; llovió = it rained; dormido = asleep.

sentence: El celular funciona bastante bien para lo que costó: pagué muy poco y puedo hacer todas las llamadas que necesito.
part_of_speech: evaluative preposition followed by a neuter relative expression
grammar: Para lo que introduces a benchmark expressed by the finite clause costó. Performance exceeds expectations associated with the low price.
register: Everyday evaluation of an inexpensive purchase.
note: Celular = cell phone; bastante bien = quite well; costó = it cost.

sentence: No sabemos si vamos a reparar la bicicleta o comprar otra; por lo pronto, usaremos la de mi hermana y decidiremos el domingo.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution of provisional scope
grammar: Por lo pronto limits the borrowing choice to an interim measure while a later decision remains open. Pronto does not mean soon here.
register: Everyday planning while comparing alternatives.
note: La de mi hermana = my sister's bicycle; usaremos = we will use; decidiremos = we will decide.

sentence: La reunión era el lunes; la aplazamos para el jueves y todos vamos a asistir ese día.
part_of_speech: preposition introducing a rescheduled event date
grammar: Aplazar para introduces the new date on which the event will occur. Ese día confirms Thursday as the event date.
register: Neutral coordination of a changed meeting date.
note: Aplazamos = we postponed; ese día refers to Thursday.

sentence: El cuaderno está por encuadernar: las hojas ya están impresas y ordenadas, pero siguen sueltas; mañana yo las uniré con una cubierta.
meaning: bind into a book or notebook
part_of_speech: infinitive verb
grammar: Encuadernar names binding pages together with a cover. The visible estar por frame marks this unperformed action with el cuaderno as its patient subject.
register: Neutral account of a notebook's preparation.
note: Hojas sueltas = loose pages; impresas = printed; cubierta = cover; uniré = I will join.

sentence: El paquete ya está para salir: tiene la etiqueta; el chofer lo tiene en la mano y solo espera la señal de salida.
part_of_speech: preposition in the readiness construction estar para plus infinitive
grammar: Estar para salir presents actual readiness for imminent departure. Labeling is complete and the driver holds the package, awaiting only the signal.
register: Neutral coordination of a delivery.
note: Chofer = driver; señal de salida = departure signal; lo refers to the package.

sentence: La mesa grande bloqueaba el paso; la sustituimos por una plegable, que ahora usamos y guardamos después de comer.
part_of_speech: preposition introducing the replacement after sustituir
grammar: In sustituir X por Y, X is removed from use and Y takes its place. La refers to the large table; una plegable is the replacement.
note: Bloquear el paso = obstruct the way; una plegable = a folding table.

sentence: Ana, para ser franco, no quiero compartir el departamento contigo: necesito silencio de noche y tú ensayas con tu grupo de música hasta tarde.
part_of_speech: masculine singular adjective in a candid-stance formula
grammar: Para ser franco introduces the male speaker's candid opinion. It frames an unwelcome refusal rather than stating a future goal.
register: Familiar tú address; a direct refusal supported by reasons.
note: Departamento = apartment; ensayar = rehearse; hasta tarde = until late.

sentence: En mi familia tenemos por costumbre llamar antes de visitar a alguien; así sabemos si tiene tiempo y evitamos interrumpir.
part_of_speech: preposition in tener por costumbre plus infinitive
grammar: Tener por costumbre introduces a habitual practice directly followed by an infinitive. This frame uses por costumbre rather than la costumbre de.
note: Evitar interrumpir = avoid interrupting; alguien = someone.

sentence: El cambio de horario fue para bien: ahora mi hermano llega a cenar con nosotros y ya no come solo a medianoche.
part_of_speech: adverbial locution evaluating a beneficial outcome
grammar: Para bien evaluates the completed change through its actual improvement. It does not merely identify an intended purpose.
note: Cambio de horario = schedule change; come solo = eats alone.

sentence: Yo respondo por el texto que escribí: revisé cada dato; del resto del boletín no puedo opinar, pues no lo he leído.
part_of_speech: preposition introducing the contribution assumed as one's responsibility
grammar: Responder por introduces the text for which the speaker takes responsibility. The claim is expressly limited to the contribution personally written and checked.
register: An accountable statement among bulletin contributors.
note: Boletín = bulletin; cada dato = every factual detail; el resto = the remainder; pues introduces the reason here.

sentence: Marta guardó la noticia para sí; su hermana le preguntó qué pasaba, pero Marta no contó nada.
part_of_speech: prepositional phrase with a tonic reflexive pronoun
grammar: Sí refers back to Marta, the subject who keeps the news. Guardar la noticia para sí means retaining it privately rather than passing it to a different recipient.
note: Guardar una noticia para sí = keep news to oneself; Marta is explicitly the person who withholds it.

sentence: Ana y yo llegamos a la misma panadería por pura coincidencia; no quedamos de vernos y cada quien salió de su casa a comprar pan.
part_of_speech: feminine singular intensifying adjective
grammar: Pura intensifies coincidencia: chance alone explains the matching arrivals. It agrees with feminine coincidencia and does not describe material purity.
note: Por pura coincidencia = by sheer coincidence; panadería = bakery; cada quien = each person.

sentence: Mi hermana llegará a cenar a las ocho; necesito tener la sopa lista para cuando llegue, aunque todavía no empiezo a cocinar.
part_of_speech: temporal preposition-plus-conjunction sequence
grammar: Para cuando introduces the pending event by which the soup must already be ready. Llegue is present subjunctive because the arrival remains future.
note: Lista agrees with sopa; both llegará and llegue refer to the sister's arrival.

sentence: Todavía no veo el sillón que vende Luis; por muy cómodo que sea, prefiero conservar el mío porque no tengo dinero para otro.
part_of_speech: concessive adjective-degree marker
grammar: Por muy cómodo que sea concedes any possible degree of comfort without changing the choice. Sea presents the unassessed quality within this concessive frame.
note: Sillón = armchair; el mío refers to the speaker's own armchair.

sentence: Dormí mal y acabo de perder mi cartera; Ana, hoy no estoy para bromas.
part_of_speech: preposition in the idiomatic receptiveness construction no estar para bromas
grammar: No estar para bromas expresses current unwillingness to receive jokes. Poor sleep and the lost wallet explain the speaker's mood.
register: A familiar, firm request for a serious interaction.
note: Cartera = wallet; bromas = jokes.

sentence: Puedo quedarme en casa o salir a caminar; estoy por salir, pero aún no decido y sigo sentado.
part_of_speech: preposition in personal estar por plus infinitive
grammar: Estoy por salir expresses the speaker's inclination toward one optional action. The competing choice and continued sitting exclude an already completed departure or a pending patient-task reading.
note: Aún no decido = I have not decided yet; sigo sentado = I remain seated.

sentence: Ayer el vecino puso música hasta las dos y hoy, para variar, empezó otra vez a medianoche; ya me cansé de no poder dormir.
part_of_speech: ironic discourse locution expressing unwelcome repetition
grammar: Para variar ironically comments on another occurrence of the same nuisance. Yesterday's late music and today's renewed music establish repetition rather than an intentional change.
register: Informal complaint with explicit irony.
note: Poner música = play music; me cansé de = I am fed up with here.

sentence: La vecina dice que vio un camión de mudanzas frente a la casa de Luis; por lo visto, él se va a mudar, aunque no he hablado con él.
part_of_speech: evidential discourse locution
grammar: Por lo visto marks an inference from the neighbor's report. The speaker explicitly lacks confirmation from Luis.
note: Camión de mudanzas = moving truck; mudarse = move home.

sentence: Perdí el camión y, para colmo, empezó a llover; llegué a la reunión tarde y con la ropa mojada.
part_of_speech: additive evaluative discourse locution
grammar: Para colmo adds the rain as a further unwelcome circumstance after the missed bus. Both problems contribute to the unpleasant arrival.
note: La ropa mojada = wet clothes; empezó a llover = it began to rain.

sentence: Cancelaron el concierto que quería ver, pero por lo menos pude pasar la tarde con mi hermana; casi nunca tenemos tiempo de platicar.
part_of_speech: consolatory evaluative discourse phrase
grammar: Por lo menos identifies an actual positive aspect despite the disappointment. It does not set a numerical lower bound.
register: Everyday Mexican-compatible personal conversation.
note: Platicar = chat; casi nunca = hardly ever.

sentence: No apoyo la idea de reunirnos en ese café: para empezar, cierra antes de que Luis salga del trabajo; además, casi no hay espacio.
part_of_speech: discourse phrase introducing a first argument
grammar: Para empezar opens the first reason against the proposal. Además introduces another reason, making the argumentative function explicit.
note: Apoyar una idea = support an idea; espacio = room or space.

sentence: Ana y Luis todavía no deciden si van a ayudar en la comida del barrio; por mi parte, llevaré el arroz y lavaré los platos.
part_of_speech: discourse phrase limiting a commitment to the speaker
grammar: Por mi parte limits the announced contribution to the speaker. It does not imply that Ana and Luis have agreed to help.
note: Llevaré = I will bring; lavaré = I will wash; comida del barrio = neighborhood meal.

sentence: Dije que la película duró casi una hora; para ser exactos, duró cincuenta y ocho minutos: empezó a las siete y terminó a las siete cincuenta y ocho.
part_of_speech: precision-marking discourse formula
grammar: Para ser exactos refines the approximate duration of the same film. The explicit start and end times support fifty-eight minutes rather than merely an approximate hour.
note: Casi una hora = almost an hour; a las siete cincuenta y ocho = at 7:58.

sentence: Ana, Luis y yo votamos a favor de abrir el club los sábados; aprobamos el cambio por unanimidad, sin ningún voto en contra.
part_of_speech: prepositional locution specifying unanimous approval
grammar: Por unanimidad means that every participant supports the decision. The named voters support the change, and sin ningún voto en contra explicitly excludes opposition.
register: Neutral report of an ordinary club decision.
note: Votar a favor = vote in favor; ningún voto en contra = no opposing vote.

sentence: Necesitábamos datos para aclarar la duda, pero Luis solo repitió una frase vacía: era hablar por hablar.
part_of_speech: preposition linking repeated identical infinitives
grammar: Hablar por hablar describes speaking merely for its own sake without useful content. Para aclarar names the practical purpose that the empty repetition failed to serve.
register: An ordinary critical assessment of an unhelpful contribution.
note: Datos = factual information; frase vacía = empty phrase without useful content.

sentence: Le di mi palabra a mi hija: he de asistir a su función de teatro el viernes y ya organicé mi trabajo para salir a tiempo.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present modal auxiliary with de
grammar: He de plus infinitive presents a personal resolution carrying commitment. Haber functions as a modal auxiliary here rather than existential hay or a perfect auxiliary.
register: A slightly formal or emphatic personal resolution.
note: Función de teatro = theater performance; organicé = I organized.

sentence: La luz de la cocina está encendida y oigo platos; mi hermano debe de estar preparando la cena, aunque todavía no lo veo.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present inferential modal component with de
grammar: Debe de introduces a probable explanation inferred from light and sounds. Inferences can also use deber without de; de is not an absolute obligation-versus-probability switch.
note: Encendida = on or lit; lo refers to the brother.

sentence: Ana y yo acordamos cerrar la cocina compartida a las diez; debemos atenernos a ese horario, aunque hoy tengamos ganas de seguir platicando.
part_of_speech: pronominal infinitive with attached first-person plural nos
grammar: Atenerse a means conforming one's actions to an agreement or rule. Nos identifies Ana and the speaker as the people who must keep their agreed schedule.
note: Cocina compartida = shared kitchen; tener ganas de = feel like doing something.

sentence: La entrada del frente estará cerrada mañana durante la reparación; habrá que rodear el edificio y entrar por atrás.
part_of_speech: transitive infinitive expressing movement around an obstacle
