grammar: Rodear el edificio means going around its exterior to reach the rear entrance. Visible habrá que states general future necessity without assigning it to a named obligated person.
note: Entrada del frente = front entrance; edificio = building; por atrás = through the back here.

sentence: La mejor amiga de Rosa se mudó lejos; al leer el mensaje de despedida de su amiga, Rosa rompió a llorar y no pudo seguir leyendo.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite onset auxiliary with a
grammar: Romper a llorar expresses a sudden emotional onset of crying. It is a restricted natural collocation, not a general replacement for starting any task.
note: Despedida = farewell; llorar = cry.

sentence: Durante la foto familiar, el perro se sentó en el sombrero de papá; mi hermano se echó a reír al ver a papá buscarlo debajo de la silla.
part_of_speech: third-person singular pronominal preterite onset construction with a
grammar: Echarse a reír expresses spontaneous onset of laughter. Se belongs to the onset construction, and the humorous incident supplies its trigger.
note: Sombrero = hat; reír = laugh; ver a alguien hacer algo = see someone do something; buscarlo refers to looking for the hat.

sentence: Ana y yo ya lavamos y cortamos las verduras; ahora pasamos a preparar la sopa, con todos los ingredientes listos.
part_of_speech: first-person plural present transition construction with a
grammar: Pasar a plus infinitive introduces the next phase after an earlier phase is complete. Ahora makes pasamos present here; lavamos and cortamos report completed preparation.
note: Verduras = vegetables; ingredientes = ingredients.

sentence: Quería reparar la silla; probé dos arreglos, pero ninguno funcionó y acabé comprando otra.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite resultative auxiliary governing a gerund
grammar: Acabar plus gerund introduces the eventual outcome after the failed repairs. Acabé comprando does not mean that the speaker had just bought the chair or finished an already ongoing purchase.
note: Arreglos = attempted fixes here; otra means another chair.

sentence: Yo quería cenar en casa; mi hermana insistió en salir, dudé un rato y terminé cediendo para no seguir discutiendo.
part_of_speech: regular gerund with a figurative concession meaning
grammar: Cediendo means yielding one's position here, rather than transferring a seat or object. The visible terminé frame presents giving in as the eventual action after hesitation.
note: Dudé = I hesitated; discutir = argue here.

sentence: Ana y yo venimos revisando los gastos de la casa desde enero; cada mes comparamos lo que pagamos y ahora tenemos un registro completo.
part_of_speech: first-person plural present auxiliary governing a gerund
grammar: Venir plus gerund presents repeated activity extending from an earlier period to the current point. It does not describe physical approach, and its emphasis differs from ir plus gerund expressing gradual progress.
note: Registro = record; revisando = reviewing; comparamos = we compare.

sentence: Acordé el precio con Luis, el pintor, y di por zanjado el asunto, aunque todavía falta elegir el color.
part_of_speech: masculine singular participle in a presumed-state complement
grammar: Dar por zanjado means treating a matter as settled. Zanjado agrees with asunto; the pending color choice shows that this assessment does not assert completion of every detail.
register: Neutral conversation about settling a practical arrangement.
note: Pintor = painter; asunto = matter; zanjar = settle conclusively.

sentence: En la agencia dejé abonada la mitad del costo del viaje; tengo el recibo y pagaré el resto el lunes.
part_of_speech: feminine singular past participle functioning as a resultative object complement
grammar: Abonada describes the completed payment state left by dejé and agrees with feminine mitad. The remaining balance is explicitly unpaid; dejar de would instead express cessation.
register: Ordinary discussion of a travel payment.
note: Abonar una cantidad = pay an amount toward a cost; agencia = travel agency here; la mitad = half.

sentence: Ya tengo escritas las cinco invitaciones: ayer redacté tres y hoy las otras dos; siguen aquí, listas para entregar.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present verb in a resultative tener-plus-participle construction
grammar: Tengo escritas presents accumulated completed invitations that remain available. Escritas agrees with invitaciones; after perfect haber, escrito would be invariant.
note: Redactar = compose a text; listas para entregar = ready to hand over.

sentence: El dueño cerró la única entrada del taller sin avisar; Clara se vio obligada a cancelar su reunión porque nadie podía entrar.
part_of_speech: third-person singular pronominal preterite construction with a feminine predicative adjective and infinitival linker
grammar: Verse obligado a presents a necessity imposed by circumstances. Clara is the affected actor who cancels; the owner's closure creates the obstacle. Obligada agrees with Clara.
note: Taller = workshop; sin avisar = without giving notice.

sentence: Ya reunimos cien pesos, pero estamos lejos de pagar la reparación: cuesta mil y todavía no tenemos otra ayuda.
part_of_speech: metaphorical distance expression introducing an infinitive
grammar: Estar lejos de plus infinitive measures distance from achieving a goal rather than physical location. The collected amount is only a small part of the required payment.
note: Reunimos cien pesos = we have collected one hundred pesos here; mil = one thousand.

sentence: Ana y yo discutimos mucho por el horario, pero no llegamos a gritar; hicimos una pausa y después hablamos con calma.
part_of_speech: first-person plural preterite threshold construction with a
grammar: Under visible no, llegar a marks an escalation threshold that was not reached. The discussion occurred, but shouting did not.
note: Con calma = calmly; discutir = argue here.

sentence: Probé las únicas dos llaves disponibles y ninguna gira; no hay manera de abrir este cajón con ellas.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun with an infinitival complement preposition
grammar: No hay manera de plus infinitive denies a workable method within the stated resources. Both available keys have been tried, and con ellas limits the claim to those keys.
note: Girar = turn; ninguna refers to neither of the keys; con ellas = with those keys.

sentence: En la reunión del lunes y en la de hoy hablé demasiado rápido; tengo tendencia a hacerlo cuando estoy nervioso.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun with an infinitival complement preposition
grammar: Tener tendencia a describes a recurring disposition. The two actual meetings support the pattern; hacerlo refers to speaking too quickly.
note: Demasiado rápido = too quickly; nervioso = nervous, referring to the male speaker.

sentence: Tengo intención de visitar a mi abuela el domingo; aún no he comprado el boleto y el viaje no está confirmado.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative verb governing a nominal intention complement
grammar: Tengo takes the noun intención as its complement, and de plus infinitive specifies the intended action. This predicates an intention; con la intención de instead gives another action's purpose. Neither construction guarantees fulfillment.
note: Tener intención de hacer algo = intend to do something; aún no = not yet; confirmado = confirmed.

sentence: Antes Luis creía todo lo que le contaban; después de varios engaños se volvió desconfiado y desde hace años pide pruebas antes de creer una historia.
part_of_speech: third-person singular pronominal preterite change-of-state verb
grammar: Volverse plus adjective describes a change in character. The earlier trust, intervening deception, and continuing demand for evidence establish a durable development rather than a return or repeated action.
note: Engaños = deceptions; desconfiado = distrustful; pruebas = evidence here.

sentence: Desde que vive solo, Diego aprende a organizar sus gastos y a resolver los problemas de casa; poco a poco se hace más responsable y ya no espera ayuda para todo.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present pronominal change-of-state verb
grammar: Hacerse presents Diego's development through learning and personal effort. Here it describes increasing responsibility rather than manufacturing something.
note: Organizar = organize; responsable = responsible. Esperar ayuda means expect help here.

sentence: Salimos al patio con cielo azul, pero de repente se puso a llover a cántaros; Ana y yo entramos a la casa con la ropa mojada.
part_of_speech: fixed adverbial expression modifying llover
grammar: Llover a cántaros means rain very heavily. Se puso a llover describes the weather's onset; se does not identify a person acting on themself.
register: Expressive everyday weather description.
note: Patio = courtyard; cielo azul = blue sky; ropa mojada = wet clothing.

sentence: Luis esperaba cinco personas en su fiesta, pero llegaron veinte; se quedó sorprendido al ver a tantos amigos en la puerta.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite pronominal verb with a resulting-state adjective
grammar: Quedarse sorprendido presents the surprised state produced by the unexpected turnout. It does not describe choosing to remain at a place.
note: Esperaba = expected here; fiesta = party; sorprendido = surprised; al ver = on seeing.

sentence: Durante varios meses arreglamos el patio y pusimos mesas y sillas; ese espacio se convirtió en un lugar de reunión para los vecinos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite pronominal verb governing en
grammar: Convertirse en introduces the new role attained by the courtyard after practical changes. The changing subject is an inanimate space.
note: Espacio = space; lugar de reunión = meeting place; vecinos = neighbors.

sentence: Primero Ana repartía libros; después aprendió a organizar los turnos y llegó a ser coordinadora de la biblioteca.
part_of_speech: feminine singular role noun
grammar: Coordinadora names Ana's attained role. Llegó a ser presents her progression to that role after distributing books and learning to organize shifts.
note: Repartía = used to distribute; a coordinadora organizes a group's tasks and participation.

sentence: El cuarto dejó de ser bodega cuando sacamos las cajas y pusimos una cama; ahora mi hermano duerme ahí.
part_of_speech: infinitive ser preceded by the cessation link de
grammar: Dejar de ser expresses cessation of a defining status or use. The room stopped functioning as storage after its conversion to a bedroom.
note: Cuarto = room; bodega = storage room; cama = bed.

sentence: Aunque esta semana ayuda en la cocina, Rosa sigue siendo la maestra del grupo; el lunes vuelve a dar clase.
part_of_speech: gerund of ser in an identity-continuation construction
grammar: Seguir siendo preserves Rosa's defining role despite a temporary change of task. Siendo is the gerund of ser.
note: Rosa's kitchen work lasts this week; her teaching role continues.

sentence: Pedí una constancia de asistencia al curso; volví a llamar ayer, pero continúo sin recibir ese documento.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun naming written confirmation
grammar: Constancia names a document confirming attendance. Continúo sin recibir keeps the nonreceipt ongoing despite another telephone call.
register: Ordinary course administration.
note: Asistencia al curso = course attendance; documento = document; continúo sin recibir = I still have not received.

sentence: Mi hermano dejó de usar azúcar el año pasado; yo estoy dejando de usar azúcar poco a poco y todavía pongo una cucharada en el café.
part_of_speech: gerund cessation component with governed de inside a progressive construction
grammar: Estoy dejando de presents cessation as currently developing. The remaining spoonful shows that the speaker has not completed the change, unlike the brother.
note: Cucharada = spoonful.

sentence: Cuando empecé a compartir casa con Ana, tuve que acostumbrarme a cocinar sin hacer ruido; al principio la despertaba y ahora ya no.
part_of_speech: infinitive with attached first-person singular lexical-pronominal clitic
grammar: Acostumbrarse a plus infinitive describes acquiring a routine through experience. Me identifies the speaker as the person adapting; a introduces the new activity.
note: La despertaba = I used to wake Ana up; hacer ruido = make noise.

sentence: En casa tengo la costumbre de abrir las ventanas al amanecer; así entra aire frío.
part_of_speech: governed preposition introducing the infinitival complement of costumbre
grammar: Tener la costumbre de requires de before the infinitive naming the habitual action.
note: Al amanecer = at dawn; aire = air.

sentence: El camión sale a las ocho y son las siete; a Julia le da tiempo a desayunar antes de ir a la terminal.
part_of_speech: third-person singular time-opportunity construction with experiencer dative le
grammar: Dar tiempo a plus infinitive expresses an available opportunity before a limit. Le identifies Julia as the person with time; the sentence does not assert that she eats.
note: Desayunar = eat breakfast. A Julia identifies the experiencer, not the subject of da.

sentence: Solo faltaba escribir la fecha del cartel; apuré los últimos cinco minutos del plazo y lo entregué completo a tiempo.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite transitive verb
grammar: Apurar the remaining minutes means using them to their limit. The completed delivery shows the practical result; this is more specific than merely hurrying.
note: Cartel = poster; los últimos cinco minutos = the final five minutes.

sentence: Ya arreglamos las sillas y limpiamos las mesas; el salón está en condiciones de recibir al grupo esta tarde.
part_of_speech: predicative prepositional expression introducing an infinitive
grammar: Estar en condiciones de expresses practical fitness for an action. The repairs and cleaning establish readiness to receive the group.
note: Salón = hall or shared room here; recibir al grupo = welcome the group.

sentence: Según el programa que acordamos entre todos, el inicio del taller está previsto para las diez; todavía falta confirmar la asistencia del maestro.
part_of_speech: masculine singular participial adjective functioning as a subject complement
grammar: Previsto presents the start as planned in an agreed program. It agrees with inicio and does not guarantee that the event will occur as planned.
register: Neutral discussion of an agreed event program.
note: Programa = event schedule here; inicio = start; asistencia del maestro = the teacher's attendance.

sentence: Ofrecimos a Pablo una tarea fácil, pero se negó a participar: dijo que no quería trabajar con el grupo, aunque tenía tiempo.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite lexical-pronominal verb governing a
grammar: Negarse a plus infinitive expresses refusal to act. Pablo's stated unwillingness and available time distinguish refusal from inability.
note: Ofrecimos = we offered; participar = participate.

sentence: Nunca he cantado frente a otras personas; puedo equivocarme, pero decidí arriesgarme a cantar con mis amigos en la fiesta.
part_of_speech: infinitive with attached first-person singular lexical-pronominal clitic
grammar: Arriesgarse a plus infinitive expresses choosing to try despite a possible unwanted outcome. Here the ordinary social risk is making a singing mistake.
note: Cantar = sing; frente a = in front of; equivocarme = make a mistake; decidí = I decided.

sentence: Con las verduras y el arroz, la comida viene a costar unos cien pesos; es un cálculo, porque el precio cambia cada semana.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present approximation component with a
grammar: Venir a costar gives an approximate amount rather than physical movement. Unos and the explicit calculation reinforce the estimate.
note: Verduras = vegetables; cálculo = estimate or calculation here.

sentence: Durante meses planeamos una biblioteca para los vecinos; ayer reunimos los libros, abrimos las puertas y logramos echar a andar el proyecto.
part_of_speech: fixed causative verbal expression in the infinitive
grammar: Echar a andar a project means putting it into operation. The collected books and opened doors establish an actual start.
note: Planear = plan; proyecto = project or shared undertaking. The expression does not describe beginning to walk.

sentence: Di por hecho que Luis iba a traer las sillas porque siempre ayuda, pero él aclaró que esta vez no podía; nunca confirmó su participación.
part_of_speech: fixed presumed-state complement containing por and masculine singular hecho
grammar: Dar por hecho que means assuming content is settled or true. The speaker assumed Luis's help without confirmation, and Luis later corrected that assumption.
note: Participación = participation; iba a traer = was going to bring.

sentence: Creía que Ana no me contestaba; al revisar el teléfono me di cuenta de que su respuesta ya estaba ahí.
part_of_speech: governed preposition de followed by the finite-clause complementizer que
grammar: Darse cuenta de retains de when the realized content is a finite que-clause.
note: Me di cuenta = I realized; respuesta = reply; al revisar = on checking.

sentence: Pensaba que el curso era gratis, pero ahora veo el precio junto al horario y me doy cuenta: hay que pagar cada clase.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present verbal component with lexical-pronominal me
grammar: Me doy supplies the present verbal component of darse cuenta. The visible price triggers a current realization that corrects the earlier assumption.
note: Darse cuenta means realize; it does not mean giving oneself a restaurant bill.

sentence: Buscaba mi vaso mientras hablaba con Ana y, sin darme cuenta, tomé el suyo; cuando vi su nombre en él, se lo devolví.
part_of_speech: adverbial prepositional phrase containing a pronominal infinitival expression
grammar: Sin darme cuenta describes the speaker's lack of awareness during the taking. The later discovery and return make the unintended action explicit.
note: El suyo = Ana's glass; él refers to that glass; se lo devolví = I returned it to Ana.

sentence: Luis, date cuenta: si dejas las cajas frente a la puerta, tu abuela no puede salir de la casa.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached lexical-pronominal te in darse cuenta
grammar: Date cuenta appeals directly to Luis to recognize a consequence. Date joins da and te and needs no written accent; te belongs to the pronominal realization expression.
register: Direct familiar appeal to a named peer.
note: Frente a la puerta = in front of the door; dejas means leave objects somewhere here.

sentence: Vi las dos fotos y por fin caí en la cuenta de que la bolsa roja era la mía: reconocí la mancha que hice la semana pasada.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite verb in the fixed expression caer en la cuenta
grammar: Caer en la cuenta describes arriving at a realization. En belongs to the expression, while de que introduces its content; the recognized stain supplies the decisive clue.
note: Caí has an accented í. It describes realization here, rather than a physical fall.

sentence: Ana escribió un mensaje para dar cuenta de la mudanza: explicó que tres cajas llegaron abiertas y que revisó su contenido.
part_of_speech: nonpronominal verbal locution in the infinitive
grammar: Dar cuenta de means reporting or explaining something. Ana conveys an account to others; there is no pronominal se marking her realization.
register: Neutral to somewhat formal reporting.
note: Contenido = contents; llegaron abiertas = arrived open, describing the boxes' condition.

sentence: Marta dio cuenta de la gotera a las vecinas en la reunión: explicó dónde entraba el agua y qué reparación hacía falta.
part_of_speech: audience-marking preposition with a feminine plural definite article
grammar: In dar cuenta de algo a alguien, de introduces the content and a introduces the audience. Las agrees with the female neighbors receiving Marta's account.
register: Neutral to somewhat formal reporting at a neighborhood meeting.
note: Dio cuenta = gave an account; gotera = roof leak; hacía falta = was needed.

sentence: Usamos el dinero de todos para comprar libros; el sábado vamos a rendir cuentas al grupo y explicar cuánto pagamos por cada uno.
part_of_speech: infinitive verbal component of the accountability expression rendir cuentas
grammar: Rendir combines with cuentas to express accounting for one's use of shared resources. The group receives the explanation of the book purchases.
register: Ordinary group accountability.
note: Rendir cuentas al grupo = explain one's actions and use of resources to the group.

sentence: Pablo cambió el horario del club sin consultar al grupo; mañana vamos a pedirle cuentas por esa decisión y escuchar sus razones.
part_of_speech: plural noun in the fixed expression pedir cuentas
grammar: Pedirle cuentas means asking Pablo to explain his decision. The plural cuentas concerns accountability, rather than a restaurant bill.
register: A firm request for an explanation within a group.
note: Decisión = decision; razones = reasons; le identifies Pablo as the person asked.

sentence: El camión directo cuesta menos, pero solo pasa dos veces al día; en resumidas cuentas, ahorramos dinero y perdemos opciones de horario.
part_of_speech: fixed summarizing discourse expression
grammar: En resumidas cuentas introduces a concise conclusion. This conclusion retains both the lower cost and the reduced choice of departure times.
register: Neutral conversational summary.
note: Ahorramos dinero = we save money; opciones de horario = choices of travel time.

sentence: Todavía no hemos elegido la hora del paseo; tenemos que tener en cuenta que Julia trabaja por la mañana, aunque Luis prefiere salir temprano.
part_of_speech: fixed prepositional component of tener en cuenta
grammar: Tener en cuenta means including relevant information in a decision. Here Julia's morning work is a constraint; considering it does not itself settle the departure time.
note: Elegido = chosen, the participle of elegir; temprano = early.

sentence: Ana quiere ayudar y conoce todos los horarios del grupo; tómala en cuenta al organizar el paseo y escucha lo que propone.
part_of_speech: affirmative tú imperative with attached feminine singular personal direct-object la
grammar: Tómala en cuenta asks the listener to consider Ana as a contributor. La refers to Ana, and the accent preserves the stress of toma after attachment.
register: Familiar advice to someone organizing a group outing.
note: Al organizar = when organizing; propone = she proposes. Ana's knowledge of the schedules makes her contribution relevant.

sentence: No hemos elegido el lugar de la fiesta; antes de decidir, hay que tomar en consideración el ruido, porque mi abuela necesita descansar temprano.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun in tomar en consideración
grammar: Tomar en consideración means including something relevant in deliberation. Here consideración concerns weighing a decision constraint, rather than considerate treatment.
register: Neutral to somewhat formal discussion.
note: Decidir = decide; no hemos elegido = we have not chosen.

sentence: Luis quiere reunirse de noche, pero Ana pide salir temprano porque madruga; debemos tener en cuenta a ambos y no ignorar la petición de Ana.
part_of_speech: transitive infinitive
grammar: Ignorar means leaving a known concern out of consideration here. Ana's request is explicitly known, so this is not the sense of lacking knowledge.
note: Madruga = gets up early; petición = request.

sentence: Ana pidió reparar la gotera y Luis pidió pintar la sala; tomamos en cuenta ambas ideas, pero dimos prioridad a la reparación porque ya entraba agua.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun in dar prioridad a
grammar: Dar prioridad a ranks one need ahead of another. Both proposals receive consideration, but the entering water makes the repair the first task.
note: Ambas ideas = both ideas; sala = living room; dimos = we gave.

sentence: Clara ya no recibe un sueldo de la tienda: ahora trabaja por cuenta propia, elige sus horarios y vende sus bolsas a distintos clientes.
part_of_speech: fixed adverbial expression describing independent employment
grammar: Trabajar por cuenta propia describes independent work rather than salaried employment. Clara chooses her hours and sells her bags to customers.
register: Ordinary description of a work arrangement.
note: Sueldo = salary; distintos clientes = various customers.

sentence: Nadie estaba en casa para ayudarme; armé la silla por cuenta propia, siguiendo las instrucciones, y después me senté a descansar.
part_of_speech: fixed adverbial expression describing action without others' help
grammar: Por cuenta propia means acting independently here. The absence of anyone to help establishes this action sense rather than an employment arrangement.
note: Armar una silla = assemble a chair; siguiendo las instrucciones = following the instructions.

sentence: Pintamos sobre el mantel blanco por cuenta y riesgo de Luis: él eligió usar el suyo y aceptó que su mantel podía mancharse.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun in the responsibility expression por cuenta y riesgo de
grammar: Por cuenta y riesgo de Luis attributes responsibility for the choice and its possible unwanted result to Luis. He owns the cloth and explicitly accepts possible staining.
register: Emphatic attribution of responsibility for an ordinary choice.
note: Mantel = tablecloth; el suyo = Luis's tablecloth; mancharse = become stained.

sentence: Las vecinas me pidieron entregar su propuesta al club; fui a la reunión por cuenta de ellas y expliqué las ideas que ellas acordaron.
part_of_speech: fixed prepositional expression introducing the represented group
grammar: Por cuenta de ellas describes acting on the neighbors' behalf. Their request and agreed ideas establish representation; the sentence assigns no expense.
register: Neutral report of representing a neighborhood group.
note: Ellas refers to the female neighbors; acordaron = they agreed on.

sentence: El taller de teatro es autónomo: organiza sus horarios y elige sus obras por cuenta propia, sin recibir órdenes de otro grupo.
part_of_speech: masculine singular predicative adjective
grammar: Autónomo describes control over the workshop's own decisions. Its independent scheduling and choice of plays establish this meaning.
register: Neutral description of a community arts project.
note: Teatro = theater; obras = plays here; órdenes = instructions or orders.

sentence: Para hacer los mismos viajes en camión esta semana, el pase cuesta cien pesos y los boletos sueltos cuestan ciento sesenta; comprarlo me sale a cuenta, así que elijo el pase y me quedan sesenta pesos más.
part_of_speech: fixed adverbial component of salir a cuenta
grammar: Salir a cuenta evaluates whether a choice provides a worthwhile return. The pass covers the same journeys for sixty pesos less; me identifies the speaker as the beneficiary.
register: An ordinary personal comparison of transport costs.
note: Pase = transport pass; boletos sueltos = individual tickets; elijo = I choose.

sentence: Ana piensa viajar al otro mercado para pagar cuarenta pesos menos por la compra, pero el desembolso de sesenta pesos en transporte es mayor; ese viaje no le sale a cuenta y decide comprar aquí.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Desembolso names money paid out. The sixty-peso transport outlay exceeds the forty-peso reduction in the shopping cost.
register: An everyday fictional shopping decision.
note: Le refers to Ana; ese viaje is the singular subject of sale. Compra = shopping purchase here.

sentence: La entrega cuesta treinta pesos, pero nos evita un viaje de cincuenta; evitar ese gasto compensa el costo de la entrega y por eso la pedimos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative transitive verb
grammar: Compensar means offsetting a cost through a sufficient practical benefit here. Its object is el costo, rather than a person receiving compensation.
register: An ordinary shared delivery choice.
note: Nos evita un viaje = saves us a trip; costo = cost.

sentence: En la venta del domingo, Ana recibió quinientos pesos por sus panes y gastó trescientos en todo lo necesario; el pequeño negocio fue rentable y le dejó doscientos pesos.
part_of_speech: singular predicative adjective
grammar: Rentable describes an activity yielding more money than its costs. The stated receipts and total costs leave Ana two hundred pesos.
register: A fictional account of a small food sale.
note: Negocio = business or venture; le dejó doscientos pesos = left Ana two hundred pesos after costs.

sentence: La mochila nueva cuesta trescientos pesos y repararla cuesta cien; el ahorro de doscientos justifica caminar veinte minutos hasta el taller, así que voy a repararla.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Ahorro names the two hundred pesos not spent by choosing repair. It is a reduction in expenditure, rather than money received from sales.
register: A personal fictional repair choice.
note: Mochila = backpack; justifica = makes worthwhile or justifies.

sentence: El patio es más ruidoso que la sala, pero tiene la ventaja de que cabemos todos; por eso lo elegimos para la reunión.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Ventaja identifies a useful feature supporting a choice. The patio's capacity is an advantage despite its explicitly acknowledged noise.
register: A group discusses an ordinary meeting venue.
note: Ruidoso = noisy; cabemos todos = there is room for all of us; elegimos = we choose.

sentence: En la comida del club, cada invitado paga sus tacos, pero las bebidas son por cuenta de Julia: ella va a pagarlas para todo el grupo.
part_of_speech: fixed prepositional expression identifying the payer
grammar: Por cuenta de Julia assigns the drinks' expense to Julia. Her explicit intention to pay establishes the expense sense.
register: An explicit payment arrangement for a club meal.
note: Invitado = guest; bebidas = drinks; pagarlas refers to the drinks.

sentence: Para la fiesta del sábado, acordamos que la renta de las sillas va a correr por cuenta de Luis; él aceptó ese gasto y todavía no lo ha pagado.
part_of_speech: infinitive in the expense-responsibility expression correr por cuenta de
grammar: An expense can correr por cuenta de someone: that person is responsible for paying it. The arrangement does not assert completed payment.
register: An explicit agreement about a shared celebration.
note: Renta de las sillas = chair rental; acordamos = we agreed; lo refers to the rental expense.

sentence: La mesa cuesta mil pesos y el carpintero me la entrega el viernes; hoy lunes le pagué doscientos a cuenta de esa cantidad y todavía le debo ochocientos.
part_of_speech: fixed prepositional expression marking partial advance payment
grammar: A cuenta de marks a payment applied toward a larger amount owed. Two hundred is paid before delivery, leaving eight hundred of the thousand-peso price.
register: An ordinary fictional purchase arrangement.
note: Carpintero = carpenter; esa cantidad = that amount; both instances of le refer to the carpenter.

sentence: Clara trabaja por cuenta ajena en una panadería: la dueña le paga un sueldo y fija sus horarios; su hermano, en cambio, vende pan por cuenta propia.
part_of_speech: fixed adverbial expression describing employment for another party
grammar: Trabajar por cuenta ajena describes Clara's work for an employer. The salary and employer-set hours distinguish her arrangement from her brother's independent sales.
register: An ordinary description of two work arrangements.
note: Panadería = bakery; fija sus horarios = sets her working hours.

sentence: La cuenta está desglosada: aparecen dos sopas de sesenta pesos y un agua de veinte, pero el total dice ciento cincuenta en vez de ciento cuarenta.
part_of_speech: feminine singular participial adjective
grammar: Desglosada describes a bill presented in separate items. The listed charges total one hundred forty, exposing the ten-peso discrepancy.
register: A restrained restaurant-bill observation.
note: Aparecen = are listed here; en vez de = instead of; un agua = one serving of water.

sentence: Hice cuentas para un viaje de dos tramos: en camión pago cuarenta pesos por tramo, mientras que el taxi cobra ciento veinte por los dos; elijo el camión porque en total pago ochenta.
part_of_speech: feminine plural noun in hacer cuentas
grammar: Hacer cuentas means doing arithmetic. The two forty-peso bus segments total eighty, compared with one hundred twenty for both taxi segments.
register: An everyday transport comparison.
note: Por tramo = per route segment; los dos refers to the two stated segments; elijo = I choose.

sentence: Para la comida del grupo, llevo las cuentas en un cuaderno: anoto los doscientos pesos que recibimos y los ciento cincuenta que gastamos, para saber cuánto queda.
part_of_speech: feminine plural noun phrase in llevar las cuentas
grammar: Llevar las cuentas means keeping a record of money received and spent. The notebook and both kinds of entries establish recordkeeping.
register: Informal responsibility for a shared meal.
note: Anoto = I write down or record; gastamos = we spend.

sentence: No recuerdo cuántas veces repetimos la canción en el paseo; perdí la cuenta cuando los niños la pidieron otra vez.
part_of_speech: fixed feminine noun-phrase component of perder la cuenta
grammar: Perder la cuenta means no longer knowing the exact number of occurrences. The speaker remembers repeating the song but cannot give the exact repetition count.
register: A lighthearted account of an outing with children.
note: Canción = song; repetimos = we repeated; la pidieron = they requested it.

sentence: Las cantidades no cuadran: anotamos cien pesos de comida y ciento cincuenta de sillas, pero pusimos doscientos ochenta como total; vamos a revisar la suma.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present indicative verb
grammar: Cuadrar describes figures matching the required total. The two recorded expenses add to two hundred fifty, rather than the recorded two hundred eighty.
register: A practical correction of a shared expense record.
note: Cantidades = amounts; suma = sum; pusimos = we put or entered.

sentence: Para terminar el collar, falta una cuenta azul con un agujero en medio; Ana va a pasar el hilo por ella junto a las piezas rojas.
part_of_speech: feminine singular count noun
grammar: Cuenta names a small pierced piece used in a necklace. Una and azul describe the single missing bead.
register: An ordinary craft activity.
note: Collar = necklace; agujero = hole; hilo = thread; piezas = pieces.

sentence: Mi cuenta de correo es personal; los mensajes llegan a mi dirección y solo yo tengo la contraseña.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun referring to an email account
grammar: Cuenta de correo identifies the speaker's own email account. Messages and a password establish the communication sense.
register: An ordinary explanation of personal correspondence.
note: Correo = email here; contraseña = password; personal = for the speaker's individual use.

sentence: En la comida familiar, mis primos dieron buena cuenta del arroz: repitieron con gusto y no dejaron ni un grano en la olla.
part_of_speech: fixed noun-phrase component of dar buena cuenta de
grammar: Dar buena cuenta de food expresses eating it thoroughly here. Taking seconds with enjoyment and leaving no rice establish the enthusiastic consumption in this account.
register: A lively, approving meal narrative.
note: Primos = cousins; repitieron = had seconds here; ni un grano = not even one grain; olla = pot.

sentence: Al organizar las mesas de la fiesta, tu comentario sobre el espacio para las sillas de ruedas viene a cuento: tenemos que dejar un paso libre.
part_of_speech: fixed adverbial component of venir a cuento
grammar: Venir a cuento means being relevant to the subject under discussion. Wheelchair space directly affects the current table arrangement.
register: A cooperative response to a familiar co-organizer.
note: Cuento alone = story; silla de ruedas = wheelchair; paso libre = clear passage.

sentence: Ana, estamos eligiendo la hora de la comida y de pronto hablas del precio de los zapatos; ¿a cuento de qué sacas ese tema ahora?
part_of_speech: fixed interrogative expression
grammar: A cuento de qué asks why a topic or action has been introduced. The speaker explicitly questions the change from meal timing to shoe prices.
register: A direct question in familiar tú address; the wording can sound reproachful.
note: Sacar un tema = bring up a topic; de pronto = suddenly; eligiendo = choosing.

sentence: Empecé a esperar a Julia a las nueve y ya son las diez; llevo una hora esperándola y ella todavía no llega.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present duration auxiliary governing a gerund
grammar: Llevar plus a duration and gerund measures an activity continuing now. Waiting began at nine and remains in progress at ten.
register: An ordinary update during a wait.
note: Esperándola = waiting for Julia; todavía no llega = she has not arrived yet.

sentence: El sábado empecé a preparar la sopa a las doce; cuando llegó Julia a la una, llevaba una hora cocinando y la sopa aún no estaba lista.
part_of_speech: first-person singular imperfect duration auxiliary governing a gerund
grammar: Llevaba measures the cooking already underway at a past reference point. Julia's one-o'clock arrival follows the noon start; the soup was unfinished then.
register: A connected account of preparing a shared meal.
note: Cocinando = cooking; aún no estaba lista = was still not ready.

sentence: Antes hablaba con mi hermano cada domingo, pero la última llamada fue hace tres semanas; llevo tres semanas sin hablar con él y hoy quiero llamarlo.
part_of_speech: preposition introducing an infinitive in llevar duration sin
grammar: Llevar a duration sin an infinitive measures how long an action has remained unperformed. It contrasts with the ongoing activity expressed by a gerund.
register: A personal explanation of interrupted family contact.
note: La última llamada = the last phone call; llamarlo = call the speaker's brother.

sentence: Estoy leyendo un libro de diez capítulos; llevo leídos seis y voy a continuar después del descanso.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present verb in an accumulated-completion construction with an agreeing participle
grammar: Llevar plus an agreeing participle tallies completed work so far. Six of the ten chapters are finished; leídos agrees with the understood capítulos.
register: A reading-progress update.
note: Capítulos = chapters; seis means six chapters; continuar = continue.

sentence: A Julia le llevó dos horas armar la silla ayer; empezó a las cuatro y terminó a las seis, mientras yo preparaba la cena.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite verb with an infinitival task subject and a person dative
grammar: Armar la silla is the task that took time; Julia is the person whose time it occupied, represented by le. The task began at four and ended at six.
register: An ordinary account of parallel household activities.
note: Armar = assemble; preparaba = I was preparing.

sentence: Yo me llevo bien con Ana: repartimos las tareas de la casa y nos escuchamos cuando alguna tiene un problema.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present pronominal verb phrase in llevarse bien con
grammar: Llevarse bien con expresses a good interpersonal relationship. Me belongs to the pronominal verb; con introduces Ana.
register: An ordinary description of a cooperative household relationship.
note: Repartimos = divide up; nos escuchamos = listen to each other; alguna = either one of us here.

sentence: Ana se lleva mal con Julia: discuten por cualquier cambio, aunque siguen organizando juntas la fiesta de la mamá de Ana.
part_of_speech: adverb in the relationship expression llevarse mal con
grammar: Mal gives llevarse con a strained-relationship interpretation. Their continued cooperation shows that getting along badly does not mean having no contact.
register: A neutral description of a strained relationship.
note: Discuten = argue; por cualquier cambio = over any change; juntas refers to Ana and Julia.

sentence: Ana y Julia antes se llevaban bien y se llamaban a diario; con el tiempo se distanciaron y ahora solo se saludan en las reuniones.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Distanciarse describes emotional separation here. Former daily calls contrast with the women's present contact limited to greetings.
register: A restrained account of a changed personal relationship.
note: Se llevaban bien = used to get along; se llamaban = used to call each other.

sentence: Ana y Julia se llevan con confianza y acordaron tutearse: desde hoy, cada una le dice «tú» a la otra.
part_of_speech: infinitive with attached reciprocal se
grammar: Tutearse means using tú with one another. The explicit agreement establishes their chosen address form; familiarity alone does not impose it.
register: Two women explicitly agree on familiar reciprocal address.
note: Con confianza = with interpersonal familiarity here; acordaron = they agreed; cada una = each woman.

sentence: Probé la salsa con el queso y me gustó la mezcla: esos dos sabores se llevan bien, así que voy a usar esa combinación en los tacos.
part_of_speech: third-person plural present pronominal verb phrase describing compatibility
grammar: Llevarse bien can describe compatible things. The speaker's tasting experience establishes a pleasant flavor combination, rather than a human relationship.
register: An ordinary personal food preference.
note: Mezcla = mixture; sabores = flavors; combinación = combination.

sentence: Acordamos limpiar el patio entre todos y hoy vamos a llevar a cabo el plan: Ana lava las mesas, Luis barre y yo recojo la basura.
part_of_speech: fixed adverbial component of llevar a cabo
grammar: Llevar a cabo means carrying out a plan. The task assignments explain the planned implementation; vamos a presents it as prospective.
register: An ordinary shared cleaning plan.
note: Entre todos = with everyone contributing; barre = sweeps; recojo = I pick up. The present forms specify each person's assigned task.

sentence: Ya anunciamos que vamos a llevar a cabo la limpieza del parque, pero falta pasar a la ejecución: todavía no hemos limpiado nada.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Ejecución names actually carrying out the announced task. The explicit absence of cleaning separates implementation from announcement.
register: A somewhat formal assessment of progress on a shared project.
note: Limpieza = cleaning; pasar a = move on to; anunciamos = we announced here.

sentence: La limpieza del patio se llevó a cabo ayer; Ana y Luis participaron y hoy ya podemos usar las mesas.
part_of_speech: passive se in llevarse a cabo
grammar: La limpieza is the event subject of se llevó a cabo. Se presents its realization without making a named person the grammatical agent; it is not reflexive self-cleaning.
register: A neutral report of a completed shared activity.
note: Llevó is singular because limpieza is singular; participaron = took part.

sentence: La lluvia dañó varias mesas del taller, pero encontramos otras prestadas y decidimos llevar adelante el proyecto; ya seguimos con las clases.
part_of_speech: adverbial component of the figurative expression llevar adelante
grammar: Llevar adelante means continuing to implement a project despite difficulty. Borrowed replacement tables allow the classes to continue after the damage.
register: An account of continuing workshop classes after a setback.
note: Dañó = damaged; decidimos = we decided; otras prestadas = other borrowed tables.

sentence: La secretaria del club escribió: «El intercambio de libros se va a llevar a efecto el sábado, como acordamos»; las familias ya preparan sus libros.
part_of_speech: fixed adverbial component of llevar a efecto
grammar: Llevar a efecto means putting an agreed arrangement into practice. It supplies a more formal expression for implementation, without adding a different completion stage.
register: Somewhat formal wording in a club secretary's written notice.
note: Secretaria = female secretary; intercambio de libros = book exchange; como acordamos = as we agreed.

sentence: Ana lleva la blusa al revés: la etiqueta del cuello y las costuras que normalmente quedan por dentro ahora se ven por fuera.
part_of_speech: fixed adverbial expression describing garment orientation
grammar: Al revés describes the garment's inside-out orientation here. The normally inward label and seams are visibly on the outside.
register: An ordinary observation about clothing.
note: Etiqueta del cuello = neck label; normalmente = normally; se ven = are visible.

sentence: Esta chamarra lleva dos bolsas interiores cosidas a la tela; forman parte de la prenda y sirven para guardar las llaves.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative transitive verb describing a built-in feature
grammar: The garment is the subject of lleva, and its built-in pockets are the object. This describes construction or design rather than a person wearing clothing.
register: An ordinary garment description.
note: Bolsas = pockets here; interiores = inside; cosidas = sewn; tela = fabric; prenda = garment.

sentence: Este cuaderno lleva el nombre de Julia en la portada; por eso ella lo reconoce entre los demás.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative transitive verb describing an identifying inscription
grammar: Llevar describes an object bearing an identifying name. Julia's name on the cover lets her recognize the notebook.
register: An everyday explanation of recognizing a notebook.
note: Portada = cover; los demás = the others; lo refers to the notebook.

sentence: La receta de este pan lleva leche en vez de agua; mi papá mezcla la leche con la harina para preparar la masa.
part_of_speech: feminine singular mass noun
grammar: Harina names the flour used as an ingredient. It is mixed with milk to prepare the masa, or dough; visible lleva describes what the recipe includes.
register: An ordinary home-baking explanation.
note: Mezcla = mixes; masa = dough. Llevar an ingredient means including or calling for it in a recipe.

sentence: Para pintar, Ana lleva el pelo recogido en una cola; una liga lo mantiene lejos de la cara.
part_of_speech: masculine singular participial adjective describing a hairstyle
grammar: Recogido describes hair gathered and secured rather than loose. It agrees with pelo; the ponytail and hair tie establish the hairstyle.
register: An ordinary practical description of hair worn for painting.
note: Pelo = hair; cola = ponytail here; liga = hair tie; lo mantiene = keeps it.

sentence: Mi hermana tiene treinta años y yo, veintisiete; me lleva tres años y por eso es la mayor de las dos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present comparative verb phrase with a first-person singular dative
grammar: In this age comparison, the older person is the subject, me identifies the younger person, and tres años states the difference.

sentence: En el juego de preguntas, mi equipo tiene siete puntos y el de Ana tiene cinco; le llevamos dos puntos, aunque todavía no termina el juego.
meaning: we are ahead of it by
part_of_speech: first-person plural present comparative verb phrase with a singular opponent dative
grammar: Le refers to Ana's team. Dos puntos measures the speaker's team's current lead; the unfinished game leaves the final result open.
note: Equipo = team; puntos = points; juego de preguntas = quiz game.

sentence: Ana lleva ventaja para organizar el paseo: ya conoce la ruta y los horarios del camión, mientras que nosotros todavía tenemos que buscarlos.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present verbal expression
grammar: Llevar ventaja describes a favorable starting position. Ana's existing information gives her that advantage without guaranteeing a future outcome.
note: Buscarlos refers to the route and bus schedules.

sentence: Para terminar juntos el mural, Ana pinta ocho flores y Luis otras ocho; Ana lleva la delantera, con seis terminadas frente a las tres de Luis.
part_of_speech: fixed feminine noun phrase in llevar la delantera
grammar: Llevar la delantera means being ahead in progress. Both painters have eight assigned flowers, and their completed totals establish the comparison.
note: Mural = wall painting; frente a = compared with here.

sentence: En el concurso de cocina, Laura lleva las de ganar: ya practicó la receta tres veces y los demás apenas la están aprendiendo; aun así, todavía falta la prueba.
part_of_speech: fixed nominal component of llevar las de ganar
grammar: The expression presents favorable prospects. The remaining test makes clear that Laura has not won yet.
register: Ordinary conversational assessment of someone's chances.
note: Concurso = contest; apenas = only just here; prueba = test.

sentence: Aunque ensayamos toda la semana, llevamos las de perder en el concurso de baile: los otros grupos tienen mucha más experiencia, pero todavía podemos hacerlo bien.
part_of_speech: fixed nominal component of llevar las de perder
grammar: The expression describes an unfavorable position despite preparation. It does not assert that defeat has already occurred or is unavoidable.
register: Ordinary conversational assessment of a group's chances.
note: Concurso de baile = dance contest; hacerlo bien = perform well here.

sentence: Mi hermana lleva el asunto de las sillas para la fiesta: consigue el préstamo y confirma cuántas necesitamos; yo preparo la comida.
part_of_speech: third-person singular present indicative transitive verb
grammar: Llevar un asunto means handling responsibility for a matter. Arranging the loan and checking the quantity specify that responsibility.
note: Asunto = matter; préstamo = loan.

sentence: En nuestro taller, Ana lleva el control de las tijeras: anota quién recibe cada par y quién lo devuelve, mientras los demás repartimos el material.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun phrase in llevar el control
grammar: Llevar el control de something means keeping track of it. Ana records loans and returns while other people distribute the materials.
note: Tijeras = scissors; cada par = each pair.

sentence: En el ensayo, yo llevo el ritmo con las palmas para que Ana y Luis entren juntos después de cada pausa.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun phrase
grammar: Ritmo names the musical beat maintained through clapping. Llevar el ritmo describes keeping that beat.
note: Ensayo = rehearsal; con las palmas = by clapping; entren = come in, in the musical activity.

sentence: En el taller llevamos un ritmo de dos sillas reparadas por hora; todavía quedan seis, así que calculamos terminar en tres horas.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun phrase with a rate-complement preposition
grammar: Un ritmo de introduces a production rate, measured here in completed chairs per hour. It does not state time already spent.
note: Reparadas = repaired; calculamos terminar = we estimate finishing.

sentence: El camión viene con veinte minutos de retraso; intento llevar la espera con paciencia y leo mientras espero.
part_of_speech: transitive infinitive verb
grammar: Llevar an inconvenience con paciencia describes how someone copes with it. Reading during the wait illustrates the speaker's response without removing the delay.

sentence: El calor en la cocina llevó a Marta a abrir la ventana; necesitaba aire mientras preparaba la sopa.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite causative transitive verb
grammar: The heat is the cause, Marta is the personal direct object introduced by a, and a abrir names the resulting action.
note: Aire = air; Marta is also the understood subject of necesitaba and preparaba.

sentence: Dos avisos con horas distintas llevaron a una confusión: Ana llegó al café a las cinco y Luis, a las seis para la misma reunión.
part_of_speech: third-person plural preterite verb governing a nominal result with a
grammar: The two notices are the plural cause. A una confusión names the resulting situation, with no person object or physical destination.
note: Horas distintas = different times; café = café as a meeting place here.

sentence: Creía que mi hermano seguía en Toluca; me llevé una sorpresa cuando abrí la puerta y lo vi con su maleta.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite pronominal verbal component of llevarse una sorpresa
grammar: Llevarse una sorpresa means experiencing surprise. Seeing the brother at the door contradicts the speaker's prior belief.
note: Maleta = suitcase; lo refers to the speaker's brother.

sentence: Luis se llevó una regañada de su hermana por dejar las piezas del juego en el piso; luego ambos las recogieron.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Una regañada is a scolding. In llevarse una regañada, Luis receives it, his sister gives it, and por introduces the reason.
register: Everyday Mexican-compatible vocabulary.
note: Piezas del juego = game pieces; piso = floor here.

sentence: Ana pintó todo el letrero y yo solo lo colgué; cuando el grupo vio su trabajo, ella se llevó el mérito.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Mérito is credit for the contribution here. Ana receives it because she painted the sign; the speaker only hung it.
note: Letrero = sign; colgué = I hung up.

sentence: Ana lleva la camisa remangada: dobló las mangas hasta los codos para lavar los platos sin mojarlas.
part_of_speech: feminine singular participial adjective agreeing with camisa
grammar: Remangada describes the worn shirt's rolled-up sleeve configuration and agrees with camisa. The folded sleeves reaching the elbows make that configuration explicit.
note: Mangas = sleeves; codos = elbows; dobló = folded; mojarlas = get the sleeves wet.

sentence: Ana lleva un pañuelo a juego con su blusa: ambos son azules y tienen las mismas flores blancas.
part_of_speech: fixed adjectival expression with a con complement
grammar: A juego con describes items that match in appearance. The shared blue color and white-flower pattern establish the match.
note: Pañuelo = scarf here; azules = blue.

sentence: Hoy llevo un vestido de diario para hacer las compras; para la boda formal de mañana voy a elegir otro.
part_of_speech: fixed adjectival prepositional expression
grammar: De diario classifies clothing by everyday use. The explicitly formal wedding motivates choosing a different dress.
register: Everyday clothing description contrasted with a formal social occasion.
note: Hacer las compras = do the shopping; boda = wedding; elegir = choose.

sentence: Para la fiesta, Julia lleva un arreglo de flores en el pelo: tres flores blancas unidas con una cinta azul.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Arreglo names a decorative arrangement worn in the hair. The joined flowers and ribbon specify its appearance.
note: Unidas = joined together; cinta = ribbon.

sentence: Mi abuela vive ahora en otra ciudad; la extraño cuando preparo la comida del domingo, porque antes cocinábamos juntas.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative transitive verb
grammar: Extrañar a alguien means feeling an absent person's absence. La identifies the grandmother as the direct object.
note: Juntas identifies the speaker and her grandmother as women who used to cook together.

sentence: Desde que cambié de turno, echo de menos las pláticas con Ana después de comer; ahora salgo cuando ella entra.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present verbal expression
grammar: Echar de menos takes the missed activity as its object here. The opposing shifts explain why the familiar conversations no longer happen.
register: Ordinary conversation about missing a familiar routine.
note: Pláticas = chats; turno = work shift here.

sentence: Ayer convivimos con los vecinos en el patio: cada familia llevó algo de comer y platicamos toda la tarde; después todos volvimos a nuestras casas.
part_of_speech: first-person plural preterite indicative verb with a con complement
grammar: Convivir con describes spending social time with people here. The participants return to separate homes afterward.
register: Ordinary Mexican-compatible social narration.
note: Vecinos = neighbors; algo de comer = something to eat; platicamos = we chatted.

sentence: Al principio me costaba compartir la cocina con mi compañera de casa; luego me acomodé a los turnos que acordamos y ahora preparo mi comida sin problemas.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Acomodarse a describes settling into an arrangement. Me belongs to the pronominal verb, and a introduces the agreed kitchen schedule.
note: Compañera de casa = female housemate; turnos = allocated turns here.

sentence: Ana, eres mi amiga y confío en ti; estoy frustrada y necesito desahogarme contigo porque hoy hice toda la limpieza y mi hermano no ayudó.
part_of_speech: pronominal infinitive with attached first-person singular me
grammar: Desahogarse con alguien means expressing pent-up feelings to a listener. Attached me identifies the speaker as the person seeking that emotional release.
register: Personal disclosure to a trusted friend.
note: Frustrada = frustrated; contigo = with you.

sentence: Ana dudaba en entrar al taller de dibujo; la animé a probar una clase porque la maestra ayuda a cada alumno, y aceptó.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite indicative transitive verb
grammar: Animar a alguien a hacer algo means encouraging that person to try an action. La represents Ana as direct object; a probar names the encouraged action.
note: Dudaba en entrar = was hesitant to join; taller de dibujo = drawing workshop; aceptó = she agreed.

sentence: El club no aceptó mi dibujo para la exposición y me desanimé; por unos días no quise dibujar, pero hoy volví a intentarlo.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Desanimarse expresses becoming discouraged. The later return to trying makes the reaction temporary within this account.
note: Exposición = exhibition; dibujar = draw; intentarlo = try again at the activity here.

sentence: Ana, estás cuidando a mi hijo mientras termino mi trabajo; te agradezco que lo cuides esta tarde.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present gratitude verb with a finite-content complementizer
grammar: Agradecer que introduces the appreciated action as a finite clause with present subjunctive cuides. The ongoing care is explicitly real; subjunctive marks the gratitude evaluation.
register: Direct thanks to a familiar helper.
note: Cuidar a un niño = look after a child; lo refers to the speaker's son.

sentence: Ana, te interrumpí mientras explicabas tu idea; me disculpo por eso y ahora voy a escucharte hasta el final.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present pronominal verb phrase
grammar: Disculparse por introduces the action being apologized for. Ana is the interrupted speaker and the person receiving the apology; the narrator commits to listening.
register: A direct apology in familiar tú address followed by a stated repair.
note: Por eso refers to interrupting Ana; hasta el final = through to the end.

sentence: Luis llegó diez minutos tarde a nuestra comida; le perdoné el retraso y seguimos platicando tranquilos.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite indicative transitive verb
grammar: El retraso is the direct object specifying what is forgiven. Le identifies Luis as the person forgiven for that delay.
register: An ordinary account of forgiving a minor social mistake.
note: Seguimos platicando = we continued chatting; tranquilos = calmly, agreeing with the participants.

sentence: Ana no quería venir a la comida porque el último camión sale temprano; la convencí de venir cuando le ofrecí llevarla a casa y aceptó.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite indicative transitive verb
grammar: Convencer a alguien de hacer algo takes Ana as direct object, represented by la, and retains de before the chosen action. Aceptó confirms her agreement.
note: Ofrecí = I offered; llevarla a casa = take Ana home.

sentence: Mi hermana quería usar la mesa para coser toda la tarde y yo necesitaba estudiar; negociamos un horario: ella la usará hasta las cinco y yo, después.
part_of_speech: first-person plural preterite indicative transitive verb
grammar: Negociar describes discussing competing needs to reach an arrangement. Each sibling receives a different part of the afternoon.
register: An ordinary household negotiation.
note: Usará = will use; la refers to the shared table.

sentence: Mi hermano pidió música hasta medianoche; hice una concesión al aceptar las diez en vez de las nueve, pero no cedí en la condición de mantener el volumen bajo, como acordamos.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: A concesión yields one disputed point. The speaker accepts a later stopping time while retaining the explicitly stated condition of keeping the volume low.
note: Cedí = I gave in; mantener el volumen bajo = keep the volume low; al aceptar = by accepting.

sentence: Ayer Ana y yo acordamos vernos el sábado a las cuatro en el parque; las dos anotamos el lugar y la hora para no olvidar nuestro plan.
part_of_speech: first-person plural preterite indicative transitive verb with an infinitive complement
grammar: Acordar plus infinitive states a joint agreement about an action. Ayer establishes the preterite reading of acordamos. Pronominal acordarse de instead means remembering.
note: Vernos = meet each other; anotamos = we wrote down here.

sentence: Le prometí a mi hermana que el lunes le devolvería su libro; hoy es martes y todavía lo tengo: incumplí mi promesa y voy a devolvérselo esta tarde.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite indicative transitive verb
grammar: Incumplir una promesa means failing to honor it. Monday is explicitly the promised return day, and Tuesday's continued possession establishes nonfulfillment.
note: Promesa = promise; prometí = I promised; devolvería = would return, viewed from the promise; se in devolvérselo refers to the sister.

sentence: Ana y yo acordamos no poner música después de las diez; ayer ella respetó ese límite y apagó la bocina a esa hora, aunque tenía visitas.
part_of_speech: third-person singular preterite indicative transitive verb
grammar: Respetar a stated boundary means honoring it through one's actions. The direct object is ese límite, rather than a person receiving respectful treatment.
note: Límite = boundary or limit; bocina = speaker; visitas = guests here.

sentence: Con el apoyo de Ana terminé la mudanza el domingo: ella cargó las cajas más pesadas y me prestó su carro.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Apoyo names practical help here. Carrying boxes and lending a car specify the support Ana actually provided.
note: Cargó = carried; cajas = boxes.

sentence: Mi propuesta de abrir el patio los domingos tiene el respaldo de Ana, que dijo en la reunión de vecinos: «Estoy de acuerdo, siempre que cerremos a las seis».
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Respaldo names Ana's expressed backing for the proposal. Her quoted condition limits that backing to closing at six.
register: Ordinary discussion of a shared neighborhood proposal.
note: Cerremos = we close, present subjunctive after conditional siempre que.

sentence: Ana, gracias por invitarme al cine mañana, pero no puedo ir: tengo el compromiso de acompañar a mi hermana a su curso; ya se lo prometí.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Compromiso names an obligation the speaker has accepted. The explicit promise makes it stronger than an unspecified intention and explains declining Ana's invitation.
register: A reasoned refusal of a familiar person's invitation.
note: Se refers to the sister; lo represents the promised action of accompanying her.

sentence: La convivencia en el departamento que compartimos Ana, Luis y yo mejoró cuando repartimos las tareas: ella lava los platos, él saca la basura y yo limpio el baño.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Convivencia names the experience of sharing everyday space. The improved division of household duties explains the positive change.
note: Departamento = apartment; repartimos las tareas = we divided the chores; ella refers to Ana and él to Luis.

sentence: Ana, quiero seguir siendo tu amiga, pero voy a poner límites a tus visitas: después de las nueve necesito descansar y ya no te voy a recibir.
part_of_speech: infinitive verbal locution
grammar: Poner límites establishes boundaries. The speaker specifies that she will not receive Ana for visits after nine while explicitly preserving the friendship.
register: A direct boundary addressed to a friend.
note: Recibir a alguien = receive or welcome someone as a visitor.

sentence: Yo quería ir al cine y Ana prefería caminar; después de hablar, nos pusimos de acuerdo en pasear hoy y ver una película mañana.
part_of_speech: first-person plural preterite indicative verb within a pronominal verbal locution
grammar: Nos pusimos de acuerdo en introduces reaching a joint arrangement after different preferences, rather than merely already agreeing.
register: Ordinary planning between Ana and the speaker.
note: Pasear = go for a walk; prefería = preferred.

sentence: Mis vecinos Ana y Luis discutían sobre el patio: ella quería cerrarlo a las ocho y él, a las diez; tomé partido por Ana porque el ruido no me deja dormir.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite indicative verbal locution
grammar: Tomar partido por alguien means supporting that person's side. The speaker explicitly supports Ana's earlier closing time.
register: An ordinary neighborhood disagreement.
note: Discutían = were arguing; cerrarlo = close the patio; no me deja dormir = keeps me from sleeping.

sentence: Escogí ir en camión y puedo justificar mi decisión: cuesta menos y pasa cerca de casa, aunque tú prefieres el taxi.
part_of_speech: transitive infinitive verb
grammar: Justificar una decisión means supplying reasons for it. The reasons explain this choice without establishing that everyone should make it.
register: A reasoned explanation to a familiar person.
note: Decisión = decision; cuesta menos = costs less.

sentence: La cena fue en casa de Marta; acabo de releer la invitación, que dice «en casa de Julia, hermana de Marta»: mejor dicho, cenamos en casa de Julia.
part_of_speech: rectificative discourse marker
grammar: Mejor dicho corrects the speaker's preceding inaccurate claim. The invitation supplies new evidence identifying Julia's home.
register: An immediate conversational self-correction.
note: Releer = reread; cenamos = we had dinner here.

sentence: Ayer dije que Luis escondió mi libro; no tengo pruebas y me retracto de esa acusación, aunque todavía no sé dónde está el libro.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative pronominal verb
grammar: Retractarse de una acusación withdraws the accusation. It does not assert that the opposite account has been proved.
register: A direct acknowledgment in an ordinary disagreement.
note: Escondió = hid; pruebas = evidence; acusación = accusation.

sentence: Ana, dije «hoy necesito estar sola» y respondiste «ya no quieres ser mi amiga»; malinterpretaste mi mensaje: sí quiero tu amistad, solo necesito descansar hoy.
part_of_speech: second-person singular preterite indicative transitive verb
grammar: Malinterpretar identifies an incorrect interpretation. Ana's quoted response and the speaker's repair make the mismatch explicit.
register: A repair between female friends using tú.
note: Respondiste = you replied; amistad = friendship; sola = alone, describing the female speaker.

sentence: Di por sentado el consentimiento de Ana y reservé dos lugares sin preguntarle; ella respondió «no quiero ir», así que cancelé su reserva.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Consentimiento names a person's consent. Here it was presumed without asking, and Ana subsequently declines the outing.
register: Careful, somewhat formal wording for consent in an ordinary social arrangement.
note: Di por sentado = I took for granted; reserva = reservation.

sentence: La mochila tiene apenas seis meses, pero las correas muestran desgaste por cargar libros a diario: la tela ya está más delgada.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Desgaste names deterioration from use. Daily carrying and thinning fabric establish wear despite the bag's short age.
register: Ordinary description of wear on an everyday item.
note: Mochila = backpack; correas = straps; tela = fabric; delgada = thin; apenas = only here.

sentence: La camisa es de mi talla, pero necesito un poco de holgura en los hombros: al levantar los brazos, la tela me aprieta.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Holgura names an amount of extra room that allows movement. Un poco de quantifies the needed room rather than labeling the whole garment holgado.
register: An ordinary clothing-fit explanation.
note: Hombros = shoulders; al levantar = when raising; me aprieta = feels tight on me.

sentence: Mi falda me quedaba grande de la cintura; la costurera hizo un ajuste de dos centímetros y ahora la misma falda me queda bien.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Ajuste names a modification to improve fit. La misma falda makes clear that the garment was altered rather than replaced.
register: An ordinary account of a clothing alteration.
note: Cintura = waist; costurera = seamstress; centímetros = centimeters.

sentence: La rueda de mi carrito de compras se rompió; conseguí una refacción para sustituir esa rueda y conservar el resto del carrito.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Refacción names a replacement component. The broken wheel is the component being replaced, while the rest of the trolley is retained.
register: Mexican-compatible everyday replacement-part vocabulary.
note: Rueda = wheel; carrito de compras = shopping trolley; el resto = the remainder.

sentence: Esta tapa es compatible con mi frasco porque tiene la medida correcta y cierra bien; la otra es demasiado grande.
part_of_speech: singular descriptive adjective
grammar: Compatible con describes items that work together. Correct size and successful closure supply the relevant fit requirement.
register: An ordinary household comparison.
note: Tapa = lid; frasco = jar; medida = size or measurement here.

sentence: En un cuento, una vendedora le dice a Ana: «Puedes probar esta silla sin compromiso; si no te gusta, te vas sin comprar nada».
part_of_speech: adverbial prepositional locution
grammar: Sin compromiso removes a purchase obligation from the offered trial. It does not describe warranty coverage.
register: A fictional seller's friendly tú offer.
note: Cuento = story; vendedora = saleswoman; probar la silla = try the chair before buying.

sentence: Hoy es 12 de mayo en nuestro cuento; mi pase del club dice «válido del 1 al 31 de mayo» y sigue vigente, así que puedo entrar hoy.
part_of_speech: singular descriptive adjective
grammar: Vigente describes validity at the stated reference time. May 12 falls within the pass's explicitly limited May validity period.
register: An explanation within a fictional club setting.
note: Pase = admission pass; válido = valid; sigue = remains here.

sentence: En el club de un cuento, hoy es 2 de junio; mi pase dice «válido hasta el 31 de mayo», así que ya está caducado y no puedo entrar con él.
part_of_speech: masculine singular participial adjective
grammar: Caducado describes validity that has ended. June 2 is later than the stated May 31 endpoint.
register: An explanation about a fictional admission pass.
note: Con él refers to using the admission pass.

sentence: Luis cargó cajas toda la mañana y ahora está agotado; necesita sentarse a descansar antes de continuar con la mudanza.
part_of_speech: masculine singular participial adjective
grammar: Agotado describes Luis's exhaustion after effort. The identified human experiencer excludes an out-of-stock reading.
register: An ordinary account of tiredness during a move.
note: Continuar con la mudanza = continue with the move.

sentence: —Ana, ¿estás disponible mañana de cuatro a cinco para ordenar libros conmigo? —A esa hora no tengo otros planes, pero todavía no decido si voy a participar.
part_of_speech: first-person singular present indicative verb followed by an indirect-question conjunction
grammar: Decidir si introduces choosing whether to do something. Todavía no leaves Ana's participation undecided despite her available time.
register: A familiar invitation using tú.
note: Estar disponible para una tarea = be available for a task; participar = take part.

sentence: Ya acordamos el lugar y el día del paseo, pero quedan cabos sueltos: falta decidir quién lleva el agua y a qué hora salimos.
part_of_speech: masculine plural fixed noun phrase
grammar: Cabos sueltos names unresolved details within a mostly settled arrangement. Quedan agrees with the plural phrase.
register: Ordinary shared planning.
note: Quedan = remain; the missing details concern water and departure time.

sentence: Acordamos devolver las sillas el lunes; esa entrega es inaplazable porque sus dueños las necesitan para una fiesta ese mismo día.
part_of_speech: singular descriptive adjective
grammar: Inaplazable rules out postponement. The owners' same-day need explains why the agreed return date cannot move.
register: An explanation of an ordinary shared obligation.
note: Dueños = owners; esa entrega refers to returning the chairs.

sentence: Cuidé los libros del club de cuatro a cinco; a esa hora llegó Ana, mi relevo, y se quedó a cargo hasta las seis.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Relevo names the person taking over a responsibility. The masculine noun can identify Ana, a woman.
register: An ordinary account of alternating club duties.
note: Cuidé = looked after; a cargo = in charge; a esa hora refers to five.

sentence: En la comida familiar, Ana cuenta que perdió su empleo y Luis dice «ahora tendrás vacaciones»; ese comentario está de más y ella responde «no es momento de bromas».
part_of_speech: adverbial locution completing estar de más
grammar: Estar de más evaluates the comment as socially unnecessary or unwelcome. Ana's response makes the inappropriate joking explicit.
register: A critical evaluation of a comment during a family meal.
note: Comentario = comment; bromas = jokes; ella refers to Ana.

sentence: No pensaba comprar pan, pero vi las conchas de la tienda y ahora tengo antojo de una; voy a comerla con café.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Tener antojo de names a spontaneous desire for something. Seeing the bread changes the speaker's earlier intention.
register: Ordinary Mexican food conversation.
note: Conchas = shell-patterned Mexican sweet breads; una and la refer to one concha.

sentence: La sobremesa fue amena: Ana contó historias de su infancia, yo compartí las mías y las dos seguimos conversando porque queríamos escuchar más.
part_of_speech: feminine singular descriptive adjective
grammar: Amena evaluates the conversation as enjoyable and engaging. Reciprocal stories and continued interest make the evaluation interpretable.
register: An ordinary positive evaluation of an after-meal conversation.
note: Las mías = my stories; las dos identifies Ana and the female speaker.

sentence: Mis amigos y yo tenemos una tertulia de cine en casa de Inés una vez al mes: cada quien comenta una película y conversamos sin un programa fijo.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Tertulia names a gathering centered on informal conversation. Shared film comments and the absence of a fixed agenda establish its character.
register: An informal cultural gathering among friends.
note: Cada quien = each person; programa fijo = fixed agenda here.

sentence: Mañana tenemos un ensayo de la obra de teatro: repetiremos las escenas sin público para preparar la presentación del domingo.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Ensayo names preparation through practice before a performance. Repeating scenes without an audience establishes the theatrical sense.
register: Ordinary planning among performers.
note: Obra de teatro = play; escenas = scenes; público = audience; presentación = performance here.

sentence: La función de teatro empieza el sábado a las seis; quiero llegar antes para sentarme y ver la obra desde el principio.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Función names a scheduled theatrical performance. The starting time and the intention to watch the play establish this sense.
register: Ordinary planning by a theatergoer.
note: Desde el principio = from the beginning.

sentence: Compré una entrada para el concierto del viernes; la guardé en mi cartera porque tengo que mostrarla para pasar.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Entrada names a ticket here. Buying, storing and showing it distinguish the object from a physical entrance.
register: Ordinary event attendance.
note: Cartera = wallet; mostrarla = show the ticket.

sentence: Compré un abono para los cuatro conciertos de junio; con ese mismo pase puedo entrar a los cuatro, sin comprar un boleto para cada uno.
part_of_speech: masculine singular noun
grammar: Abono names one pass covering a defined series. The same pass admits its holder to all four specified concerts.
register: Ordinary cultural-event planning.
note: Cada uno refers to each of the four concerts.

sentence: En mi cuento, la biblioteca publicó una convocatoria para un concurso de dibujo: cualquier vecino puede participar si entrega su dibujo antes del 10 de junio.
part_of_speech: feminine singular noun
grammar: Convocatoria names a public invitation to participate. The activity, eligible participants and submission deadline are explicit.
register: A fictional community announcement.
note: Biblioteca = library; concurso de dibujo = drawing contest; cualquier vecino = any neighbor.

sentence: Me acerqué a Ana para asistirla con sus bolsas; ella cargó una y yo llevé las otras dos hasta su puerta.
part_of_speech: transitive infinitive verb with attached feminine singular direct-object clitic
grammar: Asistir means helping a person here. Attached la represents Ana as direct object; it does not introduce an event being attended.
register: Asistir in this helping sense has a more formal tone than everyday ayudar.
note: Me acerqué = I went up to her; las otras dos refers to Ana's other two bags.

sentence: Presencié la discusión de Ana y Luis: estaba con ellos en el patio y vi cómo empezó, así que puedo contar lo que pasó.
part_of_speech: first-person singular preterite indicative transitive verb
grammar: Presenciar means witnessing an event while present. The speaker's location and direct observation establish firsthand experience.
register: An ordinary firsthand account.
note: Discusión = argument; vi cómo empezó = I saw how it began.

sentence: Me gusta caminar con mis vecinos; decidí apuntarme al paseo del sábado y anoté mi nombre en la lista del grupo.
part_of_speech: pronominal infinitive verb with attached first-person singular clitic
grammar: Apuntarse a an activity means signing up for it. Al contracts the governed a with the article el.
register: Ordinary voluntary participation in a neighborhood activity.
note: Decidí = I decided; anoté = I wrote down; lista = list.

sentence: Hablamos de organizar una comida en el parque, pero el plan se quedó en una propuesta: nadie aceptó una tarea y no fijamos una fecha.
